headline: Eagles in the Arena: After state title loss, Bakersfield Christian HS looks to right the wrongs of the past
content:
The Daily Brief

Eagles in the Arena: After state title loss, Bakersfield Christian HS looks to right the wrongs of the past

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 14, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a look at the night that was — from a high-speed DUI south of the Grapevine to a welfare check for a woman seen crying for help in a red pickup. Today’s high will reach 95°, with an overnight low around 67°, and air quality is moderate at AQI 59. Let’s get you caught up.

The Kern Overnight

The night opened quietly enough, with a traffic unit requested around 9:10 p.m. for the 600 block of 33rd Street. But by 9:23 p.m., dispatchers were sending city units to White Lane for a road-rage disturbance involving a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both repeatedly stopping and blocking the eastbound roadway. The incident drew no further update on the air. Around 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street; officers took the report, and no arrests were announced. The night’s most serious call came around 11:34 p.m., when Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male hanging out the driver’s window, a female crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound, and the broadcast went out citywide. Fire crews were comparatively quiet, handling a residential alarm on Greenview Lane around 11 p.m. that amounted to nothing and a vehicle accident that drew an engine, battalion, and rescue unit before the air went quiet. Just after midnight, a theft from a space at a mobile home park on Barlow Road was reported, with a loss estimated near $3,900 and a suspect named. And shortly before 3 a.m., a traffic collision in the Flying J truck stop parking lot at Frazier Park saw a burgundy Freightliner hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement. CHP was investigating the hit-and-run claim as the feed moved on.

Today's weather

Today’s high will reach 95° under sunny skies, with a low tonight around 67°. It’s currently 77° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and no active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at AQI 59.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield Christian High School’s football team is looking to right the wrongs of last year’s state title loss as they gear up for the new season. The Eagles are working to build on their experience and come back stronger, with a focus on teamwork and determination.

23ABC tells us that Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works.

23ABC also shares that Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, traveled to San Diego on August 12 to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development.

KGET 17 reports that Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that would place Kern and dozens of other counties in a new state, separate from coastal California. Kern County District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores said the effort is about making sure the region’s industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. An analysis presented to the board found the proposed inland state would account for only about 15 percent of California’s current real GDP. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart said that number tells a stark story about what separation would actually mean for the region.

Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will receive a portion of the $109 million federal aviation funding. This funding will support improvements and upgrades to local airport infrastructure.

Coming up this week

This afternoon, the Special Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at 1 p.m., followed by the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee at noon and the Special Laws and Legislation Committee at noon. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon, the Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4 p.m., and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets at 2 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board meets at 10 a.m. On Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. And this weekend, the Fox Theater will host PEPPER With CYDEWAYS on August 14, Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22, Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29.

headline: STEM in Kern: Understanding recent major earthquakes
content:
The Daily Brief

STEM in Kern: Understanding recent major earthquakes

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 15, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a reminder of the Eagles’ resolve. Today’s top story follows Bakersfield Christian High School’s football team as they regroup after a state title loss. We’re looking at a high of 95° and a low of 69°, with clear skies and good air quality. Let’s see what happened overnight and what the day holds.

The Kern Overnight

A night that opened with a road-rage pair stalling traffic on White Lane and closed with a stolen van on Kentucky Street and a fender dispute between big rigs at the Flying J. Law enforcement carried most of the load: a 90-plus mph DUI south of the Grapevine, a reported theft from a mobile home park on Barlow Road, and the night's most serious call — an attempt-to-locate after a woman was seen crying for help out the window of a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace. Fire crews were comparatively quiet: a residential alarm that amounted to nothing and a vehicle accident that drew an engine, battalion and rescue unit before the air went quiet.

Around 11:34 p.m., Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male hanging out the driver's window, a female crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound. It's the kind of call dispatchers don't sit on: no description of plates or direction of travel beyond southbound, so the broadcast went out citywide for any unit to catch the truck. No further update was heard on the air before the feed moved on.

headline: 3 dead after wrong-way crash on Highway 99 near Bakersfield, CHP says
content:
The Daily Brief

3 dead after wrong-way crash on Highway 99 near Bakersfield, CHP says

Good morning Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 16th, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm start to the day with temperatures already in the low 80s. Today’s top story is a tragic wrong-way crash on Highway 99 that claimed three lives overnight. We’ve also got a moderate air quality day ahead, with no active weather alerts for Kern County.

The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious incident unfolded just before 1 a.m. on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a vehicle fire and extrication drew a heavy response. Crews worked to free a pinned, unconscious subject from a vehicle, ultimately pulling two patients out as green tags. Around the same time, a DUI driver fled eastbound from the 33rd Street area in a white BMW 5 Series. Earlier in the evening, a palm tree fire climbed into the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way off Villalobos Street, drawing a reinforced alarm with Engine 7 as incident commander. Units also staged on Price Street around 9:48 p.m. for a possible shooting that never developed on the air, and handled a long string of domestics and disturbances — including one at a Camellia Village apartment where a wall was punched. Shortly before 5:40 a.m., one vehicle struck a parked car at Myrtle Avenue, drawing multiple engine companies and Battalion 4 for a patient assessment.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 98° and a low around 72° tonight. It’s currently 82° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is holding at a moderate AQI of 58.

Top stories

23ABC reports that three people are dead after a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99 early Sunday morning. According to California Highway Patrol Bakersfield, a white Honda Accord was traveling northbound in the southbound lanes on Highway 99, north of 7th Standard Road, when it collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado at around 12:44 a.m. The crash caused the Honda to catch fire. CHP says all 3 occupants inside the vehicle died from their injuries. The driver and one other occupant of the BMW sustained major injuries, while the 2 occupants in the Chevrolet sustained minor injuries. Officials say it is unknown whether alcohol or drugs were a factor in the crash.

KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with significant injuries and even fatalities reported. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works to deter illegal fireworks use.

23ABC shares that Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, helped shape a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development. Baldovinos said one of the most debated topics during the two-day Washington meeting was how long recovery should last, pushing back on the view that recovery should only be for a treatment program of 28 days.

Something good

Kern County is making a mark on the national stage this week. Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, traveled to San Diego to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. This initiative highlights local expertise contributing to broader solutions for addiction challenges.

The Daily Brief

Fight to save the Crystal Palace in Bakersfield

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 17, 2026 — a day that starts with a high of 99° and air quality at a moderate 55. The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came around 11 p.m., when a group of five juveniles — one of whom pointed a firearm at the reporting party — was reported on Monterey Street. All were described as wearing dark clothing, and though no shots were fired, units were responding as the feed moved on. Earlier, shortly before 9:40 p.m., a possible shots-fired incident had units checking local hospitals for gunshot victims and looking for a suspect vehicle, though the exact location was unclear on the air. Fire crews also handled a one-acre grass fire near the bike path off Oak Street just after 10:30 p.m., with a slow rate of spread. In other incidents, multiple units responded to a domestic violence call in progress on Animas Court at 9:54 p.m., and an ex-boyfriend reportedly smashed a vehicle windshield with a shotgun in the FoodMaxx parking lot on Ming Avenue around 11:03 p.m. The small hours ran quieter, with the usual spread of disturbances, medical aids, and welfare checks.

According to 23ABC, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recently toured a Bakersfield program that he believes could reshape how schools teach children about food and nutrition. Kennedy visited Edible Schoolyard Kern County, a program that brings gardening and cooking into the school curriculum. Students grow their own food in school gardens and then use that fresh produce in kitchen lessons. The goal is to connect classroom learning with what ends up on their plates, and Kennedy said the program’s focus on fresh food — including school cafeterias buying fresh produce — could be a model for schools nationwide.

KGET 17 also shared that a Bakersfield police sergeant has been appointed as the next Kern County District Attorney’s chief of investigations. The move highlights the close working relationship between local law enforcement and the DA’s office, and it’s expected to bring a wealth of experience to the role.

In other news from KGET 17, the Kern County Sheriff’s Office arrested four individuals on various gun and drug possession charges after a copper wire theft. The incident underscores the ongoing challenges with property crime in the county and the collaborative efforts by law enforcement to address it.

23ABC reported on Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs sharing their Fourth of July findings at a recent meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Bakersfield Fire Chief Kevin Albertson noted that the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with a total of 106 citations issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined. Despite a 6% decrease in fire-related responses compared to 2025, officials say more work remains to deter illegal fireworks use.

Something good

On a brighter note, Carlos Baldovinos — executive director of the Mission at Kern County — recently helped shape a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., to develop the toolkit with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the Department of Health and Human Services. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction, covering topics like program length, transitional housing, and long-term mentorship. It’s a proud moment for Kern County to be at the forefront of such important work.

Crews worked to access the burn, with a reporting party pointing out lights on the hill during the response.

Around 3:45 a.m., a 53-foot trailer north of Pond on Garzoli Road was fully involved, with a spot of grass fire spreading alongside it. Battalion crews responded to what dispatch dubbed the Garzoli Incident and remained on scene for hotspots.

Just before 10:45 p.m., a caller reported roughly 30 shots fired, mostly in a field in the area of Panama Lane and South Allen Road. The call stood for service while units investigated.

Around 3:06 a.m., a welfare check near the Wells Fargo on Columbus Street escalated when a man on a bicycle was approached by subjects and an impact sound was heard, followed by a fight involving three people. Two suspects fled northbound Columbus; units searched.

Bakersfield residents react to fears church expansion funds may be lost in Diocese of Fresno bankruptcy

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Wednesday, August 19, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 102° and air quality at a moderate 62. Overnight, a grass fire east of the city drew a heavy response from county crews. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the weather, and the week ahead.

The Kern Overnight

The night’s biggest incident was a grass fire that broke out just after 1 a.m. about 2 miles east of the county dump and north of the railroad tracks. First reports put it at 3–5 acres, but it grew to 5–10 acres as units arrived. Crews dispatched to what they called the Apollo Incident included Engine 345, Water Tender 12, dozers, a safety officer, and helicopter 409. They worked access through corral roads, and Union Pacific train traffic was held while they mopped up.

Around 2:22 a.m., a fire in an alley near 9th & K streets spread into a garage and drew the Station 1 assignment: Engine 1, Truck 1, Rescue 1, Battalion 1, and Engine 6. Just before 2:20 a.m., a burglary in progress sent units searching for a suspect described as a white male, 5-foot-11, about 150 pounds, in a white tank top and black gym shorts. He was last seen riding a blue beach cruiser and exiting onto Union Avenue. Around 12:24 a.m., units responded to 21st & O streets for a person in crisis, reportedly nude with a shirt draped over them and possibly in the middle of a psychiatric episode.

The log also noted a few other incidents: at 22:01, unknown subjects in a blue Honda dropped items off at a vacant residence on Madera Street in Maricopa, then left southbound. At 22:07, a report came in of a 6-year-old possibly locked out of a residence in the 700 block of Jefferson Street. At 23:00, a disturbance was reported at a business in the 2700 block of White Lane. At 23:46, a vehicle was reported not stopping on Highway 99 toward the 223, with a possible pursuit in progress. And at 2:34 a.m., a woman reported a man banging on her door as she screamed at him to leave; banging was audible in the background, and a heavy-duty response was requested.

Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 102° and a low around 74° tonight. It’s currently 73° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County at this time, and air quality is holding at a moderate 62.

Top stories

23ABC reports that college costs continue to surge, with the average family spending more than $34,000 on college this past school year—a sharp 10% jump from the year before. Financial expert Jennifer Finetti, director of student advocacy at ScholarshipOwl, says a combination of factors is driving tuition higher, including changes in federal research funding and a decline in international students. "Plus, of course, inflation. Just like it makes costs for all of us go up, it also makes the cost go up for colleges as well. All the suppliers and things they need to keep running," Finetti said. Finetti says one of the biggest mistakes parents make is waiting too long to have honest conversations about what their family can realistically afford—and what students may need to contribute. "That's something I think parents can talk to their kids about, and to say 'Hey, integrate applying for scholarships into your life. If you want to go to college, you need to do your part,'" Finetti said. Finetti also says families shouldn't rule out community college, even for students who have good grades and could go straight to a four-year university. "They can get two years done at a very low cost, living at home, and then they can transfer to complete their bachelor's degree," Finetti said. For families considering student loans, there are major new rules to watch. Finetti says changes that took effect July 1 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act give new borrowers fewer federal repayment options. One plan can tie monthly payments to a borrower's income, meaning payments could climb.

According to 23ABC, a fake government form is circulating in AI-generated videos online, falsely promising seniors they can freeze their property taxes or stop paying school-bond charges, and Kern County officials say it is already generating calls and walk-ins at the assessor-recorder's office. The videos promote a form called "1098-SR," claiming people over 65 can use it to eliminate certain tax obligations. Kern County Assessor-Recorder Laura Avila says the form does not exist. "In the last couple weeks, we've been receiving phone calls and customers—or taxpayers, property owners—coming into our counter and asking to fill out this form 1098-SR," Avila said. Avila says her office searched for the form and could not find any federal program tied to it. While some other states offer similar property tax programs, California does not. When her staff explains the form is not real, residents are often upset because they heard about it from friends or saw it in videos online and often believe they are being denied. Avila says some of the videos appear on YouTube and are labeled as AI-generated at the bottom. The videos are broad, she says, targeting multiple states without specifying which programs apply where, and they feature what appear to be real people explaining programs that do not exist in California. Avila says her office has not confirmed anyone losing money or being asked to pay, which is why she is calling this a preventive advisory. But she is concerned about what could come next. "My fear is that the next phase of this will be somebody soliciting seniors."

KGET 17 tells us that early heat waves are shrinking Kern County pistachio harvests, raising prices for consumers. Hot summers are nothing new to Kern County, but early extreme heat waves this year are taking a serious toll on pistachio crops, shrinking harvests across the region. Fewer blooms on trees can mean a sharper drop in fruit production, leaving growers with fewer pistachios to harvest. LaBorde's business manager Jonathan Romero says pistachio trees naturally follow a cycle of higher-yield years followed by lower-yield years. Growers are currently facing one of those lower-production seasons, with extreme heat adding even more pressure. "Not only are we faced with a low crop yield this year, but we're also being affected by inflation." Romero says higher market prices help even out the disparity for farmers when numbers rise on shelves. He says he is worried about how this is affecting smaller-scale pistachio farmers who rely solely on a handful of nut varieties. "Pistachios might be a bit more expensive this year, but you're helping the growers—the local growers, family farms; I think that's what they should all take into consideration," Romero said. Dr. Richard Gearhart, a professor of economics at California State University, says that when a product becomes rare, local and overseas shoppers must compete to buy it, which drives up the price for everyone domestically and internationally. According to the United States Department of Agriculture, the estimated projected yield for California's total pistachio harvest sits at around 600 to 900 million pounds this year, compared to last year's harvest of 1.63 billion pounds.

Something good

Senators Schiff and Padilla announced $43 million in funding for Kern County's Amtrak Gold Runner Route. This investment will enhance local transportation infrastructure and services.

Coming up this week

This week brings several public meetings and events worth noting. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board meets at 10:00 a.m. On Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission convenes at 5:30 p.m. And on Wednesday, August 26, there are two city council meetings: one at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full lineup. On Saturday, August 22, catch Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los Caminantes, y Grupo Yndio. Around 9:19 p.m., a burglary at a furniture business on Baker Street had suspects possibly still inside, with a silver Prius spotted in an alleyway nearby. Officers set a perimeter at Baker and Kentucky with a second boundary at Baker and Jackson. Just before midnight, a person in crisis on Di Giorgio Road reportedly made threats against family members and was possibly in possession of a knife, with a child present in the residence. content:
The Daily Brief

Large police presence at Independence High School after reports of shots fired

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 21, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 101° and air quality at 108 — unhealthy for sensitive groups. Overnight, a semi truck fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine became the night’s longest-running incident, with crews still working the Tejon fire after 6 a.m. and traffic backing up to the Lebec service route. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the news, and the week ahead.

The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident was a semi truck and trailer fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine. Just before 1 a.m., CHP and Engine 56 were on scene with command established as the Tejon Incident. The fire burned for hours: by 6 a.m. crews were still working it, a heavy-duty tow had been called in, and traffic was backing up to the Lebec service route. Earlier in the evening, around 10:34 p.m., a quarter-acre brush fire on McCombs Road (State Route 43 north of Wasco) was burning with a fast rate of spread and potential to run west. Multiple engines and a water tender responded, additional wildland equipment was ordered, and crews split into Division Bravo and Division Yankee for what command described as a lengthy mop-up. In north Bakersfield, just after 3 a.m., two subjects were on a Woodford Boulevard property behind a white pickup, possibly taking items. The subjects were known to be in possession of firearms, though none were visible at first; officers later made contact and located a firearm. Around 9:50 p.m., a robbery at gunpoint was reported on Denise Avenue in north Bakersfield. The suspect was described as a transient white male in his late 30s, wearing a baseball cap and black face mask, pulling a wagon, and accompanied by a white female. Finally, around 4:36 a.m., three subjects at a trucking yard south of Gibson Street were reported possibly taking items. Deputies set a perimeter and the subjects ran — one headed south toward a fence with an officer holding the hole. One subject was described as known to carry a knife.

headline: McFarland police investigate fatal shooting at Capri Laundromat on Perkins Avenue
content:
The Daily Brief

McFarland police investigate fatal shooting at Capri Laundromat on Perkins Avenue

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm one — expect a high near 103° today, with a low around 75° tonight. Overnight, the big story was a shooting reported at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area just after midnight. We’ll have more on that and other overnight incidents below. First, let’s look at what happened while you slept.

The Kern Overnight

A shooting outside a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area was the most serious call of the night. Just after midnight, a witness reported seeing someone shot, with the suspect last seen in a white vehicle. Before that, crews knocked down a fire at a vacant house on King Street around 2:16 a.m. — flames were visible inside the single-story structure, and heavy smoke was showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Earlier in the evening, just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded to what was dubbed the Harris Incident, though injuries are unknown. And around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported — no injuries were noted, and the suspect fled on foot northbound. Elsewhere, multiple reports of a grass fire along southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road drew a heavy response, though crews found only a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 91° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is not currently available, and there are no active fires to report.

Top stories

23ABC reports that McFarland police are investigating a homicide after a 26-year-old man was shot and killed Saturday afternoon at the Capri Laundromat in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue. Officers responded to the scene at approximately 3:18 p.m. and found the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds inside the laundromat. Preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects arrived at the Capri Liquors in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue and confronted the victim inside the Capri Laundromat, which is adjacent to the gas pumps. An argument led to one of the suspects producing a firearm and shooting the victim multiple times. The two suspects then fled the area in an unknown vehicle. No suspects have been identified, no arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown. The victim’s identity will be released after next of kin have been notified. McFarland Police Department detectives are actively working the scene and gathering investigative information. Police say there is no current threat to the community, but the public is advised to avoid the area until the scene is processed. Anyone with information about this investigation is asked to call Detective Galvan or Detective Cazares at 661-792-2121.

KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School. The mayor’s statement comes after a 15-year-old suspect was arrested in connection with the incident. Mayor Goh emphasized that the safety of our community is her top priority and that she is closely monitoring the situation. She urged anyone with information to come forward and cooperate with law enforcement. The mayor’s office is working with local authorities to ensure a thorough investigation and to support the affected families and community members.

Bakersfield Now reports that Southwest Market has canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School after the fatal shooting. The decision was made out of respect for the community and to allow for ongoing investigations. Southwest Market organizers expressed their condolences to the families affected by the tragedy and said they plan to reschedule the event for a later date.

Something good

A family is organizing a flea market to help raise funds for a prosthetic leg for Villafana. The event aims to collect $8,900 to support this cause. It’s a heartening reminder of how our community comes together to help one another in times of need.

Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there’s plenty happening in Bakersfield this week. On Tuesday, August 26, the Bakersfield City Council will hold a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater has a busy schedule: Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio will perform tonight, August 22. On Tuesday, August 26, you can catch the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. content:
The Daily Brief

Cal State Bakersfield launches first mariachi ensemble

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Sunday, August 23, 2026, and we're starting the day with a high of 103°, air quality at a moderate 64, and no active weather alerts. Overnight, the big story was a grass fire that grew to three or four acres south of Highway 46 near Wildwood Road, drawing a battalion-level wildland response. We'll have more on that and the night's other incidents below, along with the details on a pair of deadly shootings that have shaken our community. Grab a cup of coffee and read on.

The Kern Overnight

The night's most significant call came around 4:30 a.m. when a grass fire broke out in a field near a small trailer community just east of Wildwood Road, reachable off Highway 46. Crews reported three to four acres burning with roads on three sides of the fire; Battalion 3 was on scene and asked for additional wildland units as Engine 931 worked its way in from the south. Before that, just after 3:30 a.m., a vehicle rolled over in the median on a northbound highway just south of Twisselman Road, with reports of power lines down across the lane. Units were en route to that incident as well. Earlier in the night, around 1:55 a.m., an outside fire was reported on the 100 block of Sumner Street near the railroad tracks, and engine companies were dispatched. About 2:10 a.m., someone was reported coming into a campground wearing a gray t-shirt, gray pants and no shoes; units were checking the area. Hot, dry late-August conditions kept fire crews on the move overnight: the three-to-four-acre grass fire south of Highway 46 near Wildwood Road drew a battalion-level wildland response, and an outside fire was reported on Sumner Street near the railroad tracks. The Twisselman Road rollover with downed power lines prompted a quick highway response, and overnight temperatures stayed warm across the valley.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 103° and a low around 74° tonight. It's currently 73° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 64 — moderate.

Top stories

Bakersfield Now reports that Southwest Market has canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School after a fatal shooting. The cancellation comes after a deadly shooting occurred near the school's football game, prompting concerns for public safety. Organizers of the market event have decided to postpone the gathering in light of the incident.

According to 23ABC, a 26-year-old man was shot and killed at the Capri Laundromat on Perkins Avenue in McFarland. Officers responded to the scene at approximately 3:18 p.m. and found the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds inside the laundromat. Officers immediately provided medical aid and initiated CPR, but the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. Preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects arrived at the Capri Liquors in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue and confronted the victim inside the Capri Laundromat, which is adjacent to the gas pumps. An argument led to one of the suspects producing a firearm and shooting the victim multiple times. The two suspects then fled the area in an unknown vehicle. No suspects have been identified, no arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown. The victim's identity will be released after next of kin have been notified. McFarland Police Department detectives are actively working the scene and gathering investigative information. Police say there is no current threat to the community, but the public is advised to avoid the area until the scene is processed.

KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School. In her statement, Mayor Goh addressed the incident and its impact on the community, emphasizing the importance of safety at public events and the need for continued vigilance.

Something good

A family is hosting a Saturday flea market to raise $8,900 for Villafana's prosthetic leg. This community effort aims to support a local resident in need.

Finally, on Saturday, September 4, the Fox Theater will host MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA. Be sure to check the Fox Theater's website for ticket information and showtimes.

Search and Rescue search for a body at Lake Ming

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Tuesday, August 25, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 102° and air quality at a moderate 54. Overnight, officers responded to a possible attempted abduction near Union Avenue and Columbus Street, and today we’re following the community’s response to the tragic shooting at Independence High School. Let’s get you caught up.

The Kern Overnight

Overnight activity kept officers busy across Bakersfield, with a notable incident unfolding shortly before 11 p.m. near Union Avenue and Columbus Street. A caller reported two men in an older tan Toyota Camry attempting to get an 18-year-old woman into their vehicle. Officers searched the area as the vehicle was last seen heading northbound on Union Avenue. Into the early hours of Tuesday, police also responded to a disturbance on the 2800 block of C Street, where a subject was reported in possession of a butcher knife while the reporting party stayed barricaded in a bathroom. Elsewhere, officers pursued a minibike at low speed through east Bakersfield, with the chase moving westbound on Oregon Street, northbound on Gage Avenue, and across Niles Street at speeds between roughly 15 and 37 mph. Around 3:15 a.m., a unit began tracking a 2017 Nissan that refused to stop in east Bakersfield. And around 12:30 a.m., a woman reported her ex-boyfriend threw a brick through her vehicle and patio door on Coventry Drive, with officers investigating the incident.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 102° today with a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 75° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is holding at a moderate 54. Conditions should remain calm and clear as we move through the day.

Top stories

23ABC reports that the Bakersfield community gathered Monday night at the Dignity Health Sports Complex for an evening of prayer and music to remember 17-year-old Levi Brown, who was killed outside an Independence High School football game Friday night. Bakersfield police say the shooting was gang-related, and a 15-year-old suspect was arrested Saturday. On Monday, police announced six more arrests, including three teens, as officers worked to prevent potential retaliatory gang violence. Police say those arrests are not directly connected to Brown’s homicide. Bakersfield Chief of Police Brent Stratton spoke Monday morning about the shooting’s ties to gang activity, noting that the age range of those involved in such incidents is unfortunately common. Manuel Carrizalez, founder and director of Stay Focused Ministries, knew Brown through his organization, which mentors teens and other students through school visits and office meetings. Carrizalez said Brown had a lot of goals and was looking towards his future.

KGET 17 tells us that the California State Parks Foundation is now accepting submissions for its 2026 Photo Contest. Take a picture at one of California’s 280 state parks and submit it online at CalParks.org. You can enter up to three photos in each of the following five categories: Scenic Landscapes, Wildlife & Nature, Recreation & Activities, People in Parks, and California History. Winners will receive a free membership to the California State Parks Foundation and will be featured in the Foundation’s 2028 calendar. It’s free to enter, and submissions will be accepted through September 21.

The Bridal Quince Expo in Bakersfield is set for September, offering a celebration of local culture and traditions. This event provides an opportunity for the community to come together and enjoy a festive occasion.

On Friday, August 28, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE takes the stage, and on Saturday, August 29, Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will perform. The Kern Overnight

Overnight activity was relatively light across Kern County, though a few notable incidents kept law enforcement busy. Around 9:18 p.m., officers responded to repeated intruder reports on the 2400 block of South M Street. A resident barricaded himself in his bathroom with his dog after an unknown subject was reported attempting to enter his apartment for a fourth time. The situation kept officers on scene into the evening. Elsewhere, at 22:17, a juvenile fled in a vehicle in Bakersfield, prompting a brief search. A family member followed but had not yet provided a direction of travel or a description of the vehicle. Later, at 05:09, police staged for a subject experiencing a mental-health crisis on the 2800 block of University Avenue. Overall, the night was calm with no major incidents reported elsewhere in the county.

Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 102° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 99° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 87. Be sure to stay hydrated and take precautions if you’ll be outdoors for extended periods.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that two individuals have been charged following a shooting at Independence High School. The incident has raised concerns about safety on campus, and school officials are working closely with law enforcement to ensure that measures are in place to protect students and staff. The charges come as the community grapples with the aftermath of the shooting, and discussions about security enhancements are expected in the coming weeks.

Bakersfield Now tells us that the driver accused in a deadly wrong-way crash on Highway 99 worked at North Kern State Prison. The crash, which resulted in fatalities, has sparked questions about road safety and the potential for impaired driving. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the incident, and any findings will be crucial in understanding how to prevent similar tragedies in the future.

According to 23ABC, the California City Council denied two appeals challenging the approval of the CoreCivic ICE detention facility. The appeals argued that immigration detention is not the same as a prison or correctional facility and is not a permitted use under the city's zoning code. Despite these challenges, the council voted 4-1 to deny both appeals, allowing the facility to continue operating under its existing approvals. The decision has sparked debate about the role of such facilities in the community and the interpretation of local zoning laws.

KGET 17 also shared that the trial for a Bakersfield crash that killed a married couple is expected to begin by October. The case has been closely watched by the community, and the upcoming trial will be an important step in seeking justice for the victims. Details of the crash and the circumstances surrounding it will likely come to light as the trial progresses, and the outcome may have implications for traffic safety measures in the area.

Something good

In a delightful community event, a local Bakersfield bakery is honoring Dolly Parton with special sweet treats. The bakery is celebrating the iconic singer’s contributions to child literacy through a variety of desserts that pay homage to her work. It’s a heartwarming gesture that brings a smile to our faces and reminds us of the power of community spirit.

Coming up this week

headline: Rep. Vince Fong on the golden mussel in Kern County and protecting water infrastructure
content:
The Daily Brief

Rep. Vince Fong on the golden mussel in Kern County and protecting water infrastructure

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Thursday, August 27, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a high of 94° and a low of 74° tonight. Air quality is moderate at AQI 64, and the Kern County High School District is tightening safety measures following last week’s deadly shooting at Independence High School. Overnight, responders handled a possible overdose on White Lane and a couple of medical-welfare calls. Let’s get you caught up.

The Kern Overnight

Overnight activity across Kern County was light, with no major incidents reported anywhere in the county. Responders handled a possible overdose, two medical-welfare calls, and a downed tree branch over the course of the night. Around 4:35 a.m., medical responders were called to a motel on White Lane for a possible overdose and administered Narcan after the caller was transferred to medical aid. Just after midnight, a medical aid call came in from Stine Road. Several people got on the phone asking for an ambulance, but no one could explain what the situation was. Shortly before 12:05 a.m., units were sent to check on an elderly woman with dementia who could not be reached at her home on Mountain Oak Road. At 9:40 p.m., a tree branch came down onto a telephone wire and a vehicle in an unincorporated part of the county, reported as a hazard condition.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 94° and a low around 74° tonight. It's currently 77° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 64 — moderate.

Top stories

According to 23ABC, Kern County water agencies are taking early action against golden mussel threat to water supply. Golden mussels remain a growing threat to California's water supply, but water agencies in Kern County are taking early action to stay ahead of the invasive species before it can disrupt water delivery. On Tuesday, a round table was held in Bakersfield, bringing together Representative Vince Fong, local water agencies and other stakeholders to discuss ways to fight back against golden mussels. Andrea Sealock with SePRO Water attended the event and said interagency cooperation was a central theme. Sealock pointed to Arvin Edison Water Storage District as an example of a district acting responsibly after it detected golden mussels in its system in December 2025. SePRO worked with Arvin Edison on a treatment program using an EPA-approved, copper-based treatment while monitoring the system. Sealock said the work is showing promising results. SePRO is also currently working with multiple water districts throughout Kern County.

Bakersfield Now reports that a "severe vermin infestation" has shut down Pho Hut on California Avenue after roaches were found. The restaurant was closed by health inspectors after a routine inspection uncovered a significant rodent and cockroach infestation. The closure comes after inspectors found live and dead roaches throughout the facility, as well as rodent droppings and gnaw marks. The restaurant will remain closed until it addresses the vermin issues and passes a re-inspection.

KGET 17 tells us the City of Bakersfield is set to finalize the purchase of the Bank of America building. The city council is expected to approve the final purchase agreement for the downtown building at its next meeting. The city plans to use the building to consolidate several departments currently spread across multiple locations, potentially saving on lease costs. The building is expected to house the city’s finance, administrative services, and parks and recreation departments.

According to 23ABC, a judge has ordered a 15-year-old held on a murder charge after a 17-year-old was shot dead at a Bakersfield football game. The 15-year-old teen charged with the shooting death of another made his first court appearance in Juvenile Court on Wednesday morning. Kern County District Attorney Cynthia Zimmer identified the suspect as Gabriel Torres Reyes. A judge ordered Reyes to remain in custody on a first-degree murder charge in the death of 17-year-old Levi Brown, who was shot at a football game at Independence High School last Friday. Prosecutors charged Reyes with premeditated, first-degree murder, along with a gang enhancement and an allegation that he personally used a firearm causing Brown's death. Reyes denied the charges and allegations — the juvenile court equivalent of a not-guilty plea. Kern County District Attorney Cynthia Zimmer said California law requires the case to remain in juvenile court because Reyes was 15 at the time of the shooting.

KGET 17 reports that at least 1 person is in custody after a vehicle pursuit that ended in south Bakersfield. Police say the pursuit started in the area of South H Street and ended near South Union Avenue and Pacheco Road. No injuries were reported, and the suspect is facing charges.

According to 23ABC, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central California is expanding its one-on-one mentorship program to Kern County. The nonprofit, which has been mentoring young people for more than 50 years, currently serves Madera, Fresno, Kings, and Tulare counties. CEO Diane Phakonekham said Kern County has long been a priority for the organization. The program creates matches between adult volunteers and children ages 6 through 18. Children's safety is the organization's top priority.

KGET 17 tells us the Kern County High School District has announced tightened safety measures, following the deadly Independence HS shooting. The district says it will increase the number of security officers at all high school football games and other large events. It will also implement a clear bag policy for all events and increase the use of metal detectors at the gates. The district says it will work with local law enforcement to review its safety plans and make any necessary changes.

Something good

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central California is expanding its one-on-one mentorship program to Kern County and is looking for adult volunteers and business partners to support local youth. This expansion will provide more local youth with positive role models and support.

Coming up this week

The Personnel and Processes Committee will meet on Thursday, September 2, at 12:00 p.m. The Planning Commission will meet on Thursday, September 3, at 5:30 p.m. The Fox Theater will host a variety of events, including Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 on August 24, Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29, and MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA on September 4.

content:
The Daily Brief

Aaron Donald ends his 2 1/2-year retirement and returns to the Los Angeles Rams

Good morning, Bakersfield — it’s Sunday, August 30, 2026. Today’s top story is the return of NFL star Aaron Donald to the Los Angeles Rams after a two-and-a-half-year retirement. We’re waking up to a warm morning, with temperatures already at 86° at Meadows Field and an expected high of 92° later today. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 74, and no weather alerts are active in Kern County.

The Kern Overnight

Overnight, Kern County saw a series of incidents that kept law enforcement busy. The most significant call came around 11:26 p.m., when crews responded to a tractor-trailer fire on Pacheco Road. By 11:35, the tractor was reported as a total loss, though the trailer was salvaged. Around the same time, shortly before midnight, a caller reported hearing a shot fired from inside his living room; medical units were on scene. Later, around 2:48 a.m., officers went to Ginger Oak Lane for a welfare check after a crying caller reported a baby in the background. A subject was later seen running through the carport toward a warehouse, and units held the perimeter. Elsewhere, around 12:58 a.m., a large party on Potomac Avenue near Oswell Street turned into a physical fight, with one caller reporting possible shots — though it was unclear whether fireworks were involved. In addition, around 10:08 p.m., a man threatened to shoot the reporting party’s husband during a verbal dispute at a Bakersfield apartment complex. No weapon was seen at first, but the same subject was later seen walking through the complex with a baseball bat. Other incidents included a collision near Panama Lane and Ashe Road that required a tow, a verbal dispute with a possible gunshot heard, and a physical fight at an apartment on H Street.

Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 92° and a low around 62° tonight. It’s currently 86° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and no active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 74. Skies are expected to be clear, making for a warm late-summer day across the county.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Aaron Donald has ended his two-and-a-half-year retirement and will return to the Los Angeles Rams. The NFL star’s decision to come back to the field after an extended break is expected to bring a significant boost to the Rams’ defensive line. This move has generated excitement among fans and analysts alike, as Donald’s return promises to add depth and experience to the team’s roster for the upcoming season.

According to 23ABC, the League of Dreams tipped off its 2026 basketball season with more than 140 athletes and a new mascot. The event, held at Riverlakes Ranch Community Center, marked a milestone for the organization that provides adaptive sports opportunities for athletes with disabilities. The gym filled with cheers as teams came together for the season opener, and the Cal State Bakersfield women’s basketball team made a special appearance. Board Vice President Laura Avila emphasized that community support makes the programs possible, and the season also introduced the league’s first-ever mascot, Dreamer.

KGET 17 also reports that a man accused of posing as an NFL player to scam women allegedly tricked AI and Google, according to court documents. The suspect, who has not been named, is said to have used sophisticated methods to deceive his victims, highlighting the evolving nature of online scams. The case underscores the importance of vigilance in the digital age, as technology can sometimes be exploited for fraudulent purposes.

23ABC said the USS Abraham Lincoln sailed past Singapore on its way home from the Middle East. The U.S. aircraft carrier, one of the Navy’s largest warships, was supporting the U.S. war against Iran during its deployment. Its transit near Singapore early Sunday morning comes after a grueling deployment that included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 250 days. The Lincoln is expected to stop in Thailand for a port visit before returning to its base in San Diego, following concerns about the crew’s mental health and supply shortages during the lengthy deployment.

KGET 17 also announced that thousands of cold remedy nasal swabs have been recalled nationwide. The recall affects a specific batch of the product and is due to potential contamination concerns. Consumers are advised to check the batch numbers of their nasal swabs and to discontinue use if they have the affected product. Further details on the recall and instructions for returning the product are expected to be released by the manufacturer.

23ABC reported that Nova Sorella hosted a resource fair in Bakersfield to honor the founder’s son. The nonprofit brought together organizations such as Serving Hope and The Open Door Network to connect community members with essential services. PJ Jones, founder and executive director of Nova Sorella, organized the fair in honor of her son, Ty Jr. Jones, who was killed by gun violence in January 2017. The event, held on what would have been Ty Jr.’s birthday, aimed to bring hope to an underserved community and provided attendees with resources for work, housing, and more.

Something good

The League of Dreams tipped off its 2026 basketball season with more than 140 athletes and a new mascot. This event highlights the community’s commitment to providing inclusive sports opportunities for local youth, and the debut of the organization’s first-ever mascot, Dreamer, added to the excitement. Board Vice President Laura Avila noted that community support makes the programs possible, and the season opener was a heartwarming display of the impact adaptive sports can have on athletes and their families.

Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several events and meetings are on the calendar for Kern County residents. On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater will host a variety of shows, including the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 starting on August 24, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA on September 4, The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies also on September 4, Talib Kweli -- One Night Only In Bakersfield on September 5, JUSTIN WILLMAN: ONE FOR THE AGES TOUR on September 10, and MAX AMINI LIVE IN BAKERSFIELD! on September 12.

headline: Shafter PD investigates fatal crash on East Lerdo Highway
content:
The Daily Brief

Shafter PD investigates fatal crash on East Lerdo Highway

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 31, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a high near 91° and air quality at a moderate 58. Overnight, a tractor-trailer fire on Pacheco Road made for a busy night for our first responders. Let’s get you caught up on Kern County.

The Kern Overnight

The night brought a mix of incidents across Kern County, from fires to welfare checks. Around 11:26 p.m., crews responded to a reported fire on Pacheco Road. By 11:35, units described the tractor as a total loss, with the trailer being salvaged. Shortly before midnight, a caller reported hearing a shot from inside his living room, and medical units were on scene. Around 2:48 a.m., officers went to Ginger Oak Lane for a welfare check with medical aid requested. The reporting party was crying and unable to answer questions, with a baby heard crying in the background; a subject was later seen running through the carport toward a warehouse, and units held the perimeter. Around 12:58 a.m., officers were sent to Potomac Avenue near Oswell Street for a large party that turned into a physical fight, with one caller reporting possible shots heard — unclear whether fireworks. Around 10:08 p.m., a man threatened to shoot the reporting party’s husband during a verbal dispute at a Bakersfield apartment complex. No weapon was seen at first, but the same subject was later seen walking through the complex with a baseball bat. Other incidents included a collision near Panama Lane and Ashe Road, a verbal dispute during which a possible gunshot was heard, a physical fight at an apartment on H Street, a trucker on the highway needing CHP to arrange a tow, an attempt to locate a 7-year-old last seen on a residence’s front porch wearing a black shirt, a welfare check on a woman who told bystanders she had been thrown out of a vehicle, medical aid for an unknown complaint on South 8th Street, medical aid for a possible overdose where Narcan was administered, a search for a suspect armed with a switchblade who fled on foot north on Mount Vernon Avenue, medical aid on South Haley Street where interpreters were requested, medical aid for a seizure, and a man on a scooter reportedly armed with a knife — and possibly a gun — last seen near a 711 parking lot in the Olive Drive area.

Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 91° and a low around 60° tonight. It’s currently 70° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is at a moderate 58. We’re expecting clear skies and calm conditions throughout the day.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Aaron Donald has ended his 2 1/2-year retirement and is returning to the Los Angeles Rams. The star defensive tackle’s decision to come out of retirement and rejoin the team has surprised fans and analysts alike. This move is expected to bolster the Rams’ defensive line significantly, and it comes as the team prepares for the upcoming NFL season. Aaron Donald’s return is a major development for the Rams and for football fans across Southern California.

According to 23ABC, the USS Abraham Lincoln sailed past Singapore early on Sunday as it headed home after a grueling deployment in the Middle East. The aircraft carrier, one of the U.S. Navy’s largest warships, was supporting the U.S. war against Iran during its deployment. Its transit near Singapore marks a key point in its journey back to its base in San Diego. The Lincoln’s deployment included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 250 days, and concerns had grown about the crew’s mental health and supply shortages. The carrier is expected to stop in Thailand for a port visit before continuing its journey home.

KGET 17 also told us that thousands of cold remedy nasal swabs are being recalled nationwide due to potential contamination. The recall affects certain lots of the product and is being conducted in cooperation with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Consumers are advised to check the lot numbers of their nasal swabs and to discontinue use if their product is affected. Further details on the recall, including the specific lot numbers and instructions for returning or disposing of the affected items, are expected to be released by the manufacturer.

Bakersfield Now said that the Bakersfield Police Department is seeking possible victims after a man was arrested for sexual assault cases dating back to 2017. The arrest has prompted investigators to look into whether there may be additional victims who have not yet come forward. The BPD is encouraging anyone with information related to these cases to contact them. This development underscores the importance of reporting such incidents to law enforcement.

Something good

The League of Dreams tipped off its 2026 basketball season with more than 140 athletes and introduced a new mascot. This community-focused event provides opportunities for individuals with physical and developmental disabilities to participate in sports. The gym filled with cheers as teams came together for the season opener, and the organization’s first-ever mascot, Dreamer, made its debut. The event also featured a special appearance by the Cal State Bakersfield women’s basketball team. Board Vice President Laura Avila noted that community support makes these programs possible and that donations and partnerships are the foundation of everything the league offers. This season marks a milestone for the organization and brings joy to many families in Kern County.

Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several public meetings and events worth noting. On Tuesday, September 2, the Police Civil Service Commission will meet at 8:30 a.m., and the Personnel and Processes Committee will convene at 12:00 p.m. On Wednesday, September 3, the Planning Commission is set to meet at 5:30 p.m. Additionally, the Fox Theater has a variety of shows scheduled. On Saturday, September 6, the theater will host “The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies.” On Sunday, September 7, Talib Kweli will perform for one night only in Bakersfield. And on Wednesday, September 10, Justin Willman’s “One for the Ages Tour” will take the stage. Be sure to check the Fox Theater’s website for ticket information and additional details on these upcoming events.

headline: From Melbourne to Bakersfield: The unlikely match for Bakersfield College's starting quarterback
content:
The Daily Brief

From Melbourne to Bakersfield: The unlikely match for Bakersfield College's starting quarterback

Good morning, Kern County. It’s a mild start to September, with temperatures expected to top out at a comfortable 85 degrees today, but our top story carries some weight: four Bakersfield City Council seats are officially contested for the November ballot, setting up what could be a significant shift in local leadership. We’re also tracking the aftermath of a busy overnight for first responders, including a rollover on Highway 58 and a shots-fired report in the Coburn Ridge area, all while air quality holds at a moderate 57.

The Kern Overnight

It was a steady night for emergency crews across the county as Monday’s heat lingered into the evening and carried a familiar rhythm of calls into the early hours. Just after midnight, a vehicle rollover on westbound Highway 58 west of Tucker Road brought a multi-unit response, including a battalion chief, with an air unit standing by as a precaution. Westbound lanes were reduced while crews worked the scene; the extent of any injuries was not immediately available. Around 1:48 a.m., officers were sent to a residence in the Coburn Ridge area on reports of five to six shots fired, with callers describing subjects in ski masks at the door and a vehicle fleeing the area. The reporting party was checking security cameras as officers responded.

Elsewhere in the county, a grass fire off Wasco Pond Road north of Cecil Avenue drew an engine, a patrol unit, and additional assistance around 1:30 a.m., with crews stopping the fire’s progression and being released from the scene. In north Bakersfield, officers ran a short foot pursuit of a male on a dirt bike along a Chester Avenue bike path, losing visual at Chester Avenue before units began searching the area. Deputies and medics also responded to a residence on Marble Street just before 11 p.m., where a 17-year-old was reported making suicidal statements; family members were contacted. A separate crisis call on West China Grade drew a mental health response, and a domestic disturbance on Meadows Street involving juveniles prompted officers to respond given the concern for children.

The overnight log included a steady stream of lesser calls as well: a small roadside fire on northbound Highway 99 south of Olive Drive, a vehicle fire on Elk Hills Road that turned out to be a dropped flare, a search for a subject in dark clothing last seen heading toward the Mount Vernon Bridge, and a welfare check on a missing 15-year-old last seen near Bernard Street. Crews also handled a court order violation with a firearm threat at Virginia Avenue and Powell Street, and CHP responded to a family member walking on the shoulder of northbound I-5 near the escape ramp. The night was busy, but by sunrise the county had settled into a routine, quieter Tuesday morning.

Today's weather

Expect a pleasant September day with a high near 85 degrees and a low around 58 degrees tonight. It’s currently 72 degrees at Meadows Field (KBFL), with no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is sitting at 57, which is moderate — sensitive individuals may want to take it a bit easier outdoors, but most residents will find conditions just fine. Fire crews are currently monitoring one active fire in Kern, the Rose Fire, so smoke-sensitive folks should stay aware of their local conditions.

Top stories

A local political scientist tells 23ABC that the November election could reshape Bakersfield city leadership, as four council seats — Ward 1, Ward 3, Ward 4, and Ward 7 — each drew at least one challenger against an incumbent. Ward 1’s Eric Arias, Ward 4’s Bob Smith, and Ward 7’s Manpreet Kaur each face a single challenger, while Ward 3 has the most crowded field with six candidates. Councilman Ken Weir is the only sitting member not seeking re-election this season. Political professor Ian Anderson noted that Kern County and Bakersfield tend to lean conservative, a pattern he says may continue in these races, and he highlighted a key detail for first-time voters: city council elections are decided by plurality, not majority, meaning the candidate with the most votes wins outright. Anderson expressed hope the competitive races will drive higher turnout, emphasizing that local elections often affect residents more directly than state or federal contests.

KGET 17 reports that a hit-and-run charge has been filed in the death of a man last October on Camino Media, moving the case one step closer to resolution for a family that has waited nearly a year for accountability. The charge stems from an incident on the street, and prosecutors have now formally brought the case forward. The report does not name the victim or the accused, but the filing signals that investigators have identified a suspect and believe they have enough evidence to proceed. For neighbors along that stretch of road, the news closes a chapter of uncertainty and opens the door to a court process that will determine what happened that night.

According to KGET 17, the Community Action Partnership of Kern is seeing demand for food assistance rise, with the agency’s leadership saying plainly, “We see the need going up.” CAPK, which has long been a backbone of food security efforts in the county, is grappling with increased pressure as families continue to navigate economic strain. The organization is working to meet the moment, but the signal from its leadership is clear: the need is real, it is growing, and community support will be essential to keep pace. For readers who have wondered whether their neighbors are still struggling, the answer from CAPK is an unequivocal yes.

Bakersfield Now reports that crews responded to a drone-like aircraft fire at the Elk Hills-Buttonwillow Airport, a scene that drew a first-alarm response before being handled. The incident involved some type of aircraft with drone-like characteristics, though the full details of what happened and how the fire started remain under investigation. The airport is remote and primarily serves industrial and agricultural traffic, but any fire on an airfield carries inherent risks. That crews contained it quickly is a relief; the investigation into the cause will determine whether this was a mechanical failure, a crash, or something else entirely.

Bakersfield Now also looks at the question of flash flooding in Kern County, turning to the National Weather Service to explain the risk and how residents can stay safe. While the desert and valley are no strangers to dry conditions, the NWS notes that the terrain here can be particularly vulnerable to flash flooding when storms do arrive, especially in burn scars and low-lying crossings. The key message is one of preparedness: know your route, don’t drive through flowing water, and heed warnings when they are issued. It’s a useful primer for a county where rain can be rare but dangerous when it finally comes.

The 23ABC report on the multi-state Salmonella outbreak linked to recalled eggs notes that Kern County has not been impacted locally, according to Kimberly Hernandez with Kern Public Health. The FDA and CDC are investigating 98 infections and 26 hospitalizations across 17 states, including California, with the outbreak linked in part to eggs from Midwest Poultry Services sold under brands like Country Morning, Simple Truth, and Kroger. The recalled eggs carry sell-by or best-by dates between July 20 and Aug. 17. Hernandez said the county has not been made aware of any affected product arriving locally or any connected cases, but she cautioned that travel or secondary distribution could still tie California cases to the outbreak — a reminder that food safety doesn’t always respect state lines.

Something good

One of the more heartening items on the calendar this week is the Spanish Speaking Conference, which KGET 17 reports will connect families with special resources available in the community. The event offers local families a chance to find support, information, and connections in a setting designed to meet them where they are. It’s a reminder that in Bakersfield, help is often just a conversation away — and that the community’s strength is built on neighbors reaching out to neighbors. For families navigating the often-complicated world of special needs services, having a dedicated space like this can make all the difference.

Coming up this week

For those who like to keep an eye on local government, the week ahead has a few gatherings worth noting. The Police Civil Service Commission meets Wednesday, September 2 at 8:30 a.m., and the Personnel and Processes Committee follows later that same day at noon. On Thursday, September 3, the Planning Commission convenes at 5:30 p.m. These are public meetings where decisions get made about the shape of the city — from the makeup of its police oversight to the growth and development that define its future — and residents are welcome to attend in person.

On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater is hosting The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies this Friday, September 4, followed by Talib Kweli’s One Night Only in Bakersfield on Saturday, September 5. Both are sure to draw a crowd, and they offer a good excuse to enjoy the cooler evening air and support one of downtown’s iconic venues. The following week brings Justin Willman on September 10, Max Amini on September 12, and Clay Walker’s Doin’ What I Love Tour on September 13, so the theater is busy with a little something for every taste.

As you head into the day, take a moment to be good to your neighbors — the overnight calls remind us that a lot of people are carrying heavy loads. Whether that’s a warm greeting, a helping hand, or simply patience in the checkout line, it matters. We’ll be back tomorrow morning with the news you need to start your day.
