The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Wednesday, September 23, 2026

Good morning, Kern County. As the Kern County Fair opens its gates this evening for the 2026 season, police are asking the public for help identifying two men suspected of breaking into an Oleander home – one reportedly wearing a black wig. The morning is mild at 70 degrees with moderate air quality, and no weather alerts are in effect, so it's a comfortable start before temperatures climb into the 90s.

The Kern Overnight

The most significant overnight incident came just before 11 p.m. when a city-wide officer safety broadcast was issued for a man armed with a knife at a hospital on Mount Vernon Avenue. He was escorted off the property and last seen heading toward East High School. Officers on both radio channels received his description, and the call was cleared once he was off the grounds.

Around the county, a caller stayed on the line with sheriff's dispatchers for nearly 20 minutes just before 10 p.m., reporting that people looking for him were armed and still in dark clothing in an east Bakersfield park. Deputies responded but were told to stand by while the call remained open. Early this morning at 1:45 a.m., two units responded to an assault with a bat in the 2700 block of White Lane. No one answered when dispatchers called back, and a description of the person who was hit went out to responding officers. Shortly after midnight, a caller reported a woman screaming for help in the 100 block of Hart Street near the river bed. The caller rang back a minute later to say the screaming could still be heard and asked officers to keep coming.

Fire crews handled two outside fires near Mount Vernon Avenue overnight – one along westbound Highway 58 just west of the avenue at 12:31 a.m., and a second at Mount Vernon Avenue and Kentucky Street at 1:41 a.m. The overnight log also included a disturbance at a Motel 6 on Oak Street, a welfare check on children with a mother reported to be in mental health crisis in the 4600 block of Columbus Street, and a disturbance at a Circle K in the 5600 block of Auburn Street where two people were swinging at the air with a 17-year-old present.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 94 degrees and a low around 64 tonight. It's currently 70 degrees at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is rated moderate at 66 on the AQI scale. No active fires are reported in the county this morning.

Top stories

Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police are searching for two men responsible for a residential burglary in the Oleander area, with one suspect described as wearing a black wig. The break-in occurred at a home in the neighborhood, and authorities believe the men may still be in the vicinity. Detectives are asking anyone with information about the suspects or a possible vehicle involved to come forward as the investigation continues.

According to KGET 17, the city of Bakersfield is seeing mixed results in its homelessness outreach efforts, even as an influx of people experiencing homelessness strains local resources. The report highlights that while some outreach teams are making contact and connecting individuals with services, the overall number of unsheltered residents appears to be rising. City officials are evaluating whether current strategies need adjustment to keep pace with demand.

In Taft, 23ABC says storefront vacancies on Center Street are slowly declining as the city and local businesses work to draw customers back downtown. Despite more than a dozen commercial properties still empty, the count has decreased slightly as properties have changed ownership and undergone improvements. Business owners like Michael Long of Black Gold Brewing Company are helping revitalize the area, but challenges remain – especially the high cost of bringing older buildings into compliance with current building, fire, and ADA codes.

The Kern County Coroner's office told Bakersfield Now that a 74-year-old woman from Oildale has died due to hyperthermia. The death underscores the dangers of extreme heat, even as temperatures taper off from the triple-digit highs earlier this month. Officials remind residents to check on elderly neighbors and those without air conditioning during warm weather.

23ABC also covered the formation of a new youth council in Delano, giving high school students a formal seat at the table in local government. The program, called NextGen Delano Leaders, was championed by Councilmember Sal Solorio Ruiz and launched after two years of planning. Students like Natalia Gutierrez and Ayari Pompa say the council will allow them to voice concerns that might otherwise go unheard, and Mayor Salvador Solorio-Ruiz called it a way to put young people first in city decision-making.

Something good

A Bakersfield student has been named a recipient of the 2026 CSU Trustees’ Award for Outstanding Achievement, an honor that recognizes exceptional academic and personal accomplishments. The award brings pride to the local community and highlights the talent and determination of Kern County's young people. Congratulations to this student for representing Bakersfield so well.

Coming up this week

The 2026 Kern County Fair opens tonight at the fairgrounds, with gates welcoming visitors for the first of 11 days of rides, exhibits, food, and entertainment. Vendors, FFA students, and game operators spent Tuesday putting finishing touches on their setups. The fair runs through early October. Tonight at the Fox Theater, the indie-pop band MEN I TRUST performs with special guest Evan Wright – doors open at 7 p.m. On Saturday, September 26, comedian Mike Sherm takes the Fox stage. The theater also announced its Cults & Classics season pass for 2026-2027, which includes screenings of "Young Frankenstein" on October 5 and shows by NB RIDAZ on October 9 and FANTASIAS on October 10. In local government, the city's Laws and Legislation Committee will meet Friday, September 25, at noon. That meeting is open to the public.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Thursday, September 24, 2026

Good morning, Kern County — it’s Thursday, September 24, and the big story is yesterday afternoon’s semi-truck fire at the Shafter Pilot Travel Center, which sent a thick black smoke plume visible for miles before crews contained it. Overnight, dispatchers also handled a serious report of a woman forced into a vehicle at gunpoint, and that investigation is active this morning. Conditions today stay warm and quiet — a high near 99, air quality at a moderate 71, and no active weather alerts.

The Kern Overnight

Calls kept emergency crews moving from last evening into the early hours, with most of the night’s traffic staying inside the city and the busiest stretch running from 10 to 11:30 p.m. At 10:43 p.m., crews were sent to a downed power pole with transformers and active power lines just north of East California Avenue and Washington Street. The caller asked that the area be blocked off so nobody would walk into the wires, and the utility — which already had a work order open on that line — was asked to respond.

The night’s fire calls began just after 11 p.m., when a full structure assignment went out for a vehicle burning next to a house in the 200 block of South King Street. Crews were told the fire was spreading to the house and then to the roof, and a caller told fire dispatchers that someone had lit the house on fire and might still have been at the scene. After a separate report that an ex-husband had tried to get into the home, dispatchers set alarms at that address to priority one for the rest of the night. A structure assignment followed at 11:48 p.m. for the 700 block of Height Street, and two more structure fire assignments came in between midnight and 2:30 a.m.

Just after 1 a.m., the sheriff’s office reported a brush fire at Magnolia Avenue and 7th Standard Road, and an engine, a patrol unit and a battalion were sent. The first unit on scene found about a quarter acre burning at a slow rate of spread, moving east and south along the road, and a second engine and another patrol unit were added to the call.

The most serious call came at 3:30 a.m., when a caller told city dispatchers that a woman had been forced into a vehicle at gunpoint and made to drive. The suspect was described as under the influence of methamphetamine, wearing a gray sweater and jogger pants, and the blue sedan was last seen heading eastbound on California Avenue. A second caller, on a different phone number, reported a woman yelling for help near South Oleander, and dispatchers could hear a female voice saying a man was attacking her. Around the same time, a domestic violence call over a divorce situation came in from the 400 block of Cypress Street. Officers were given the suspect and vehicle descriptions and searched the area, while city officers also handled a foot pursuit that ended in custody near South H Street and a welfare check on Columbus Street.

Today's weather

Expect another hot one. The National Weather Service calls for a high near 99 degrees with a low around 69 tonight, and it’s currently 68 at Meadows Field (KBFL) — a comfortable start before the afternoon heat builds. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality sits at 71, which is moderate, so sensitive groups may want to take it a little easier outdoors in the heat of the day. There are no active wildfire reports for the county this morning.

Top stories

A semi-truck parked at a fuel pump caught fire around 4:40 p.m. Wednesday at the Pilot Travel Center in Shafter, 23ABC reports, and the flames quickly spread to two additional semis before crews contained them. Business owners near the truck stop said they heard a loud explosion as the fire broke out; Kern County Fire Department Public Information Officer Jeremy Ruiz said the single vehicle spread to two semis with various loads, and the tractors and trailers became fully involved. Fuel and other products fed a thick black plume that rose above Shafter and was visible for miles, but crews kept the blaze from reaching other parts of the truck stop despite being surrounded by fuel — no one was hurt, crews stayed for cleanup into the evening, and investigators have not yet determined a cause.

President Trump’s disapproval rating has reached its highest point of his second term amid economic concerns, according to a new Emerson College poll reported by KGET 17. The survey found disapproval climbing as economic worries weigh on voters.

A pilot rescued after a jet crashed into the ocean near Morro Bay has been flown to Fresno for medical care, according to Bakersfield Now. The crash happened off the Central Coast, and the pilot was taken to Fresno after being rescued; no word yet on the pilot’s condition.

Stanford University has admitted that artificial intelligence was used to swap the gender and race of a student in an image, KGET 17 reports. The admission confirms that a student’s picture was altered with AI to change how the student appeared.

Children in Kern County face growing risks from online predators who use video games and social media platforms to target minors, according to a 23ABC report. Kern County Deputy District Attorney David Eller told the station that predators often exploit gaming platforms and associated apps like Discord to reach children without their parents’ knowledge — “do you really know who your child is talking to?” — and he pointed to last week’s arrests of two suspects, one from Fresno accused of arranging to meet a minor decoy deployed by the Kern County Sheriff’s Office and another from Duarte accused of using a social networking platform to try to meet a minor in person. Eller said the cases highlight aggressive joint efforts by the Bakersfield Police Department and the Sheriff’s Office to track down people accused of preying on children online, and local counselor Yadira Vargas of the Kern County Network for Children added that predators often pretend to be other children — making regular parent-child conversations a key prevention tactic.

A federal judge has ordered the White House to immediately restore access to CNN, MSNBC, and Politico, KGET 17 reported. The ruling directs the administration to reinstate the news organizations’ credentials without delay.

Bakersfield Search and Rescue is asking for meal donations as volunteers patrol Kern County Fair parking lots, Bakersfield Now reports. Team members are spending long shifts watching over fairgoers’ vehicles, and meal donations help keep them going through the day.

Something good

One of the sweetest traditions in Kern County is back in its familiar spot: the beloved cinnamon roll vendor has returned for the 50th Kern County Fair. For fairgoers who have visited year after year, that stand is more than a place to buy a pastry — it’s part of what makes the fair feel like home. And the volunteers from Bakersfield Search and Rescue patrolling the fair’s parking lots are a quiet reminder that neighbors look out for one another.

Coming up this week

Two public meetings are on the calendar in the next several days. The Laws and Legislation Committee convenes Friday, September 25, at noon, and the Planning Commission holds its next regular session Thursday, October 1, at 5:30 p.m. Both meetings are open to the public.

At the Fox Theater, the weekend brings MIKE SHERM on Saturday, September 26, kicking off a busy stretch of fall shows. Looking ahead, the lineup includes Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein on October 5, NB Ridaz: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour on October 9, Fantasias on October 10, and United We Dance: Festival Energy on October 16. The theater has also announced its Cults & Classics Season Pass for the 2026–2027 season.

And the 50th Kern County Fair continues, with search-and-rescue volunteers out in the parking lots and that familiar cinnamon roll stand back for another year. If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make a lap around the fairgrounds, this is the week.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Friday, September 25, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield, and happy Friday, September 25. Fire crews carried the night, knocking down a garage fire off C Street in southeast Bakersfield and a vacant double-wide trailer in a Rosamond mobile home park, both before dawn. Today brings a high near 91, a mild 66 degrees right now at Meadows Field, no weather alerts anywhere in the county, and moderate air quality at 64.

The Kern Overnight

The garage fire came in at 2:21 a.m., when dispatchers sent a reinforced structure assignment to the 2200 block of C Street, across from a home there, after multiple callers reported fire on the same block. The first response included four engines, two truck companies, a rescue and two battalions. Crews held the address until a unit cleared the scene shortly after 3 a.m.

Up in Rosamond, crews were sent to a mobile home park on Rosamond Boulevard at 1:37 a.m. for several reports of a trailer on fire. The first medic squad on scene found a fully involved double-wide at the back of the park with no exposures — a vacant trailer that had been left outside the park on a graded lot. Crews knocked it down with the first tank of water and kept units on hand for water supply; a county engine and battalion added to the call were cancelled once things were under control.

Just before midnight, smoke brought a city and county battalion to the former Family Dollar building at Niles Street and Mount Vernon Avenue at 11:46 p.m. Crews found heavy smoke, and by 11:56 p.m. dispatchers confirmed primary and secondary searches were complete and the building was clear. Earlier, at 10:39 p.m., an engine responding to smoke near the freeway found a grass fire along the on-ramp from Highway 58 to Highway 99, then checked behind a nearby discount store and found nothing burning there.

At 12:59 a.m., an engine and an ambulance were sent to the gate of Kern Valley State Prison in Delano for a reported overdose, with the ambulance asked to stage in case transport was needed. On the police side, officers ran to disturbances — including a fight between two siblings — suspicious-person reports, a shots-heard call that put a description of a dark pickup leaving eastbound out to units, and a domestic violence report relayed from a hotel. There was also medical aid in the 300 block of Kentucky Street. Police traffic thinned out after 3 a.m.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 91 today and a low around 65 tonight, so it's a warm one with a comfortable finish. It's currently 66 degrees at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and nothing active on the fire front in what we're tracking this morning. Air quality is 64 — the moderate range, which is where most of us go about our day without thinking twice about it, though it's worth keeping in mind if you're planning a long run or a long shift outdoors.

Top stories

23ABC reports that professional soccer player Gyasi Zardes drew dozens of fans to Sportsplex Bakersfield for a meet-and-greet, with some supporters lining up as early as 6 p.m. Zardes, who played for Cal State Bakersfield's men's team from 2009 to 2012 and went on to the U.S. Men's National Team, toured the facility and signed autographs. The Rangel family was among the first in line: Benjamin Rangel, two years into playing soccer himself, said it was his first time meeting a pro. His mother, Cassandra, said it matters that Zardes came from the same town. Zardes told 23ABC he was speechless that kids had waited for him, and said he'd take his time with families because "one conversation can change a kid's life."

KGET 17 reports that candidates for Kern County Board of Education Trustee Area 3 gathered on a debate stage for a wide-ranging conversation. The station also posted video of the debate for voters who want to watch it in full. That's the extent of what we have on the exchange this morning, so we'll leave it there rather than guess at what was said.

Bakersfield Now reports that northbound lanes of Interstate 5 near Gorman have reopened after a semi-truck jackknifed. That headline is all the detail we have right now, but for anyone heading south over the Grapevine today, it's the answer to the question you'd have been asking.

According to 23ABC, Delano voters heard from two city council challengers Thursday at a candidate forum at the De Vino Event Center. Local realtor Elizabeth Arteaga Gonzalez said affordable housing is personal to her and wants the city to bring back a grant program that helped first-time homebuyers with down payments, so families can stay and thrive in Delano. Carlton M. Lennon, who has run for the seat before, said he doesn't think the city is maximizing its potential and wants to attract businesses and keep professionals who work in Delano spending there, pointing to sales tax as the payoff. Incumbents Liz Morris and Mario Nunez, both seeking another term, didn't appear in person; Nunez said in a written statement that he wasn't able to attend. The forum was moderated by 23ABC Delano Neighborhood Reporter Ruby Rivera.

Bakersfield Now reports, in a headline, that Bakersfield police say a child was hurt in a wreck, with a truck passenger in custody and the driver still at large. We don't have anything beyond that headline this morning — no location, no condition, no names — and we won't fill in the blanks.

Something good

Nina Ha calls herself just another mother in Bakersfield, but the kids in this town know her as something else entirely. She started volunteering at her children's schools to read aloud, and one day, on a whim, she showed up dressed as Wonder Woman. The class loved it, and the invitations followed — Celebrity Reader Day, Read Across America, Career Day — and she's been doing it ever since.

Ha moved here more than three decades ago to start a family and found her community in the Bakersfield Chinese Women's Club, a group she says has been running for more than 75 years. Its biggest fundraiser is an annual Christmas dinner that raises thousands of dollars for hard-working high school students headed to college. Local restaurants have pitched in too — Ha said China Bistro has donated thousands of dollars in profits to support the club's fundraisers and student tuition. The costume is the fun part; the fund is the point.

Coming up this week

The city's Laws and Legislation Committee meets today, Friday, September 25, at noon — a good one to watch if you follow how local rules get shaped before they reach the full council. Then the Planning Commission takes up its agenda on Thursday, October 1, at 5:30 p.m., which is where land-use and development questions in Bakersfield usually get their first real public airing.

At the Fox Theater, the calendar fills up fast after this weekend. Mike Sherm takes the stage Saturday, September 26. The Cults & Classics series continues with Young Frankenstein on Monday, October 5, part of a season pass that runs through the 2026–2027 lineup and has already been underway since late August. NB Ridaz brings the "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour to the Fox on Friday, October 9, followed by Fantasias on Saturday, October 10, and United We Dance — billed as festival energy, all night — on Friday, October 16. Tickets for the October shows are worth checking sooner rather than later if you've been meaning to go.

Enjoy the Friday, and stay cool out there this afternoon — 91 is nothing we haven't handled before, but it's still 91.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Saturday, September 26, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. As we head into a warm Saturday with a high near 92, moderate air quality at an AQI of 60, and no active weather alerts, the top story today is that Maya Cinemas in Delano is staying open despite owing nearly $150,000 in unpaid property taxes, according to a 23ABC investigation. Also making news: Bakersfield police are asking the public to help identify two forgery suspects, and a verbal altercation at Valley Plaza Mall escalated into a spray incident that left shoppers unsettled.

The Kern Overnight

Overnight, Kern County emergency crews handled a heavy fire shift and a moderate police load, with most calls concentrated before midnight and thinning out after 3 a.m. The most significant incident was a structure fire in an alley behind the 1000 block of Flower Street, dispatched just before 1 a.m. when arriving companies reported flames in an alley off Owens Street. Crews checked the building for extension and held the address through the initial attack. Shortly after 4 a.m., multiple callers reported a grass fire south of the 48th station area along East Bear Mountain Boulevard, with concern that it could reach an electrical pole; an engine, two patrols and a battalion were assigned, and crews approaching on Interstate 5 reported being just south of the fire. Two vehicle fires burned at opposite ends of the county in the pre-dawn hours, though no major injuries were reported. On the law enforcement side, officers responded around 12:58 a.m. to a motel on Union Avenue for a person reportedly armed with a firearm; the subject was described as moving on foot, and units coordinated on arrival. Earlier, at 10:26 p.m., a disturbance involving five or six females against one person drew a large response after a caller reported one woman holding a firearm near a black pickup parked in front of a residence. A victim also told dispatchers around 2:47 a.m. that he had been struck with a crowbar by a man in his 20s wearing all black clothing; the report was taken for follow-up. Additional calls included a disturbance at the 100 block of 20th Street West around 10:10 p.m., where a manager relayed a report of employees trying to separate two parties outside a business, and a loud music complaint on the 2700 block of Holland Street at 10:17 p.m.

Today's weather

Expect a dry, warm Saturday with a high near 92 degrees and a low around 65 tonight. As of early morning, Meadows Field (KBFL) reported a current temperature of 64 degrees under mostly clear skies. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 60, which is typical for this time of year and shouldn’t pose a significant concern for most residents, though those sensitive to particulate matter may want to limit prolonged outdoor exertion. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no major fires are burning locally.

Top stories

According to 23ABC, Maya Cinemas in Delano is staying open despite owing nearly $150,000 in unpaid property taxes dating back to 2021. County records obtained by the station show the theater owes $148,494.08 in back taxes, and Oct. 16 is listed as a potential seizure date if the debt is not paid. But Delano Mayor Salvador Solorio Ruiz shared a Facebook statement saying he spoke directly with Maya Cinemas CEO Francisco Schlotterbeck, who reaffirmed the theater’s commitment to remain open. The mayor encouraged community support for the local business, while Schlotterbeck provided a brief email statement to 23ABC without elaborating on how the taxes would be resolved.

Bakersfield Now reports that police are asking for the public’s assistance in identifying two suspects in a forgery investigation. The department released images of the individuals but did not specify where the forgery occurred or the nature of the documents involved. Anyone with information is urged to contact BPD, though no callback number or specifics about the case were provided in the report.

Also from Bakersfield Now, a verbal altercation at Valley Plaza Mall escalated into a spray incident, according to video obtained by the station. The confrontation involved at least two individuals, and a substance was discharged, though authorities have not said whether the spray was pepper spray or another irritant. No injuries were reported, and mall security responded to the scene. The incident underscores ongoing concerns about public disturbances at one of Bakersfield’s largest shopping centers.

KGET 17 reports that the search continues for a 16-year-old girl last seen being dropped off at Bakersfield High School. The teen was reported missing earlier this week, and Bakersfield police have asked anyone with information to come forward. The case has drawn attention from the community, with social media posts circulating widely in hopes of finding her safe.

In other KGET 17 coverage, Week 6 of the high school football season brought scores from across Kern County, with several local teams posting competitive results. The station ran a full roundup of Friday night games, highlighting matchups that could shape playoff prospects later this fall. Football remains a central part of the community’s weekend rhythm, and the results are a talking point for fans and families.

23ABC also covered Bakersfield Ward 1 councilman Eric Arias’s re-election campaign, with Arias pointing to expanded crisis response services and affordable housing as key achievements. Arias, who has served six years, noted that about 1,600 new affordable housing units are coming online, though he acknowledged the progress has been slow. He also cited a 2.3% decrease in homelessness in Bakersfield over the past year, saying, “We have to do better. We have to do more.” His challenger is competing for the seat in the upcoming election.

Something good

There’s a bright note for fans of country music and literacy alike: California has officially designated September 25 as Dolly Parton Day, an honor championed by a Bakersfield state senator. The recognition celebrates the beloved entertainer’s legacy — including her Imagination Library program that has given millions of free books to children — and brings a little extra pride to Kern County, where the senator’s efforts helped make it happen. It’s a reminder that even in a busy news cycle, our community can rally around something joyful.

Coming up this week

The public calendar has a few key items to watch. The Bakersfield Planning Commission will meet Thursday, Oct. 1, at 5:30 p.m., and the agenda typically includes land-use decisions and development proposals that shape neighborhoods across the city. Residents who want to weigh in on zoning changes or new projects should note that meeting. On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch ahead. Tonight, Sep. 26, Mike Sherm takes the stage for a live performance. Next Monday, Oct. 5, the Fox launches its “Cults & Classics” season pass series with a screening of *Young Frankenstein*, promising a blend of cult films and classic cinema. On Friday, Oct. 9, the “NB Ridaz: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour” rolls into town, followed by “Fantasia” on Saturday, Oct. 10. And on Friday, Oct. 16, “United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night.” will keep the Fox Theater lively into the late hours. For families and sports fans, high school football continues this week, with many teams heading into league play. Keep an ear out for schedule changes or cancellations due to weather, though the forecast looks clear into the start of October.

summary: Today, we remember the lives of Vanessa, Kylie, and Kloie Wetmore as their family and friends gathered for a…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Sunday, September 27, 2026

Good morning, Kern County. Today, we remember the lives of Vanessa, Kylie, and Kloie Wetmore as their family and friends gathered for a memorial service yesterday. It's a mild start to the day at 64 degrees, with moderate air quality and no weather alerts to worry about.

The Kern Overnight

The overnight hours brought a flurry of activity across Bakersfield and Kern County, with law enforcement and fire crews responding to incidents ranging from a shooting to a missing child. Just after 1:30 a.m., units were dispatched to a shooting southeast of Bakersfield where a victim suffered a gunshot wound to the arm; dispatchers had no suspect description, and crews on scene also reported a gas leak inside the structure, prompting additional units to stage nearby. Earlier in the evening, fire crews responded to a senior living complex in the Brookside Drive area after reports of a burnt smell from vents and smoke inside one of the buildings — about 50 to 60 vehicles remained in the lot as crews investigated and asked for the main breaker to the condenser unit to be shut down. Downtown, officers were sent to 21st Street and Chester Avenue for a strong-arm robbery where a woman reported her phone taken; the suspect briefly left in a black SUV before returning, and the argument continued as officers arrived. In the county, deputies responded to a park for a disturbance involving roughly 20 juveniles with unknown weapons, though a fire engine initially dispatched was canceled. A kidnapping report came in from the 10500 block of Meacham Road, where the caller said juveniles had gone missing again after entering through a side entrance and the suspect remained outstanding. At a carnival area in Bakersfield, units took a report of a missing 6-year-old girl last seen near the kids' carnival wearing a pink cowboy T-shirt, and deputies were told the subject was part of a missing juvenile case from the agency. A priority welfare check in the 4500 block of Columbus Street escalated into a report of someone on the hood of a car while the driver moved backward trying to throw her off. Deputies also responded to a domestic violence report in the Park Drive area, where a caller said a 52-year-old man had kicked her in the ribs and punched her.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 90 degrees today and a low around 60 degrees tonight. It's currently 64 degrees at Meadows Field, with no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate, with an AQI reading of 52, so it's a good day to get outside but sensitive individuals may want to limit prolonged exertion. No active fires are reported in the area.

Top stories

23ABC reports that friends and family gathered Saturday at the Legends Event Center in Northwest Bakersfield to celebrate the lives of Vanessa, Kylie, and Kloie Wetmore, the mother and two daughters killed in a wrong-way crash on Highway 99 in August. Family members described the three as loving, free-spirited, and always there for the people around them. Garrett Wilkinson, a cousin of Kylie and Kloie and nephew of Vanessa, said he grew up close to his cousins, especially Kylie, and that he misses hearing their voices. The crash occurred on Aug. 16 when the Wetmores were heading home from a concert in Fresno and their car was struck by a wrong-way driver near Seventh Standard Road; the vehicle caught fire, killing all three. The California Highway Patrol identified the wrong-way driver as Jamie Rodriguez, a 44-year-old Tulare man who was hospitalized with major injuries, and the crash remains under investigation with no arrests or charges filed.

According to Bakersfield Now, Hurricane Odalys is not expected to make landfall, but its moisture may boost rain chances in California. The system is tracking well off the coast, but forecasters say residual moisture could drift inland and increase precipitation odds for parts of the state, including Kern County, later in the week. Residents should keep an eye on updated forecasts as the week progresses.

KGET 17 reports that Week 6 of the high school football season wrapped up across Bakersfield and Kern County with a full slate of scores. Teams battled it out Friday night under the lights, and the results are now available for fans to review. The season continues to heat up as local squads jockey for playoff positioning.

Bakersfield Now also covered an incident at Valley Plaza mall where an argument ended with a woman spraying a substance, with video showing the chaotic scene. The altercation drew attention from shoppers and prompted a response from security. Details on the substance and any injuries or arrests were not immediately available.

KGET 17 tells us about a magician and ventriloquist performing in the area who delivers what he calls the worst pirate puns you'll hear anywhere on the seven seas. The show promises a mix of comedy, magic, and ventriloquism for audiences looking for family-friendly entertainment. It's a lighthearted addition to the local arts scene this week.

23ABC reports that Bakersfield Ward 1 Councilman Eric Arias is making his case for re-election amid a public safety push. Arias, who has served six years in office, points to major upgrades across Ward 1 including revitalized recreation centers, expanded city departments for crisis response, and improvements to housing units. He noted that about 1,600 units of affordable housing are coming online, though it took years to reach that point. Arias also highlighted a 2.3% decrease in homelessness in Bakersfield over the last year, acknowledging the city needs to do better. With one challenger in the race, Arias says he remains committed to delivering on promises made to the community.

23ABC also reports that Maya Cinemas in Delano is staying open despite nearly $150,000 in unpaid property taxes. Rumors of a possible closure circulated on social media after the Maya Cinemas in Fresno shut down, but Delano Mayor Salvador Solorio Ruiz posted a Facebook statement saying he spoke with CEO Francisco Schlotterbeck, who assured him the theater would remain open. However, newly uncovered records from the Kern County Treasurer-Tax Collector's website show the theater owes $148,494.08 in unpaid property taxes from 2021 to 2026. County records list Oct. 16 as a potential seizure date and auction if the taxes are not paid. Schlotterbeck responded with a brief email statement, though its full content was not provided.

Something good

California has officially designated September 25 as Dolly Parton Day, with a Bakersfield senator leading the effort. The recognition honors the singer's contributions to literacy and the arts, bringing a positive spotlight to the community. It's a fitting tribute to a beloved figure whose work has inspired generations.

Coming up this week

The Bakersfield Planning Commission will meet on Thursday, Oct. 1 at 5:30 p.m. to discuss land use and development matters. The Fox Theater has a busy lineup ahead: "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" plays on Oct. 5, followed by the NB RIDAZ "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour" on Oct. 9, "FANTASIAS" on Oct. 10, "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." on Oct. 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour on Oct. 17. For those looking to plan ahead, the "Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027" series kicked off Aug. 24 and runs through the season. Mark your calendars and enjoy the week ahead, Kern County.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Monday, September 28, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. A quiet Monday is settling over Kern County after a busy night for first responders, with a house fire knocked down before dawn on Goodman Street and a shooting investigation underway on King Street. Temperatures are mild this morning at 55 degrees, air quality is good, and a Lake Wind Advisory is in effect through this evening — so if you're heading to the water, keep an eye on the chop.

The Kern Overnight

The night's most significant call came just after 5 a.m., when firefighters were dispatched to a house fire on Goodman Street. Arriving crews reported smoke showing, then fire coming from the front of a single-story, single-family home. The alarm was reinforced, and incoming units were held for assignments while crews went to work. Command reported the fire knocked down within a few minutes and started a primary search of the home, with a truck preparing for vertical ventilation. No injuries were immediately reported.

Earlier, at 3:08 a.m., units were sent to a shooting call on King Street. Fire crews already on a medical aid at the same location relayed that a shooting had occurred there and that a victim had an injury. Deputies were dispatched to take the scene. Around 1 a.m., officers responded to the area of a hospital and the juvenile justice center after a report of a transient man with no shirt waving a machete and yelling. The description was broadcast for officer safety, but officers checked the parking lot and surrounding blocks and did not find him.

At 4:37 a.m., a truck, two engines and a battalion were sent to a vehicle into a pole at Calloway Drive and Tuscarora Drive. Crews reported the scene and cleared the call. Just before 10 p.m. Sunday, dispatchers advised units that family at a command post were trying to find a 13-year-old girl whose phone last exchanged a text message with family about 9:08 p.m. and had not moved since, showing just east of one of the buildings at the fairgrounds. She was described as wearing a white long-sleeved shirt, dark blue jeans and white shoes, and was believed to be with two other teenagers and their families. At 2:36 a.m., officers were sent to a location on North Chester Avenue after a caller reported being assaulted by two females. The caller said the suspects were across the street from the address, and dispatchers noted the call was tied to an earlier call for service at the same location.

The overnight log also included a report of a man down on Union Avenue around 9:20 p.m., with units sent after a caller reported a man with no shirt and dark pants lying on the sidewalk. The hours between 3 and 5 a.m. were mostly welfare checks and medical calls.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 80 degrees today and a low around 59 tonight. It's currently 55 degrees at Meadows Field. The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a Lake Wind Advisory in effect until 7 p.m., so boaters and anyone near local lakes should use caution. Air quality is good, with an AQI reading of 44. No active fires are being reported in the county.

Top stories

23ABC reports that the Tejon Indian Tribe brought its annual "Honoring Our Ancestors" Pow Wow back to Cal State Bakersfield for the first time since 2019, celebrating Native American culture, tradition, and community. A grand entry of dancers marked the return of the tradition to CSUB as tribal members and visitors came together for the two-day gathering. Tribal spokesperson Candi Asuncion said the pow wow is a celebration — a chance to honor ancestors, loved ones no longer here, and the tribe's traditions and cultures. Visitors from as far as Sacramento attended, and demonstrators showed traditional crafts like flintknapping, the process of shaping stone into tools.

According to 23ABC, friends and family gathered at the Legends Event Center in Northwest Bakersfield Saturday to celebrate the lives of Vanessa, Kylie, and Kloie Wetmore, a mother and her two daughters killed in a wrong-way crash on Highway 99 in August. Family members described the three as loving, free-spirited, and always there for the people around them. Garrett Wilkinson, a cousin of Kylie and Kloie and nephew of Vanessa, said he grew up close to his cousins, especially Kylie, and misses hearing their voices. The crash remains under investigation by the California Highway Patrol, and no arrests or charges have been filed against the wrong-way driver, identified as a 44-year-old Tulare man.

23ABC reports that Bakersfield Ward 1 councilman Eric Arias is making his case for re-election, pointing to public safety improvements and efforts to keep the city's budget from dipping into reserves. Arias, who has served six years in office, highlighted revitalized recreation centers, expanded city departments to strengthen crisis response services, and about 1,600 units of affordable housing coming online. He noted that homelessness in Bakersfield has decreased by 2.3% in the last year, though he acknowledged more work is needed. Arias faces one challenger for the Ward 1 seat.

KGET 17 reports on Week 6 scores from the high school football season across Bakersfield and Kern County. The Friday night action saw teams battling it out on the gridiron as the season moves deeper into league play. Full results and standings are available from the outlet.

Bakersfield Now reports that an argument at Valley Plaza mall ended with a woman spraying a substance, with video showing the chaotic scene. Details on the incident and any injuries or arrests were still developing at press time.

Something good

California has officially designated September 25 as Dolly Parton Day, with a Bakersfield senator leading the effort to honor the beloved entertainer. The recognition celebrates Parton's contributions to music and literacy, bringing a moment of statewide pride to Kern County. It's a nice reminder that even in a busy news week, there's room for a little joy and gratitude.

Coming up this week

The Bakersfield Planning Commission is scheduled to meet Thursday, October 1, at 5:30 p.m. The agenda will be posted ahead of the meeting and typically includes land-use decisions, development proposals, and zoning matters that shape the city's growth. Residents interested in local development should plan to attend or watch online.

Looking ahead on the entertainment calendar, the Fox Theater has a busy month ahead. The Cults & Classics series continues with "Young Frankenstein" on October 5. The NB RIDAZ tour rolls through on October 9, followed by "FANTASIAS" on October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." takes over the Fox on October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour arrives on October 17. Tickets and showtimes are available through the theater's website.

For high school football fans, Week 7 kicks off this Friday with teams across Kern County continuing their push toward the playoffs. Check local schedules for game times and locations.

headline: Jay Thomas Manuel makes big splash with Jeff Mouse
summary: The story leading the day is a hard one: a veteran CHP officer was killed Monday evening in a crash on…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Tuesday, September 29, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a hard one: a veteran CHP officer was killed Monday evening in a crash on Highway 99 near Tipton, and we have the details below. Closer to home, the night was busy with a structure fire that spread into grass near the Kern-Tulare county line, a grass fire near a church off Auburn Street, and a robbery that ended with one person in custody. Today looks warm and calm — a high near 86, no weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a moderate 72.

The Kern Overnight

The largest call of the night came at 1:46 a.m., when crews were sent toward County Line Road east of Road 40 after callers reported a large column of smoke and a glow on the horizon. What began as a structure fire had spread into grass and was pushing north at a slow rate of spread, settling at about five acres. Crews anchored off the roadway and worked the heel and flanks while a second unit covered the structures on the south side. Command reported the fire contained and crews in cleanup, and mutual aid requested from Tulare County was canceled.

Earlier, at 10:18 p.m., a patrol, two engines and a battalion were sent to the Morning Drive area, where grass the size of a house was burning near a church off Auburn Street after multiple callers reported it. The full assignment went to the fire. At 1:28 a.m., crews reported light smoke showing from one side of a building in the 900 block of Baker Street and said they were going in to investigate, with incoming units staged and an incident commander assigned. An earlier alarm at the same block was cleared after a crew walked the building and found no audible alarm and no sign of distress or hazard inside.

Deputies had their hands full as well. At 12:47 a.m. a priority one domestic call was broadcast for the 9500 block of Brimhall Road, behind a business; the suspect was described as a man in his 30s in all black who left in a gray pickup, with a second man in dark clothing in an unknown sedan. At 12:52 a.m. deputies were sent to a suspicious person call involving a man with a firearm reported knocking on doors. At 1:14 a.m., a resident reported that a neighbor had come into the home through an unlocked front door, gone as far as a bedroom door and then crossed the street — described as a man 18 to 20 years old in a black shirt and jeans, slim with curly hair. And at 3:01 a.m., several units were called to assist after a robbery was reported; officers put one person in custody, and the victim told officers the robbery happened just east of where the stop was made. The rest of the overnight log was medical aids, alarm calls and traffic stops.

Today's weather

It's currently 79 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 86 this afternoon and a low around 63 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is 72 — moderate, which is a reasonable day to be outside if you're not especially sensitive to smoke or dust. No active fires were reported in the county as of this morning beyond the overnight incidents crews handled. Expect a warm, still September day across the valley, with the usual evening cooldown after sundown.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that a Wasco man killed in an early morning shooting has now been identified by the coroner. The identification closes one small gap in a case that began with gunfire in the early hours, and it gives the man's family and the community a name to hold onto as investigators continue their work. We'll keep following what authorities release about the circumstances.

According to 23ABC, a veteran CHP officer was killed in the line of duty Monday evening in a crash on State Route 99 near Tipton. Officer Brian Liles, 44, was riding a department-issued motorcycle northbound just south of Avenue 152 around 5:11 p.m. when it collided with a truck-tractor; the collision ejected him from the motorcycle and he was struck by a passing vehicle. Despite lifesaving efforts, he died at the scene. Liles was a CHP veteran of more than 16 years, serving San Jose, Hayward and Fresno before transferring to Visalia in 2019, and in December 2025 he became one of the first motorcycle officers assigned to the Visalia Area. He is survived by his wife, two children, parents and siblings. The CHP's Central Division Multi-Disciplinary Accident Investigation Team is leading the investigation. This one lands hard across the valley — a motorcycle officer doing routine work on a highway many of us drive every week.

KGET 17 reports that attorneys clashed as a competency trial was granted for a woman charged in a crash that killed a married couple. The ruling means the case will pause while the court examines whether the defendant is competent to stand trial — a procedural step, but a significant one for the families of the couple who died. Competency proceedings can shape how, and whether, a case moves forward, and the families involved have already waited a long time for answers.

Bakersfield Now reports that Congressman Valadao will host Speaker Mike Johnson at a get-out-the-vote rally in Bakersfield on Wednesday. The visit puts national political attention squarely on the valley in the final stretch before the election, and it's a signal of how much both parties are watching this district. Whatever your politics, it's worth knowing the traffic and attention that will follow a visit of that size midweek.

23ABC reports that the executive director of the Mission at Kern County will hold a 24-hour addiction awareness conversation for the second year running. Carlos Baldovinos will sit on a bench for 24 consecutive hours on Oct. 8 and 9 for an event called Conversation on a Bench, and this year he wants to focus on prevention. He told the station that the most powerful moments last year came from family members of people struggling with addiction — parents asking how they can help their son or daughter — and he also saw the other side: people in recovery who reconnected with family, found work and housing, and are thriving. He pushed back on the idea that addiction is a lost cause.

KGET 17 reports that Jay Thomas Manuel is making a big splash with Jeff Mouse. We'll be honest with you: that's the headline we have, and we won't pretend to know more than it says. Consider it a curiosity worth a click if you're so inclined.

Bakersfield Now is asking readers: does hotter weather stop you from attending the Kern County Fair? It's an informal reader poll, but it touches a real local question — how much September heat shapes whether families spend an evening at the fairgrounds. If you've got an opinion, that's where to register it.

Something good

For the second year, the director of the Mission at Kern County will hold a 24-hour conversation aimed at raising awareness about addiction, and this year he's adding a focus on prevention. It continues a local effort to keep the community talking about recovery and support — and the stories from last year, from both families in pain and people who came out the other side, are exactly the kind of thing that keeps that conversation honest. If you've been touched by addiction in your own family, you'll recognize the weight of it.

Coming up this week

The Bakersfield Planning Commission meets Thursday, Oct. 1 at 5:30 p.m. — the main civic meeting on the calendar this week, and the place to be if you want to see what's proposed for your part of town before it's decided.

Looking further out, the Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. The Cults & Classics season pass for 2026-2027 is on sale, and the series brings *Young Frankenstein* to the Fox on Oct. 5. NB RIDAZ takes the stage Oct. 9 for the Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour, FANTASIAS follows Oct. 10, United We Dance brings an all-night festival energy show Oct. 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands Oct. 17. If you've been meaning to get downtown for a show, October is the month to do it.

And mark your calendar for Oct. 8 and 9, when the Conversation on a Bench returns to the Mission at Kern County — 24 straight hours of talking about addiction, recovery and prevention, open to anyone who wants to listen or share. Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield.

The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Thursday, October 1, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Thursday, October 1, and the day's top story is a shooting call in east Bakersfield that had officers and medics out before dawn, plus a stabbing on Chester Avenue and a pair of semi-truck incidents on Highway 46 and Highway 58. Expect a hot one — a high near 98 — with no weather alerts and one active fire, the Grapevine Fire, still being worked by crews.

The Kern Overnight

The overnight log opened with a shooting call at 12:25 a.m. in east Bakersfield, where a caller told officers a man stepped out of a white four-door sedan, pointed a gun in the air and fired one round, and that a person was bleeding. A second party was reported to have driven a white four-door to a nearby motel, and units were checking the area through the early hours. Not long before that, at 12:18 a.m., crews were sent to an audible burglary alarm at a home on Millwood Way, near Thornwood Drive and Woodcastle Way, to cover the perimeter and the living room door.

At 1:19 a.m., a person walked into a business on Chester Avenue with a stab wound, and deputies and a fire crew responded to the area around Decatur Street and North Chester Avenue. On the highways, two semis — a maroon rig with a silver trailer and a Walmart semi — collided at 4:33 a.m. in the eastbound lanes of Highway 46 west of Interstate 5 and ended up stuck together in the roadway, forcing a backup and closing an exit while drivers were routed around. Earlier, at 10:39 p.m., a semi was reported on fire in the westbound lanes of Highway 58, and fire crews from a nearby station knocked down a grass fire in the same stretch shortly after. At 5:12 a.m., a silver sedan rolled over near East Brundage Lane and Kincaid Street, drawing a full rescue response; all parties were reported out of the vehicles.

The rest of the log was the usual mix — medical aids on Ponce de Leon Avenue, Primrose Avenue, and at White Lane and Hughes Lane, a vehicle fire north of Panama Road and Cottonwood Road, a shots-fired call on Hall Road near the Rasmussen Center, a robbery alarm at a Dollar General on the 2900 block of Niles Street, and a possible drunken driver reported in a white Mercedes SUV that couldn't hold its speed.

Today's weather

It's currently 88 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 98 and a low around 68 tonight. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, but fire crews are on one active fire in the county — the Grapevine Fire — so the dry heat is worth keeping in mind if you're out and about. Air quality readings weren't available this morning. If you've got outdoor plans, the cooler hours are early and late; the middle of the day will feel like the valley in October usually does.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield police are asking for the public's help identifying two men accused of a burglary on Ming Avenue. The department put out the call to the community as investigators work to identify the pair. If you have information, the department is the place to bring it — this is one where a neighbor who saw something may be exactly what moves the case.

According to 23ABC, an Oildale woman says she was set on fire at a local homeless encampment in July and that the people she accuses remain free months later. Frances Lopez, 33, told the station she was visiting a friend's tent on July 11 when three people confronted her friend over a money dispute, and that the encounter turned violent — she says gasoline was thrown and a flame lit, and she escaped the burning tent and made her way to a nearby trailer park for help. She spent nearly eight weeks in a Fresno burn unit, underwent four surgeries, and says doctors found second- and third-degree burns across 32 percent of her body. She's home now but still healing, with open wounds and daily dressing changes, and she told 23ABC she's frustrated that no arrests have been made.

KGET 17 also reports on substance abuse recovery in Kern County, with the message that addiction "is not because of a moral failure." The story centers on how recovery works here and the people doing it, framing addiction as a health issue rather than a character flaw. It's a useful read for anyone in Kern who has watched a family member or friend struggle and wondered where to turn.

Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police have released week-one statistics from the Kern County Fair: three arrests, 28 ejections, and 20 missing-or-found kids. The numbers give a sense of what a fair week looks like for officers working the grounds — mostly a lot of reuniting kids with their families. It's a reminder, as the fair continues, to keep an eye on little ones in the crowds.

23ABC reports that a stretch of Highway 46 in San Luis Obispo County has officially been designated the James Dean Memorial Highway, 71 years after the actor's death. Dean was headed west on Highway 46 on Sept. 30, 1955, and his final drive brought him through Kern County, including a stop at Blackwells Corner, before he continued toward the Central Coast. He was 24 when he died in the crash. Assemblymember Dawn Addis sponsored the resolution naming 4.3 miles of the new alignment, and Caltrans notes the road itself is transformed from the two-lane highway Dean knew into a divided expressway.

And 23ABC reports that a medical helicopter transporting a patient crashed off Catalina Island on Wednesday night, killing two people, hospitalizing two, and leaving a fifth person missing as of Thursday. The Coast Guard, area firefighters, and Los Angeles County Sheriff's divers worked through the night, and the search for the missing person continued Thursday morning alongside dives on the wreckage. The FAA said the pilot and a cabin crew member were killed, another cabin crew member was seriously injured, and a passenger had minor injuries. The cause was not immediately clear.

Something good

The Running with the Angels 5K is returning to Bakersfield, and it's the kind of event that matters quietly. It's a community gathering for families honoring babies lost too soon — a shared morning to remember and to stand with one another. If you've been looking for a way to support neighbors carrying that kind of loss, this is a gentle place to start.

Coming up this week

The Planning Commission meets tonight, Thursday, October 1, at 5:30 p.m. — the first of a run of public meetings this month. Next week, the City Council holds two sessions on Wednesday, October 7: a 3:30 p.m. meeting and a 5:15 p.m. meeting. The Housing and Community Development Committee meets Thursday, October 8, at noon. If you've got opinions about what's being built or funded around town, these are the rooms where it gets decided.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. The Cults & Classics season pass for 2026–2027 is on sale now, and the series brings *Young Frankenstein* to the Fox on Monday, October 5. NB RIDAZ takes the stage Friday, October 9, with the Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. United We Dance brings an all-night festival-energy show on Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands Saturday, October 17.

Have a good Thursday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there, and keep an eye on your neighbors.

headline: Steve Hilton faces steep odds in bid for California governor after 20-year GOP drought
summary: It's Friday, October 2, and the biggest political story in California runs straight through Kern County —…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Friday, October 2, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Friday, October 2, and the biggest political story in California runs straight through Kern County — Republican Steve Hilton's long-shot bid for governor, which 23ABC reports faces a 4.6-million-voter registration gap. Closer to home, the Riverview Marketplace project takes another step toward approval, and a new state law targets social media's grip on kids. Expect a hot one: a high near 100°, no active weather alerts, and no fires reported in the county.

The Kern Overnight

It was a night of pursuits, pole strikes, and fire calls across Kern County, according to preliminary emergency dispatch reports.

In Bakersfield, officers with helicopter support chased suspects who fled on foot across a property. The search drew air units overhead before the situation was resolved. Details remain preliminary and unconfirmed by an official source.

Fire crews also responded to a fire in Bakersfield around 9:25 p.m., followed minutes later by a structure fire reported on Cranbrook Avenue at about 9:27 p.m. In eastern Kern, crews worked a pair of vehicles that struck power poles — the kind of crash that can knock out electricity for surrounding blocks and tie up a roadway while crews make repairs.

As always, these early dispatch reports are just the first word, not the last. Names, exact locations, and outcomes will come from official sources as the day develops. What we can say this morning is that it was a busy overnight shift across the county, with no confirmed reports of serious injuries in the incidents described.

Today's weather

It's 66° at Meadows Field as of this morning, according to the National Weather Service — a comfortable start before the heat settles in.

Expect a high near 100° today, with a low around 69° tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are reported. Air quality readings were not available at the time of this brief.

If you're headed out this afternoon, plan for genuine valley heat: water, shade, and a little patience go a long way. The cool morning won't last, so get the errands done early if you can.

Top stories

23ABC reports that Republican Steve Hilton faces steep odds in his bid for California governor, with mail ballots set to arrive at homes in early October. Hilton, a former Fox News commentator, is running against Democrat Xavier Becerra in a state that hasn't elected a Republican to statewide office in two decades. Registered Democrats outnumber Republicans by roughly 4.6 million voters, and President Trump's endorsement — while helpful with the base — is widely unpopular outside it. GOP consultant Mike Murphy told the Associated Press the math is "very hard." For Kern County Republicans, it's a reminder that even a friendly local electorate can't overcome a two-to-one statewide gap.

According to KGET 17, two of the three candidates for Kern's Board of Education met on the debate stage, and the conversation stayed notably amicable. The exchange gave voters a look at where the candidates stand ahead of the election. School board races rarely draw big headlines, but they shape decisions that touch every family in the county — budgets, curriculum, and how local schools are run. With ballots arriving soon, this is the kind of down-ballot contest worth a few minutes of your attention.

KGET 17 also reports that the Riverview Marketplace project moved one step closer to approval, with the Bakersfield City Council set to consider its environmental impact report. The EIR is a required checkpoint before the project can move forward, and it's the stage where traffic, noise, and environmental concerns typically get aired. For residents near the proposed site, this is the moment to weigh in. The council's review will determine whether the project keeps its momentum or faces delays.

23ABC reports that California has enacted what experts call the nation's strongest law protecting children from social media addiction. Gov. Gavin Newsom signed Assembly Bill 1709, a bipartisan measure by Assemblymember Josh Lowenthal that strips platforms of autoplay and algorithmically personalized feeds for users under 16. For one Bakersfield family, the issue wasn't abstract: Citlali Soto, a student at Independence High School, said Instagram and TikTok once consumed three to four hours of her day before her father cut them off when she was 12 or 13. Five years later, she told 23ABC she has no desire to go back. Her father said the law would have made that difficult decision easier.

Bakersfield police have arrested a 29-year-old Arvin man on multiple felony charges, including kidnapping and aggravated sexual assault of a minor, 23ABC reports. Antonio Rafael Gomez Martinez was arrested Sept. 14 and booked into the Lerdo Pre-Trial Facility without bail, with a court appearance scheduled for Nov. 3. Police say an 11-year-old Bakersfield girl was abducted in early September near the area of MLK Park and Union, then dropped off near her home the following day. Detective Bijan Gharib said surveillance footage and Flock camera data helped identify the suspect's vehicle. It's a case that has shaken the neighborhood, and one that shows how camera networks are increasingly central to local investigations.

KGET 17 reports that 71 years after his death, the "James Dean Memorial Highway" is now official. The designation honors the actor whose brief, blazing career made him a permanent fixture of American film — and whose story is woven into California's cultural memory. For Kern County, where Dean's legacy still draws visitors and film buffs, the highway marker is a small but lasting tribute.

Bakersfield police are searching for a woman accused of breaking into the Salvation Army, according to Bakersfield Now. The investigation is ongoing, and anyone with information should contact the department. Nonprofits like the Salvation Army serve some of the county's most vulnerable residents, so a break-in there hits the community twice — once in lost resources and once in the sense of security for the people who rely on it.

Something good

The Norris School District is set to build a new elementary school in Shafter, a project that marks a real step forward in expanding local school capacity. Shafter has been growing, and new classrooms mean fewer crowded campuses and shorter commutes for families. It's the kind of quiet, unglamorous investment that pays off for decades — and it's worth a smile this morning.

Coming up this week

The Bakersfield City Council meets twice on Wednesday, October 7 — first at 3:30 p.m. and again at 5:15 p.m. The Riverview Marketplace environmental impact report is expected to be part of the council's business, so if you have thoughts on that project, Wednesday is the day to show up or send a comment. Both sessions are open to the public.

Also on the calendar: the Housing and Community Development Committee meets Thursday, October 8 at noon, and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets Friday, October 9 at noon. These are the smaller, less crowded meetings where a lot of the groundwork gets done — housing policy and neighborhood safety both shape daily life in Bakersfield, and public input carries real weight at this level.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" screens Monday, October 5. The NB RIDAZ "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour rolls in Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." takes over the Fox on Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands Saturday, October 17. If you've been meaning to catch a show downtown, October is the month.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Saturday, October 3, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. Saturday, October 3, 2026, and the day's top story is a pair of police chases that kept officers moving before dawn — one ending in a crash on South Union Avenue and a foot search through backyards. It's 73 degrees at Meadows Field right now, headed for a high near 100, with no active weather alerts for Kern County.

The Kern Overnight

Two police chases kept officers busy before dawn, one of them ending in a crash on South Union Avenue and a foot search through backyards, and a stabbing sent deputies to Oildale's Linda Vista area. A carnival drew a run of missing-child calls and a fight, crews handled vehicle fires on the southwest side, and a man was reported throwing knives and striking a relative with a bat at a home on Oregon Street. The rest of the log was medical aids, alarms and traffic checks.

Just after midnight a silver sedan reported at about 80 mph on southbound Highway 99 led officers onto city streets. The driver turned south on South H Street, went east on McKee Road and hit a dead end just east of Highway 99, made a U-turn, then crashed into the median on South Union Avenue near the 7500 block. He ran west along a fence line into a residential block near Acoma Way, and a sheriff's air unit followed him over backyards near Lazy River Drive before losing sight of him behind a home. Officers set a perimeter and worked through the yards.

At 12:38 a.m. a traffic stop on westbound Niles Street turned into a chase when a vehicle reported to be carrying at least five people took off. It ran east on Pioneer Drive through a red light at Fairfax Road, turned north on Meadows, and ended near the 4900 block of Pioneer Drive, where the occupants jumped a fence and ran. Officers detained three people and reported one still outstanding.

At 11:27 p.m. officers were sent to an apartment on the 3900 block of Oregon Street after a caller reported her brother was having a mental breakdown, was throwing knives around, and had hit another relative with a baseball bat. A verbal argument could be heard in the background and the call drew a heavy police and fire response. At 9:06 p.m. deputies were sent to the Linda Vista area for a stabbing; the caller reported a man had stab wounds to his arm and that the man's girlfriend was with him, and a suspect was reported leaving in a white Chevrolet Silverado.

Through the evening a carnival drew a run of missing-child reports. A 3-year-old girl in a Dodgers jersey was reported missing and found at the main gate, a 9-year-old boy was missing for about 15 minutes before he was located, a 2-year-old was reported missing before being found, and an 8-year-old girl was reported missing later in the night. Officers also handled a fight between two groups of women at the Ferris wheel. Crews were sent to a report of multiple vehicles burning at Playfair Road and Ashe Road around 9:35 p.m., and employees and security reported a man attempted to take merchandise in the Chester Avenue area just after 10 p.m.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 100° and a low around 71° tonight. It's currently 73° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. We don't have an air quality reading or active fire information to pass along this morning, so if you're headed out for yard work or a long walk, plan around the heat and check conditions before you go. Triple digits in October are nothing new here, but they still ask something of you — water, shade, and a little patience with the afternoon.

Top stories

Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a man who allegedly broke into Howard's Mini Mart through the roof. That's the account from the department's own release, and it's the kind of detail that sticks with you — a break-in from above rather than through a door or window. Investigators are asking the public to keep an eye out as they work to identify him.

According to 23ABC, the victims of the deadly helicopter crash off Catalina Island have been identified. REACH Air Medical Services says pilot Steven "Steve" Robinson and flight nurse Jessica deVries died when a medical helicopter went down in the Catalina waters shortly after takeoff on Sept. 30. The flight was carrying a patient, Catalina Hernandez, to the mainland for emergency care; her body was recovered after she had gone missing. Another flight nurse, Brad Sparks, continues his recovery, and Hernandez's son, who was on the flight, survived. Pacific Region President Sean Russell said the tragedy "has touched every corner of our organization."

KGET 17 reports that a man faces life in prison after killing his wife, in a case where loved ones remembered that "they were all here every day." The story centers on a family's loss and the sentence now hanging over the man convicted in it — a reminder of how much weight a courtroom carries for the people left behind.

KGET 17 also reports that two Garces football stars are ineligible for Friday's game, with the status of the team's wins still up in the air. For a program and a fan base that follow every snap, that leaves real questions about the season's record and what comes next. We'll be watching for the eligibility decision to sort itself out.

23ABC spoke with criminal law attorney Jared Thompson about what California would require in a case like the one drawing national attention at Cornell University. A former Cornell student says she was drugged and sexually assaulted by fraternity members in 2024; the men accused deny wrongdoing, no criminal charges have been filed, and New York Attorney General Letitia James has been appointed special prosecutor as the case returns to criminal review. Thompson explained that California's threshold goes well beyond whether someone had been drinking — prosecutors must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that a person was so intoxicated they didn't understand the nature of the act or its consequences, and that the accused knew or reasonably should have known the other party could not consent. California does not require a survivor to have been unconscious or physically unable to speak.

KGET 17 reports that prosecutor Pedro Naveiras is making public safety the centerpiece of his bid for Bakersfield's third ward. It's a city council race where the pitch is straightforward: a career prosecutor arguing that his courtroom experience is what the ward needs. Voters in the third ward will weigh that against whatever their own priorities are when ballots arrive.

23ABC reports that Seth Griffith is back for his seventh season with the Bakersfield Condors, still chasing a Calder Cup. The captain has worn the "C," helped bring younger players along, and watched teammates graduate to the Edmonton Oilers — but the one box unchecked is a championship. "I haven't won a Calder Cup," Griffith said, pointing to how much fun the Marlies had celebrating last year. He talks about running the room like an NHL dressing room and making sure every player understands his role, which matters in the AHL, where call-ups and injuries churned through nearly 40 players last season. The Condors open the 2026-27 season this weekend in Henderson, Nevada, with four straight road games to start.

Something good

Seth Griffith's seventh season in Condorstown is worth a smile on its own. A captain who keeps showing up, keeps teaching, and keeps chasing the one trophy that's eluded him gives local hockey fans another winter of professional hockey to look forward to — and gives the younger guys in that locker room someone to learn from. Here's hoping this is the year.

Coming up this week

The week ahead is busy on the civic side. The Special Youth Commission meets this morning, Saturday, October 3, at 9:00 a.m. The Youth Commission holds its regular meeting Monday, October 5, at 4:30 p.m. Wednesday, October 7, is the heavy day: the Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 a.m., City Council Meeting 330 convenes at 3:30 p.m., and City Council Meeting 515 follows at 5:15 p.m. Then Thursday, October 8, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon, and Friday, October 9, the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at noon. If you've got a question about housing, neighborhood safety, or city business, this is the week to show up and be heard.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" screens Monday, October 5. NB RIDAZ brings the "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour" to the Fox on Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." lands Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour takes the stage Saturday, October 17. The Fox's Cults & Classics season pass for 2026-2027 is also on sale now if you'd rather plan the whole year at once.

Have a good Saturday, Bakersfield. Drink water, check on your neighbors, and we'll see you tomorrow.
