content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Sunday, October 4, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. The fair has packed up for another year, and the closing night kept officers busy — a gunfire report that turned out to be a big fight, three missing-child calls, and a handful of other incidents across the county. Today brings more heat: a high near 103 under clear skies, no weather alerts, and no active fires reported in Kern County.

The Kern Overnight

The Kern County Fair closed out its run Saturday night, and the midway kept officers moving into the early hours. At 9:52 p.m., officers were sent to the carnival's amusement area on a report of shots fired, with a caller telling dispatchers people were running. The response grew quickly, but within minutes units advised there had been no gunfire at all — it was a large disturbance. Several people were seen running from the carnival area, though officers could not locate anyone involved. About 25 minutes later, officers were called to a fight in the carnival's north corner. In that same window, three missing-child calls came in: a 13-year-old girl last seen near the Bud Pavilion stage, a 2-year-old girl at the carousel, and an 11-year-old boy near the Ferris wheel.

Elsewhere, a just-occurred assault on Edwards Avenue in the metro area left a victim unconscious but breathing, and a teen girl in a red jacket and blue jeans was seen running from the scene; the victim was later conscious and talking with officers. Just after midnight, a hit-and-run on South 8th Street in south Bakersfield left officers looking for a silver Honda last seen heading west on Highway 58 from Allen Road. At 12:55 a.m., crews found a single vehicle fully engulfed in flames off the southbound side of Highway 99 north of Kimberlina Road — the occupant was already out and conscious. And at 4:45 a.m., crews responded to a rollover at Edison Highway and Tower Line; on arrival they found no ejection, with two people out of the vehicle and breathing. The rest of the log was medical aids, alarms, and traffic checks.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 103 degrees today, with a low around 71 tonight. It's currently 75 degrees at Meadows Field. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are reported. Air quality readings were not available this morning. If you're headed out, plan around the heat — the valley's October warm spells are no joke, and the afternoon will be the hottest stretch of the day.

Top stories

23ABC reports that a 14-year-old girl was injured in a collision between her electric scooter and a vehicle in Arvin on Thursday evening, and the crash lands alongside new national data showing e-scooter injuries among children are surging. Arvin police say the girl was riding near the CVS on Bear Mountain Boulevard around 6:40 p.m. when the crash happened; she was taken to the hospital with minor, non-life-threatening injuries. An analysis of federal injury data by E-Ride Hero estimates nearly 29,000 children aged 14 and younger were hurt in e-scooter incidents in 2025 — a 64 percent increase from 2024 and an increase of nearly 700 percent since 2020. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Joshua Deutinger told the station that as e-scooters grow in popularity, officers are seeing more crashes involving them, and he reminded parents that under California law riders need a valid driver's license to operate an e-scooter on the street, and that kids shouldn't be riding them on roadways posted above 25 miles per hour.

According to KGET 17, a man faces life in prison after being convicted of killing his wife, with a courtroom account describing a household that neighbors and family say was marked by daily presence and, ultimately, violence. The station's coverage centers on the trial's closing chapter and the sentence now hanging over the defendant. For Kern County readers, the case is a reminder of how domestic violence cases move through our courts and what life terms actually mean in practice.

KGET 17 also reports that two Garces Memorial football stars have been ruled ineligible for Friday's game, leaving the status of the team's wins up in the air. The eligibility question touches the season's record and could ripple through league standings depending on how the section rules. We'll be watching for the next step from the school and the governing body.

Bakersfield Now reports that a Highland High student was arrested after ammunition was found in a classroom, with additional rounds later seized. The discovery prompted a police response at the school, and the student now faces the legal consequences. It's the kind of morning-after story that has parents talking, and it's a reminder that campus safety protocols get tested in real time.

23ABC has identified the victims of the deadly medical helicopter crash off Catalina Island that killed three people. REACH Air Medical Services says pilot Steven "Steve" Robinson and flight nurse Jessica deVries died after the helicopter went down in the water shortly after takeoff on Sept. 30. The patient being transported, Catalina Hernandez, was also killed; her son, who was aboard, survived. Another flight nurse, Brad Sparks, continues his recovery. The crash happened well outside Kern County, but the crew's work is part of the same medical-transport network that serves communities across our region, and the loss has been felt across California's air-medical community.

KGET 17 notes that viewers can watch the David Valadao and Randy Villegas debate — a matchup in one of the state's most closely watched congressional races. For Kern County voters, the debate is a chance to hear the candidates directly on the issues that shape the valley, from water to agriculture to immigration. Details on how to watch are available through the station.

Something good

A Bakersfield nonprofit is connecting community members with people held in immigration detention through pen pal letters. Wilma Goodloe spent Saturday morning at First Congregational Church joining a letter-writing session hosted by Kern Welcoming and Extending Solidarity to Immigrants, known as KWESI. Her pen pal is a 33-year-old man from Honduras she's been writing to for nearly a year — he was held at Golden State Annex in McFarland before being transferred to Texas, and he recently donated artwork for a KWESI fundraiser. KWESI Coordinator Jeannie Parent said the group visits people in detention and maintains a commissary fund, which is how it gathers names. One letter writer told the group there's nothing like the feeling of hearing your name called in the dorm and learning you have mail.

Coming up this week

The week ahead brings a full slate of public meetings and a few nights out. The Youth Commission meets Monday, October 5, at 4:30 p.m. On Wednesday, October 7, the Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 a.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. The Housing and Community Development Committee meets Thursday, October 8, at noon, and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets Friday, October 9, at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch. "Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein" screens Monday, October 5. NB RIDAZ brings the "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour" on Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. "United We Dance: Festival Energy. All Night." lands Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour comes through Saturday, October 17. The Fox also has a Cults & Classics season pass on sale for the 2026–2027 season.

Stay cool out there today, and if you're out early, give yourself a little extra time on the roads.

summary: The fair has packed up and the week is underway, but the heat is staying put — we're looking at a high near…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Monday, October 5, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. The fair has packed up and the week is underway, but the heat is staying put — we're looking at a high near 101 today with moderate air quality and no active weather alerts. The top story this morning is a big change on the local gym scene: Body Xchange has been acquired by Planet Fitness, and its Bakersfield locations are closing. Also overnight, a pursuit south of town ended in a foot chase and a K9 search near Cottonwood Road and White Lane.

The Kern Overnight

A vehicle that failed to stop drew a pursuit shortly before 11 p.m. that ran south on Wible Road past Panama Lane at speeds around 40 mph. Traffic was light, and officers held off on any pursuit-intervention attempt as the driver headed toward a dead end. The chase turned into a foot pursuit, with air support overhead and a K9 track leading into a rural property of shacks and horse pens between Cottonwood Road and White Lane. A subject was seen going into a mobile home on East Panama Lane, and the K9 made contact with a person at the front gate behind a parked truck as officers swept the property through the midnight hour.

Elsewhere, crews were sent at 12:31 a.m. to a single-story commercial building in the 1300 block of Kern Street for smoke in the bathroom ventilation of a mechanics warehouse. Engine 21 found light smoke showing and took command of a minor incident, with workers already on scene. At 2:06 a.m., crews responded to a recycling facility in the 2600 block of South Mount Vernon Avenue for a reported brush fire and found a large fire in the compost area, roughly 10 by 20 feet. They called the facility to bring in tractors and employees, dumped the water they had, and Engine 41 stayed until staff arrived to take over.

Just before 10 p.m., someone tried to strong-arm a person outside a fast-food restaurant in the 2400 block of North Chester Avenue. The suspect, in a blue shirt and blue jeans, fled on foot. At 10:42 p.m., a semi-truck with a black bed full of hay was taken from the 900 block of South MLK Boulevard; the reporting party tracked it heading south on Cottonwood Road near White Lane. Traffic units also spent the evening on a four-vehicle crash on Mount Vernon Avenue, a pedestrian struck in a three-vehicle crash on Riverlakes, and a hit-and-run at South P Street and Bell Terrace. The rest of the log was alarms, medical aids and disturbances.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 101 degrees and a low around 71 tonight. It's currently 77 at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality sits at 66 — moderate, so most folks can go about their day, though sensitive groups may want to take it a little easier during the hottest hours. No active fires are being reported. If you're working outside today, the usual advice holds: water early, shade when you can, and keep an eye on neighbors who live alone.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Body Xchange has been acquired by Planet Fitness, and the gym chain's Bakersfield locations are closing. The change means members who have been working out at Body Xchange clubs around town will need to find a new place to train, and it marks the departure of a local fitness brand in favor of a national one. If you hold a membership, it's worth checking on the status of your plan and what happens to any prepaid time.

According to 23ABC, Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders drew a large crowd Sunday night inside Harvey Auditorium at Bakersfield High School as part of a three-day tour through California. The stop was in support of Randy Villegas, the Democratic challenger running against Republican Congressman David Valadao in California's 22nd Congressional District. Sanders called on voters to back progressive candidates, and healthcare dominated the night — both men criticized Valadao over his 2025 vote for President Trump's "Big Beautiful Bill," which is projected to cut federal spending on Medicaid and other health programs by more than $1 trillion over a decade. Sanders pointed to the district's high share of Medicaid recipients, while Valadao has previously said his vote preserves the program for its intended recipients — children, pregnant women, the disabled and the elderly — and reflects the district's priorities.

KGET 17 also reports that the Supreme Court is set to hear a case Monday on whether localities can sue oil companies for climate damages. The outcome matters well beyond the courtroom, and it matters here in particular: Kern County is one of the state's largest oil-producing regions, so any ruling on how far cities and counties can reach in climate litigation could ripple through local budgets, industry operations and the legal landscape that surrounds them.

23ABC tells us that a 14-year-old girl was injured Thursday when her electric scooter collided with a vehicle in Arvin, near the CVS on Bear Mountain Boulevard. Police say her injuries were minor and not life-threatening, but the crash lands alongside new national data showing e-scooter injuries among children are surging — an analysis of federal injury data by E-Ride Hero estimates nearly 29,000 kids aged 14 and younger were hurt in 2025, up 64% from 2024 and nearly 700% since 2020. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Joshua Deutinger said officers are seeing more e-scooter crashes as the devices grow in popularity, and he reminded riders that they still have to follow the rules of the road, stay in bike lanes, and hold a valid driver's license to operate on the street. Kids, he said, shouldn't be riding them on roadways posted above 25 mph at all.

Bakersfield Now reports that a man has been convicted in the deadly stabbing of the mother of his children here in Bakersfield. The conviction closes a chapter in a case that has weighed on the families involved and on the neighborhoods around it, and it now moves toward sentencing.

Something good

The Kern County Fair wrapped up Sunday, and the heat didn't keep families away. Erin Sceales told 23ABC she was excited to be back after four or five years away — "It's the hottest day, of course. But we're excited" — and she loved that the fair lets her older kids split off with friends while she and the little ones hit the kiddie rides. Phelicia Palmer came on the final day with her grandchildren, the baby enjoying his first fair and his sister her second. "You're never too old," she said. That's a good note to end the season on.

Coming up this week

It's a full week of public meetings, so if you've got something on your mind, there's a room for it. The Youth Commission meets today, Monday, October 5, at 4:30 p.m. Tuesday brings the Police Civil Service Commission at 8:30 a.m. Wednesday is the busy one: City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m., followed by City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. On Thursday, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon, and Friday the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee gathers at noon as well. Looking a little further out, the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets Monday, October 12, at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a run of shows lined up. Tonight, Monday, October 5, it's Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein. Friday, October 9, brings the NB RIDAZ: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. United We Dance: Festival Energy takes the stage Friday, October 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour comes through Saturday, October 17. If you're already thinking ahead to next season, the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027 is also on sale.

Have a good Monday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there.

summary: It's Tuesday, October 6, and the story leading the day is a big one for Arvin High School — its Ballet…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Tuesday, October 6, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Tuesday, October 6, and the story leading the day is a big one for Arvin High School — its Ballet Folklorico program is getting a new dance studio nearly three times the size of its current room. Outside, expect a hot one: a high near 99°, a low around 70° tonight, moderate air quality, and no active weather alerts or fires for Kern County.

The Kern Overnight

Deputies had a busy night across the county, starting with a burglary on Breckenridge Road that ended with a homeowner holding a suspect at gunpoint. According to the Sheriff's Office log, the resident called dispatchers shortly before 11 p.m. to report he had the suspect detained after an earlier break-in at the home. A second suspect ran to a black GMC and left westbound on Breckenridge Road; a neighbor told deputies the truck had turned south on Comanche Drive. Units staged at Breckenridge and Comanche while a patrol car followed the vehicle westbound at normal speeds, and the search through the Comanche Drive foothills carried past midnight before the truck was reported heading south out of the area.

Elsewhere, traffic units were sent at 9:49 p.m. after roughly 50 vehicles moving eastbound on Westside Parkway approaching Calloway Drive. Officers were asked to identify anyone involved and to check Coffee Road at the parkway as the group split, with part of it reported heading toward the Truxtun Avenue off-ramp and Highway 99. Departments were advised to keep units free while the group was tracked through the area.

Fire and medical crews answered several calls overnight. At 9:55 p.m., crews were told a crash had started as a vehicle versus a tree before the vehicle went down into a ravine and came to rest with power lines down nearby; the occupants were out of the vehicle and were reported possibly trying to reach the water, and a second vehicle was reported down at the riverbank a short time later. At 4:28 a.m., a three-vehicle collision was reported in front of a business in the 1100 block of East Truxtun Avenue, with a dark-colored SUV involved and a possible pin-in. Engine 2 and Rescue 2 were on scene and reported the driver out of the vehicle with minor to moderate injuries. At 4:19 a.m., a woman whispering on the phone told dispatchers she was locked inside a car parked in front of a home in the 2500 block of Ledgeview Lane.

Deputies also worked a hit-and-run whose driver ran off on foot, an assault where a man showed a pistol and fled in an SUV, alarms at a District Boulevard business and a Truxtun Avenue building, and a string of medical aids. The rest of the log was disturbances, welfare checks and a handful of fights.

Today's weather

It's currently 75° at Meadows Field (KBFL), on the way to a high near 99° and a low around 70° tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are reported. Air quality is 65 — moderate — so sensitive groups may want to take it easy during the hottest part of the afternoon. If you're out and about, plan for a genuinely hot October day: shade, water, and a break during the peak hours will go a long way.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that school book bans hit a record high, with a new study finding nearly 12,000 removals. The figure marks the highest number recorded since researchers began tracking the trend, and it lands as districts across the country — including here in Kern County — continue to weigh which titles belong on library shelves. The study's findings add fresh data to a debate that has played out at local school board meetings for the past several years, with parents and educators on both sides pressing their case.

According to 23ABC, Arvin High School's Ballet Folklorico program is getting a new dance studio nearly three times bigger than the space students use now. Teacher Brenda Ruiz told the station the program started with just five students and has grown popular enough that space has become a problem — about 20 students fit in the current room, so the group has to split into smaller sessions. Principal Gabriel Ramirez-Leyva said talks about a larger classroom began last year because of the room's capacity, and the program currently keeps a wait list. The new facility will include dressing rooms, a laundry room and more storage for costumes and shoes. Students got their first look at the room Monday afternoon; senior Noemi Lopez Gonzalez said she can't wait for the remodeling to be finished.

KGET 17 reports that President Trump has approved death by firing squad for the convicted Fort Hood shooter. The decision concerns one of the most closely watched military cases in recent memory and is drawing national attention to how the sentence will be carried out. We'll keep an eye on any local reaction in the days ahead.

KGET 17 also reports that televangelist Jim Bakker, who built the "PTL Club" empire with Tammy Faye Bakker, has died at 86. Bakker's ministry and later legal troubles made him a fixture of American religious broadcasting for decades, and his death closes a long chapter in that world.

23ABC reports that President Donald Trump drew criticism from California politicians after remarks about Los Angeles and San Diego during a rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, on Monday. Trump suggested Iran could "take out" the two cities, calling it "a very small price to pay." San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria responded that his city is "not collateral damage" and "not expendable," while Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said on X that the president's statements are dangerous and could compromise safety. Governor Gavin Newsom called the remarks "deranged and dangerous."

According to 23ABC, calls for the release of former Bakersfield resident and Air Force veteran Travis Leake from Russian detention have been renewed as his mother demonstrates in Washington, D.C. Leake has been held in Russia since June 2023 and is serving a 13-year sentence in a penal colony after being accused of possessing and selling drugs. His mother, Garcia, traveled to the capital Monday hoping to speak with the Trump administration, saying the court records showed no real evidence against her son. Advocate Jon Franks noted that Leake has now been left behind in three successive deals, and in a recorded call Leake said his government has done "absolutely nothing" to help him.

Bakersfield Now reports that Planet Fitness has acquired Bakersfield's Body Xchange Health Club locations. The deal reshapes the local gym landscape and means members at those clubs will see the Planet Fitness brand and format going forward. We'll share more details on what it means for memberships as they become available.

Something good

Arvin High's Ballet Folklorico dancers have something real to celebrate this week. The program that began with five students is getting a dedicated studio nearly three times the size of its current room, complete with dressing rooms, a laundry room and proper storage for costumes and shoes. Students saw the space for the first time Monday, and senior Noemi Lopez Gonzalez summed it up best — looking at the room, she said, it's exciting to know this will be their future practice place.

Coming up this week

It's a full week of public meetings at Bakersfield City Hall. Wednesday, October 7, starts early with the Police Civil Service Commission at 8:30 a.m. and a special session of the same commission at 8:45 a.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. On Thursday, October 8, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon, and Friday, October 9, brings the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee, also at noon. Looking ahead to next week, the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets Monday, October 12, at noon, and the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets Tuesday, October 13, at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a run of shows lined up. NB RIDAZ brings the "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. United We Dance takes the stage Friday, October 16, with the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour on Saturday, October 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour closing out the stretch on Sunday, October 18. The Fox is also selling season passes for its Cults & Classics series.

Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there.

headline: Woman who said she was set on fire at Oildale homeless encampment dies months after suffering severe burns
summary: Good Wednesday morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a hard one: a 33-year-old Oildale woman who…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Wednesday, October 7, 2026

Good Wednesday morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a hard one: a 33-year-old Oildale woman who told 23ABC she was set on fire at a homeless encampment has died, and her family is still waiting on answers from the coroner. It's going to be a hot one — a high near 100° — with moderate air quality and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County. Here's what happened while you slept.

The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came just after 2 a.m., when crews were sent to a vehicle-versus-pedestrian crash on southbound Highway 99 just north of Lerdo Highway. A vehicle was reported facing the wrong way in the freeway, and as units responded, dispatchers learned three vehicles were involved and two people were hurt — one of them a pedestrian who was struck. That upgraded the call to a rescue. The pedestrian was reported down in the number one lane and possibly in grave condition, and a second unit passing the scene about half a mile into the southbound lanes reported several vehicles involved.

Elsewhere in east Kern County, a single vehicle landed on its roof on Highway 14, and a Mercy Air helicopter was placed on standby. Crews found one patient who was not pinned but had limited access, so they began an extrication; the air ambulance was later stood down. Fire crews also answered smoke at the back of a commercial building in the 2100 block of Niles Street — a structure that had burned before — and found smoke at the rear on arrival.

A car and a semi collided near East Bear Mountain Boulevard, with all occupants reported out of the vehicles, the car blocking traffic and one patient transported. On southbound Highway 99 south of Highway 166, a semi went into a guardrail with heavy smoke visible, hung up on the rail for about 50 feet; Caltrans was asked to respond to the road hazard. The rest of the log was the usual overnight mix: a domestic disturbance on Gold Dust Drive, a semi with brakes on fire northbound on Interstate 5 north of the Grapevine whose driver pulled into the scales, an animal bite on East Roberts Lane, and a handful of medical aids, alarms and welfare checks across the county.

Today's weather

It's currently 75° at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 100° this afternoon and a low around 70° tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires reported. Air quality sits at 71 on the index — moderate — so if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's a day to keep an eye on how you're feeling during the hottest hours. Otherwise, expect a classic early-October valley scorcher: hot, dry and still. Drink more water than you think you need, and don't leave anyone in a parked car.

Top stories

23ABC reports that Frances Lopez, the 33-year-old woman who told the station last week she was set on fire at a homeless encampment in Oildale, has died. Lopez spent nearly two months in a Fresno burn unit recovering from burns covering more than 30% of her body, undergoing multiple surgeries and needing daily care after she left the hospital. Her husband, Steven, said the couple had been together 13 years and were raising two daughters; her grandparents visited every weekend while she was treated. The Kern County Sheriff's Office told 23ABC it is awaiting the coroner's report to determine her cause of death, and the family says a full autopsy could take about three weeks. Her loved ones believe an infection, possibly sepsis, related to her injuries may have played a role, but that has not been confirmed.

According to KGET 17, State Sen. Ben Allen brought his campaign for California's insurance commissioner to Bakersfield, telling the station the Central Valley is "vital" and needs to be part of the conversation. Allen, an attorney who represents parts of the Los Angeles coast, is running in November against former San Francisco supervisor and attorney Jane Kim. The commissioner's office regulates insurance rates, licenses companies and agents, investigates fraud and enforces consumer protection laws — all subjects that land squarely on Kern County homeowners, drivers and farmers. 23ABC also sat down with both candidates; Kim told the station she wants the state to take a bigger stake in the insurance market, pitching a public nonprofit disaster insurance program for every California homeowner.

23ABC reports that Cal State Bakersfield has hired Andy Fiske, most recently of Sacramento State, as its new director of athletics — stepping into one of the most legally turbulent chapters in the department's recent history. Two former softball players have sued CSUB and a former assistant coach alleging harassment; former Athletic Director Kyle Conder filed a separate suit alleging retaliation and defamation, claims the university denies; and former assistant basketball coach Kevin Mays pleaded no contest to pimping, possession of child pornography and drug possession while armed, and was sentenced to four years in prison. At a press conference, Fiske said challenges should be faced directly and mistakes acknowledged and learned from, and that his first 90 to 100 days will focus on listening. Asked what accountability athletes should see from him, he pointed to reporting structures he has used at previous institutions and said he'd find out whether similar avenues exist here. KGET 17 also covered the hire, noting the university's aim to change the culture of the program.

KGET 17 reports that the death of a 14-year-old Oildale girl has sparked an outpouring of community support. That's the extent of what we can tell you from the headline alone this morning; we'll bring you more as details are confirmed.

Bakersfield Now reports that a CHP crackdown on Interstate 5 ended with two vehicles impounded and multiple citations issued to trucks. Commercial enforcement sweeps like this one target equipment, weight and safety violations on one of the busiest freight corridors in the state — the kind of enforcement that matters in a county where I-5 traffic and truck safety are a daily concern for everyone sharing the road.

Something good

CSUB has hired Andy Fiske as its new athletic director, and the university is framing the move as a fresh chapter for Bakersfield's hometown university and its student-athletes. It's a hard moment to step into, and Fiske's stated first move — listening — is the right one. Here's hoping the Roadrunners get the steady, accountable leadership they deserve, on the field and off.

Coming up this week

City business gets moving early today. The Police Civil Service Commission meets at 8:30 this morning, followed by a special Police Civil Service Commission meeting at 8:45, and the City Council takes up Meeting 330 at 3:30 this afternoon. On Thursday, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon. Friday brings the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee at noon — a good room for anyone who cares about the litter, blight and cleanup work that shapes how our neighborhoods look.

Next week opens with a pair of Monday meetings: a Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee session at noon and the Fire Civil Service Commission at 3 p.m. On Tuesday, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon — the place to be if you have thoughts on bike lanes, crosswalks or how traffic moves through town.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch ahead: the NB RIDAZ "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour lands Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. Later in the month, United We Dance brings an all-night festival energy to the Fox on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour stops in October 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour closes out the run on October 18. Season passes for Cults & Classics 2026–2027 are also on sale now.

Have a good Wednesday, and stay cool out there.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Thursday, October 8, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Thursday, October 8, and the day's biggest story is the Kern River case that reached the California Supreme Court this week, where justices heard arguments over how the state balances fish and water supplies. Expect another hot one — a high near 100 degrees, moderate air quality, and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County this morning.

The Kern Overnight

Firefighters spent the small hours at the old Silver Saddle Ranch & Club in California City, where a second-alarm fire broke out just after 12:30 a.m. at the two-story hotel resort. Crews arrived to find three buildings fully involved, an exposure threatened to the east, and four spot fires in vegetation to the south backing into the wind. The only hydrant on scene was dead, so a water tender was called in along with support from Edwards. Firefighters kept the flames out of the main exposure and turned their attention to a smaller on-site building, while roughly an acre to an acre and a half of grass and brush burned around the complex. The initial fire buildings were reported 100 percent involved, and crews settled in for an extensive mop-up as light southwest winds turned erratic on one side of the fire.

Elsewhere, a semi caught fire on Interstate 5 near Copus Road, south of the Grapevine, with the trailer still attached. Crews reported the fire near the wheel wells before the whole trailer went up in heavy smoke, blocking lanes and routing traffic off the freeway onto Highway 99 while heavy towing was called in. One lane was expected to reopen within about ten minutes, and the ambulance was cancelled with no one hurt.

In south Bakersfield, a hysterical caller reported that two men and a woman forced entry through the front door of an apartment in the 7000 block of Di Giorgio Road. Officers searched the unit and the surrounding area while medics staged nearby. Deputies also were sent to the North Edwards area for a man in a black shirt and gray sweatpants standing in the middle of a roadway with a large firearm, possibly a rifle or shotgun; the caller, who was picking up juveniles from a school event, told dispatchers she left with them and filed a report. And a caller reported a man in an orange Chevrolet pickup dragging a woman from a residence in the 1800 block of Pacific Street, with the woman heard yelling as she was put into the truck before the vehicle left the area. The rest of the night was crashes, disturbances, alarms and medical aids.

Today's weather

It's 79 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 100 and a low around 69 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and there are no active fires reported. Air quality sits at 83, which is moderate — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's a reasonable day to keep the strenuous outdoor work to the cooler hours. With the valley running this hot in October, keep the water handy and check on neighbors who work outside.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Ridgecrest's police chief says the city is amending its Flock camera contract in response to resident pushback and concerns. The license-plate-reading cameras have drawn questions from residents about privacy and how the data is stored and shared, and the city is now reworking the terms of its agreement rather than leaving it as written. It's a local version of a debate playing out across California, and it matters here because Ridgecrest is far from the nearest big-city police force — the cameras are part of how a smaller department stretches its coverage.

According to KGET 17, a vanload of Central Valley farm workers was reportedly picked up by ICE. Details remain limited, but the report lands in the middle of a harvest season that depends on this workforce, and it's the kind of thing that ripples through families and employers well beyond the people directly involved. We'll keep watching for more information as it comes.

KGET 17 also reports that the Bakersfield City Council approved an $8 million contract for energy savings construction at the Water Resources building. The work is pitched as efficiency upgrades that pay for themselves over time, and the council's vote moves it from proposal to project. For ratepayers, the practical question is whether the savings show up where they should — in the cost of running the department.

23ABC reports that the California Supreme Court heard arguments Wednesday in Bring Back the Kern v. City of Bakersfield, a case that could reshape how the state balances protecting fish in the Kern River with other water needs. The dispute centers on a state law requiring enough water below dams to keep fish in good condition; in 2023 a judge ordered Bakersfield to keep water flowing in the river, the city and several agricultural water districts challenged that order, and an appeals court overturned the original ruling, sending the matter to the state's highest court. The city declined to comment on active litigation, and the City Attorney's Office did not respond to 23ABC's request. As arguments unfolded, Bring Back the Kern hosted a watch party at Dagny's Coffee Co. so residents could follow along together. Gary Bray, president of the Kern River Fly Fishing Club, told 23ABC there has to be a way to allow water for drinking, for communities and for agriculture — "we need both." Isabel Stierle, a retired Bakersfield College biology professor, said how we treat the natural setting reflects how we treat each other, and that we need to think about keeping things alive and keeping the river flowing.

23ABC reports that a $2 million state investment is bringing a new resource center closer to opening for Delano farmworkers. Senator Melissa Hurtado secured the funding for the California Farmworker Foundation, capping a two-year effort that organizers first unveiled in June. The center is meant to be a central hub where farmworker families can reach healthcare and support services more easily. Foundation CEO Darrell Muniz described it as a safe and trusted place where farmworkers feel seen, heard and empowered — where a mother can get care for her family, a father can learn a skill, and a child can believe they can do anything. Farmer Melvin Archila, a member of the foundation's Agricultural Work Advisory Council, said the foundation has opened doors for him in his work and his leadership.

23ABC reports that two courthouse break-ins are under investigation in Bakersfield, and a 20-year-old man is in custody after allegedly forcing his way into the Kern County Superior Courthouse. Keenean Miranda was arrested after allegedly making his way to the sixth floor, where officials apprehended him; he faces four counts, including assault with a deadly weapon and first- and second-degree burglary. A separate break-in on Sept. 23 targeted the office of Kern County Superior Court Judge David Zulfa — police have not confirmed whether anything was taken, and no arrests have been announced in that case. Bakersfield Police Sergeant Keith Schlecht told 23ABC the courthouse incidents are among nine offenses downtown, ranging from simple vandalism to burglaries where entry was made and theft committed, with six suspects identified and five arrests made.

Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a man accused of using a stolen credit card for more than $1,000 in purchases. Investigators are asking the public to help identify him. If you think you recognize something, call BPD's non-emergency line rather than the newsroom — and never post a name or plate on social media.

Something good

The Kern County Veterans Stand Down returns for its annual event at Stramler Park, offering support and services to local veterans. It's one of those gatherings where the paperwork, the health checks and the conversation all happen in one place, and volunteers show up year after year to make it work. If you know a veteran who could use a hand, this is a good week to pass the word along.

Coming up this week

Today, Thursday, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon. Friday brings two noon meetings — the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee — so if you've had thoughts about a blighted lot or a neighborhood concern, that's your window.

Monday is busy: the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at noon, and the Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3 p.m. Tuesday, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon — a good room for anyone with opinions about bike lanes, crosswalks or traffic calming. Wednesday, the Water Board meets at 10 a.m., which lands just days after the Kern River arguments in Sacramento, so expect the case to come up. The Planning Commission meets Thursday, Oct. 15, at 5:30 p.m.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has NB RIDAZ: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off on Friday, FANTASIAS on Saturday, United We Dance on Oct. 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour on Oct. 17, and Fortune Feimster's Taking Care of Biscuits comedy tour on Oct. 18. Have a good Thursday, and stay cool out there.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Friday, October 9, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Friday, October 9, and the top story is a shooting in southwest Bakersfield that sent two people to the hospital and drew a heavy police and fire response to a Pembroke Avenue block just after 1 a.m. Expect a hot one — a high near 97 under clear skies, air quality in the moderate range, and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County. Here's what happened while you slept.

The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came just after 1:20 a.m., when officers and firefighters were sent to a residence in the 5400 block of Pembroke Avenue in southwest Bakersfield for a report of a shooting. Crews arrived to find two patients with gunshot wounds and quickly set up a perimeter around the block, holding family members back while units moved in. Hall Ambulance staged to enter from the east, and officers asked firefighters to light up the roof to check it for evidence. The scene was secured and turned over to investigators, and the department had not released any details on the victims' conditions by morning.

Deputies in the same hour worked a knife attack on the 1500 block of Lincoln Street. Callers reported a man chasing a woman down the street and attacking others, and radio traffic indicated his mother was threatened with the knife and a sister stepped in front of it. Deputies found the suspect in a cluttered shed area at the back corner of the property and were still sorting out who was hurt. A separate 911 call from nearby reported only a verbal disturbance, and the woman on that call denied anything on the callback.

Elsewhere, officers picked up a newer white Honda Accord reported stolen and moved to stop it near College Avenue and Flint Ridge. About four people bailed out and ran into an open garage, which was then pulled shut, and officers ringed the block in case the car started moving again. One man was described running southbound in a gray shirt, black shorts and a face covering toward Culver and Pioneer. A second stolen-vehicle report — another white Honda Accord, seen near Niles Road and McCurdy Drive — came in the same night. Officers also responded to the Food Maxx on Niles Street for a man with a knife, and a negotiator opened a line with him, calling for him to put the weapon down. The man was described as white, in his late thirties, dressed in black and carrying a pocket knife. Units were moved in from Lamont to cover the area while the call was worked. Earlier in the evening, deputies in the Frazier Park area handled a strong-arm robbery at a travel stop on Taft Highway. The rest of the night was alarms, crashes, disturbances and medical aids — the ordinary hum that keeps deputies busy between the calls that make the report.

Today's weather

It's currently 73 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 97 this afternoon — a proper October scorcher, so plan your outdoor work for the morning and keep the water handy. Tonight's low settles around 66. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and no active fires reported in the county. Air quality sits at 76 on the index, which is moderate — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, take it easy during the hottest hours. If you're headed over the Grapevine or down the I-5 corridor, note that all lanes are impacted near Smokey Bear Road south of us due to a fire, with evacuation warnings issued in that area — worth checking conditions before you go.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports a heavy Kern County Sheriff's Office presence in northwest Bakersfield on Friday. Deputies were out in force in the northwest part of town, though the station's report did not detail the nature of the activity. If you live or drive through that part of the city, expect to see patrol units and give them room to work. We'll pass along more specifics as they become available.

According to KGET 17, there's no mail on Monday, as the U.S. Postal Service observes a federal holiday. Post offices will be closed and there will be no regular residential or business delivery that day. If you've got something that absolutely has to go out, get it to the counter or the blue box before the weekend ends — and if you're waiting on a package, add a day to your expectations. It's a good reminder to plan around the holiday rather than be surprised by an empty mailbox.

Bakersfield Now reports that all lanes of Interstate 5 are impacted near Smokey Bear Road because of a fire, with evacuation warnings issued. That's the stretch south of us in the Grapevine corridor, a route plenty of Kern County drivers use to get to and from Southern California. If your Friday or weekend plans take you that way, check conditions before you leave and be ready to reroute. Evacuation warnings are not orders, but they mean officials want people in the area ready to move if things change.

23ABC reports that Kern County voters will decide in November whether a small sales tax increase should fund CALM Zoo's expansion. Measure Z calls for an increase of one-eighth of a percent countywide — a penny for every $8 spent — with the money going toward the zoo's long-term master plan: expanded animal habitats, new exhibits and improvements to existing facilities. Jim Damian, chair of Yes on Measure Z, told the station that CALM is a treasured community asset that draws roughly 100,000 visitors a year and called the tax an investment worth making. Kern County Republican Mark Bigger opposes it, arguing that Measure Z imposes a permanent tax increase to fund what he calls a nonessential government service, and that families already struggling with rising costs deserve fiscal responsibility instead. The measure's fate now rests with voters in the general election.

23ABC also reports that the Arvin City Council authorized $26,000 to hire a professional firm to educate voters about Measure H, a proposed one-cent sales tax increase. The firm, William Berry Campaigns, was brought on in June to educate voters and rally support, and the city has posted information on its website under "Tax Measure H" in the Quick Links. Mayor Olivia Calderon has warned that rejecting the measure could bring deeper cuts, saying the city's reserves were less than $300,000. The council's decision drew backlash on social media over both the message and the price tag, and Council Member Susana Reyes said the outreach portion will be addressed at Tuesday's council meeting. It's a reminder that in a tight budget year, even the cost of making the case for a tax is itself a public expense.

23ABC reports that Congressman David Valadao picked up dual endorsements Thursday from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Kern County Farm Bureau. The endorsements came at a press conference at a plastic manufacturing plant in southeast Bakersfield. Farm Bureau president Todd Snyder cited Valadao's support for Kern agriculture and water; Jennings Imel of the U.S. Chamber pointed to his stances on tax policy, permitting reform and workforce development. Valadao said he plans to keep working across party lines if re-elected, while noting it's unclear whether major federal tax reform will move soon, and that he's focused on the regulatory side of daily costs. For a county whose economy runs on farming and water, the Farm Bureau's nod carries real weight.

KGET 17 reports that Los Angeles-owned bio-waste farmland continues to impact the Bakersfield community. The station's report examines the ongoing effects of that land use on residents here. We'll follow the story as it develops.

Something good

Bakersfield is on track to record its fewest shootings and shooting deaths in years, city officials say — a milestone worth pausing on. Fewer triggers pulled and fewer families shattered is the kind of progress that doesn't always make headlines, but it changes lives block by block. Credit goes to the officers, outreach workers and neighbors doing the quiet, unglamorous work of keeping the peace. Let's hope the trend holds.

Coming up this week

The week ahead is full of chances to weigh in on city business. Today at noon, two committees meet at City Hall: the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee and the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee — both open to the public, and both good places to hear what's happening on the ground in your neighborhood. Monday brings a doubleheader: the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at noon, followed by the Fire Civil Service Commission at 3 p.m. Tuesday at noon, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee takes up the city's street and safety priorities — a good one for anyone with opinions about traffic on your commute. Wednesday at 10 a.m., the Water Board meets, and given how much of Kern's economy and daily life runs on water, that's always worth watching. The Planning Commission meets Thursday at 5:30 p.m. to consider land-use and development items. On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater hosts NB RIDAZ: Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off tonight, FANTASIAS on Saturday, United We Dance on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour on October 17, and Fortune Feimster's Taking Care of Biscuits tour on October 18. content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Saturday, October 10, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Saturday, October 10, and the story leading the day is a big one for local families: an $11.25 billion housing bond is headed to the November ballot, and Kern County's waiting lists show exactly why it matters. Outside, expect a warm one — a high near 86 under mostly clear skies, air quality sitting at a moderate 68, and fire crews still working the Cyrus Fire here in the county.

The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call came early, just after 2:20 a.m., when drivers on both sides of northbound Interstate 5 about two miles south of Taft Highway started dialing in about a crash. The first crew in found one vehicle fully involved in flames and a second off the shoulder, with early reports putting as many as four vehicles in the wreckage and one car left sitting in the center divider. A second ambulance came in from Lamont while firefighters knocked the fire down and units kept working the roadway.

Earlier in the evening, just after 7 p.m., responders were called to a multi-vehicle crash elsewhere in the county where two people were pinned inside a single car — one critical, one moderate. The occupants of the other vehicles were already gone by the time units arrived, and crews called for an extra engine to cut the two patients free.

Shortly before midnight, officers put out an officer safety broadcast after CHP passed along a report of a man with a silver rifle near Highway 99 at Ming Avenue, tied to a white Honda SUV and only about five minutes old. Just before 9 p.m., police and medics went to an apartment at the highest priority for a young child reported not breathing after what was described as a possible bathtub accident, with an engine and ambulance responding together. And a caller on north Chester Avenue reported being assaulted with a firearm behind a business — a man with a handgun had fired it, no one was hurt, and the people who called had left before officers arrived. The rest of the log was grass and vehicle fires from the valley floor out to the eastern county, plus alarms, welfare checks and medical aids.

Today's weather

It's 72 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 86 and a low around 61 tonight. No active weather alerts are posted for Kern County, and air quality is running moderate at 68 — fine for most folks, though sensitive readers may want to keep an eye on it if you're planning a long afternoon outside. Fire crews remain on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire, so the dry grass and the warm afternoon are worth respecting if you're out in the hills or working equipment near open ground.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that one person was injured after being struck by a vehicle in south Bakersfield. Police responded to the collision and the injured person was taken for care; details on the circumstances were limited in the initial report. It's a reminder of how quickly a morning walk or a crossing can turn dangerous on busy southside corridors, and we'll pass along more as it comes.

According to KGET 17, a new veterans center is coming to southwest Bakersfield. The secretary of Veterans Affairs announced the project, which would expand care and support services for local service members and their families. For a county with a deep military and veteran community, having those services closer to home — rather than a drive out of town — is a meaningful change.

23ABC reports that California families are still waiting as an $11.25 billion housing bond heads to the ballot. Voters will decide Proposition 1 on Nov. 3, 2026. The measure would authorize $10 billion for housing programs — affordable rentals, homeownership assistance, supportive housing and preservation of existing affordable units — plus $1.25 billion for CalVet home loans for veterans. In Kern County, the need is outrunning supply: Rebecca Moreno, CAPK's housing director, told the station that for every person they house, three more enter the system. Donnie Singleton applied for low-income housing in 2019; seven years later, she and her daughter are still rotating between a friend's home and her fiancé's, hoping for a two-bedroom she could afford at around $800 a month.

23ABC also reports that "Operation Safe California" is raising immigration enforcement concerns across the Central Valley. The Rapid Response Network of Kern said it confirmed sightings beginning October 6, and two days later reported about 61 people detained near Fresno — including people heading to work and at construction sites, shopping centers and gas stations. Immigration attorney Ana Huerta told the station she expects the activity to escalate over the next 45 days. ICE would not confirm the operation, citing operational security, while Congressman David Valadao said DHS told him enforcement is focused on people with active warrants and known criminal histories.

Keene residents are pushing back against a state effort to place a convicted sexually violent predator in their community, 23ABC reports. A closed-door court hearing Friday morning could help determine whether William Wilson is eligible for California's Conditional Release Program, which can lead to placement at a rental property in Keene under supervision and a monitored treatment plan. Wilson was convicted twice of sexually abusing two minors in Bakersfield, in 1981 and 1991. Residents Hayley Scott and Joe Martin raised questions about supervision and security. No decision was made Friday; the District Attorney's Office confirms the next placement hearing is set for October 30.

KGET 17 reports that NOR and Chevron introduced kids to friendly robots at an annual educational playday. The event gave local children a hands-on look at the technology that keeps the valley's energy industry running — the kind of early exposure that can turn into a career here at home.

Something good

The new veterans center headed for southwest Bakersfield is worth a smile this morning. For local service members and their families, it means care and support closer to home instead of a long drive out of the county — a real step toward making sure the people who served us don't have to travel far to be looked after. It's the kind of quiet, practical investment that pays off for years.

Coming up this week

City business picks up Monday with two meetings at noon and mid-afternoon: the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at 12:00, and the Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3:00. Tuesday brings the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee at noon, and Wednesday the Water Board meets at 10:00 — a good one to watch if you follow valley water. The Planning Commission closes out the week's meetings Thursday at 5:30 p.m.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. FANTASIAS takes the stage tonight, October 10. United We Dance brings festival energy on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands October 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour comes through October 18. If you're in a spooky mood, Cults & Classics presents *Psycho* on October 19 — and season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are on sale now.

Have a good Saturday, Bakersfield. Drink some water, keep an eye on your neighbors, and we'll see you tomorrow.

summary: Good Sunday morning, Bakersfield. The big story from the overnight hours is a robbery at a Union Avenue store…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Sunday, October 11, 2026

Good Sunday morning, Bakersfield. The big story from the overnight hours is a robbery at a Union Avenue store where a group of eight to ten people took food at knifepoint and fled in two cars, one north and one south. Otherwise the valley is waking up mild and quiet: 70 degrees at Meadows Field right now, a high near 79 this afternoon, moderate air quality, no weather alerts, and crews still working one active fire in the county.

The Kern Overnight

Officers spent the small hours working a robbery on Union Avenue in which the weapon was a pocket knife. According to the overnight report, the suspects were described as a group of eight to ten people, and what was taken was food from the store. One vehicle, a newer red Hyundai, ran north on Union Avenue, and a second, an older white Hyundai, went south. No arrests were reported.

West of the oil fields near Fellows, fire crews answered a smoke report off Mid Oil and found roughly two to three acres burning in brush and grass. The fire, run under the name Kirby, was reported to have roots running on three sides, and several battalions, water tenders and a helicopter were assigned to it. Earlier in the evening, a semi truck burned in a crash on the westbound side of Highway 58, and a truck caught fire on Grapevine Road just off the northbound Interstate 5 exit, closing the ramps there.

Officers also went to the area of Lowe's on Columbus Street for shots heard — no one was hurt, and the call was being checked against a separate report of a suspicious person in the same parking lot. A caller reported a brandishing that had just happened at East California Avenue and Baker Street in east Bakersfield, near MLK Park, saying a man in a green shirt had a firearm and was running toward the caller, who was in a car. The rest of the night was crashes, welfare checks, fights and medical aids stretching from Oildale out to North Edwards.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 79 degrees and a low around 52 tonight. It's currently 70 at Meadows Field. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality sits at 51 — moderate, which is a fair-weather number for a Sunday in the valley. Fire crews remain on one active fire in Kern County, the Cyrus Fire. If you're headed out early, a light layer will serve you until the sun does its work.

Top stories

23ABC reports that the third annual Cultura Fest drew families to Stramler Park on Saturday for a free celebration of cultural heritage, with traditional dancing, live music and local vendors. The event, organized by Raices of Kern, raised proceeds to support scholarships for students. Maria Torres told the station that watching her daughter perform traditional Mexican dances brought back the celebrations she grew up with, and that finding that community after moving to Bakersfield wasn't easy at first. Isaac Doria, president of Raices of Kern, said the festival is the organization's way of giving back — showcasing local vendors and putting the profits toward first-generation college students.

According to Bakersfield Now, a driver has been booked into the Kern County Jail following a fatal hit-and-run on Brundage Lane. Few details were immediately available beyond the arrest. KGET 17 separately reports that a pedestrian died in the collision and that Bakersfield police made the arrest. We'll have more as the department releases information.

KGET 17 reports that a new veterans center is coming to southwest Bakersfield, according to the secretary of Veterans Affairs. The announcement is welcome news for a county with a sizable veteran population that has long traveled out of the area for some services. Details on timing and location have not yet been released.

23ABC reports that California voters will decide Proposition 1 on Nov. 3, 2026 — an $11.25 billion housing bond that could expand affordable housing across the state and here in Kern County. Donnie Singleton applied for low-income housing in 2019; seven years later, she and her daughter still don't have a stable home, rotating between a friend's place and her fiancé's, with roughly $800 a month the most she could afford for a two-bedroom. Rebecca Moreno, CAPK's housing director, said the numbers tell the story: for every person the agency houses, three more enter the system. If passed, the measure would authorize $10 billion for housing programs — affordable rentals, homeownership assistance, supportive housing and preservation of existing affordable housing — plus $1.25 billion for CalVet home loans for veterans.

23ABC also reports that dozens gathered Saturday to mark the 50th anniversary of Colonel Allensworth State Historic Park, with guests touring the historic buildings. Lori Wear of California State Parks said Colonel Allen Allensworth was the highest-ranking Black officer of his time when he retired in 1906, and two years later founded a town that offered a safe haven for more than 300 families. His great-great-granddaughter, Anita Zachary, said it was an honor to see the crowd. Kelly Hightower and Lawonda De Leon took the train from Sacramento for their first visit; Hightower noted the town isn't in the history books they grew up with, and that knowing it existed and prospered means a great deal.

KGET 17 reports that President Trump says he will "ultimately make a decision" on whether to livestream the execution of the Fort Hood shooter. The story is a national one with limited direct bearing on Kern County, but it's drawing attention this morning.

Something good

Saturday's Cultura Fest at Stramler Park was a good reminder of what this city does well — folklorico dancers, pottery and plants, food, and neighbors who came out to celebrate heritage while quietly funding scholarships for students who are the first in their families to go to college. The same spirit showed up at Allensworth, where families from across the state walked the grounds of a town built more than a century ago on the idea that Black families deserved to live free from discrimination and violence. Both events drew crowds on a warm October weekend, and both sent something forward — one toward tuition, the other toward memory.

Coming up this week

City business resumes Monday with a special meeting of the Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee at noon, followed by the Fire Civil Service Commission at 3 p.m. Tuesday brings the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee at noon, and Wednesday the Water Board meets at 10 a.m. The Planning Commission closes out the week's meetings Thursday at 5:30 p.m.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. United We Dance brings festival energy and an all-night set to the Fox on Friday, Oct. 16. The Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour takes the stage Saturday, Oct. 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour lands Sunday, Oct. 18. Monday, Oct. 19 brings the Cults & Classics screening of "Psycho," and Switchfoot performs with special guest Anberlin on the Forever Now Tour Wednesday, Oct. 21. If you're planning further out, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are already on sale.

Have a restful Sunday, Bakersfield.

The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Monday, October 12, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Monday, October 12, and the big overnight item was a robbery at the Dollar Tree on Mount Vernon Avenue where a machete was used — two suspects got away on foot and officers are still working the area. Otherwise it's a cool, clean start: 57 degrees at Meadows Field, air quality good at 44, no weather alerts, and one active fire, the Cyrus Fire, still on crews' boards.

The Kern Overnight

Dispatch logged 32 incidents overnight, led by six crashes, six medical and overdose calls, and four disturbances and welfare checks. The one that drew the most units was the robbery in progress in the 2600 block of Mount Vernon Avenue, where a machete was used at the Dollar Tree. Two suspects were last seen on foot heading toward the fast-food lot next door, and officers were working the area. If you were near Mount Vernon early this morning, that's what the patrol cars were doing.

Out on the roads, a crash on southbound Interstate 5 north of the rest area left two people ejected from a vehicle. Traffic was held while crews worked, and one patient was flown out while the other went by ground. A vehicle rolled over on northbound Rosedale Highway just north of Jenkins Road; crews checked the area but couldn't find a reported black or blue sedan on the right shoulder. Wasco police handled a crash where the driver tried to flee and was detained — nobody was pinned, and the driver complained of generalized pain. Officers also went to Panama Lane and Pebble Point for a vehicle against a pedestrian, with a person reported down in the roadway on the southbound side.

Deputies were sent to the 2100 block of Lancer Drive, where a caller said her husband and four friends had gone dirt biking and none had returned or answered their phones — crews responded for a possible search and rescue. A woman called 911 from Yuma Way to report she had been strangled, then disconnected; officers went to check on her. Firefighters handled a house fire at a county address, finding several spots inside showing heat but no hazard to anyone, and released units from the call. The evening log also included a domestic disturbance in the 1300 block of Princeton Avenue with a criminal protective order listing the caller as a protected party, a man found unconscious and bleeding on a bicycle at Manchester Lane, and a theft in progress on the 3400 block of Mall View Road reported as five juveniles loading up.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 69 and a low around 49 tonight — a genuinely fall-feeling Monday after that stretch of triple-digit heat. It's currently 57 degrees at Meadows Field. No active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is 44, which is good. Fire crews remain on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire. If you've been waiting to open the windows or get back outside, this is the week for it.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Kyiv says Russian strikes on energy facilities are continuing despite what President Trump has called an "energy ceasefire." The story comes out of Ukraine's capital as the war grinds on, with officials there saying attacks on power infrastructure haven't stopped. For Kern County readers, the through-line is the same one we've watched all year: instability overseas tends to show up at the gas pump and in grocery prices here at home, and energy infrastructure is exactly the kind of target that moves markets.

According to 23ABC, Bakersfield's Greek Food Festival closed out its three-day run Sunday at St. George Greek Orthodox Church, and organizers hope to beat last year's crowd of about 8,000. Co-chair Annette Londquist said they think they'll max back out and go beyond 8,000, though she admitted they never really know until the numbers come in. Volunteer Tanya Alsheikh, who's worked the festival since she was 6, said tiramisu cupcakes, pistachio baklava and chocolate hazelnut baklava all sold out — and they made more this year anyway. For Katherine Rupert, it was a bucket-list weekend decades in the making; she came on her daughter's reminder and planned to try everything.

23ABC also reports that Kern County is getting relief from record October heat, but El Niño could bring a wet winter to Bakersfield. The city just logged its third-hottest first week of October on record, with four triple-digit days. Chief Meteorologist Brandon Michaels told viewers an upper-level high that had been parked over the region for weeks is finally moving out, replaced by a strong low and a much cooler pattern — though warmer temperatures could still return later this month. Nancy Banducci of Banducci's Family Farm said the heat hurt business badly, with maybe ten customers on a 102-degree day, but families are coming back now that it's cool. Looking further out, Michaels said El Niño could shape what this winter looks like here.

KGET 17 reports that a pedestrian died in a hit-and-run collision on Brundage Lane and the driver was arrested, according to Bakersfield police. The department says the driver was taken into custody after the collision. It's a reminder of how quickly things can turn on our busiest corridors, and why Bakersfield police keep asking anyone who sees a crash to stop and call it in rather than drive on.

KGET 17 also reports that a new veterans center is coming to southwest Bakersfield, according to the secretary of Veterans Affairs. Details are still thin beyond the announcement, but the news matters for a county with a large veteran population that has long had to travel for some services. We'll share specifics on location and timing as they're released.

Bakersfield Now is asking readers to vote on whether they think increased ICE enforcement makes California communities safer. It's an informal reader poll, not a news finding, but it's a useful temperature check on a question that keeps coming up in local conversation. You can weigh in on their site.

Something good

The third annual Cultura Fest brought families to Stramler Park on Saturday for a free celebration of heritage — traditional dancing, live music and local vendors — organized by Raices of Kern. Proceeds go to scholarships for students, including first-generation college students. Maria Torres watched her daughter perform traditional Mexican dances and said it reminded her of the celebrations she grew up with, and that without events like this, families simply don't get exposed to those traditions. That's a good note to start the week on.

Coming up this week

The county and city calendar is busy. Today, the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets at noon, and the Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3 p.m. Tuesday brings the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee at noon — the one to watch if you care about road projects, bike lanes or bus routes. Wednesday at 10 a.m. is the Water Board, always worth attention in a valley that lives by its groundwater. Thursday at 5:30 p.m. the Planning Commission takes up its agenda. On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate: United We Dance brings festival energy and an all-night lineup on October 16, the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour hits the stage October 17, Fortune Feimster brings her "Taking Care of Biscuits" tour October 18, Cults & Classics screens *Psycho* on October 19, and Switchfoot with special guest Anberlin plays the Forever Now Tour on October 21. Pick your night — there's something for just about everyone.

Have a good Monday, Bakersfield. Stay cool while it lasts.
