headline: Todd Lee returns to CSUB with a goal of bringing Bakersfield back to Roadrunners basketball
summary: The story leading the day is a homecoming: Todd Lee, who helped bring a national championship to CSUB three…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Tuesday, October 13, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a homecoming: Todd Lee, who helped bring a national championship to CSUB three decades ago, is back as head coach of Roadrunners basketball, and he's talking as much about the city as the scoreboard. Outside, expect a mild fall Tuesday — a high near 73, a low around 50 tonight, moderate air quality, and no weather alerts for Kern County. Fire crews remain on one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire.

The Kern Overnight

The biggest call of the night came on the southbound Highway 204 connector onto Highway 99, where a single vehicle rolled over. Fire crews reported four patients, all tagged green for minor injuries, and called for a second ambulance to the scene. One engine was canceled once things were under control. No names or exact locations beyond the connector were released.

Elsewhere in the county, a vehicle hit the front of the mountain and rolled over on northbound Highway 155 in the Kern River canyon, about a mile south of Hungry Gulch. Radio traffic described poor cell phone reception with the patient, and the wrecked vehicle was reported blocking the roadway. Multiple callers reported brush burning along eastbound Highway 58 near South Union Avenue, drawing county engines and city equipment to the grass fire.

In east Bakersfield, firefighters found light smoke at a house fire on North Kern Street. Crews were also sent to a structure fire response at a cold storage building in the 5500 block of Valpredo Avenue, where Truck 54 reported water flowing from one room and nothing from another; crews laddered the building looking for a heat source and got inside without finding anything visible.

In north Bakersfield, officers were sent to Beardsley Avenue for a disturbance involving a man on a motorized bike who was reported to be carrying a machete. He was last seen fleeing eastbound with a checkered backpack and was not located. A caller also reported impact sounds at a building on Westwind Drive in central Bakersfield, followed by a sedan leaving the area.

The rest of the log ran the usual wide range: a large debris pile burning in Wasco around 7:32 p.m., with crews calling for one additional engine and reporting power lines nearby that did not appear affected; a driver who went off the road after hitting the mountain in the canyon; a car window broken by an object thrown from a semi on Highway 166; a stolen pickup out of Los Angeles; and medical aids scattered across the county.

Today's weather

It's 52 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, on the way to a high near 73 and a low around 50 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality sits at 57 — moderate — so most folks can go about their day normally, though anyone sensitive to air quality may want to keep an eye on it. Fire crews are on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire. Otherwise, it's a quiet, comfortable October day in the valley.

Top stories

23ABC reports that Todd Lee is back at Cal State Bakersfield as head coach of Roadrunners basketball, nearly three decades after he helped the program win a national championship. Lee served as an assistant at CSUB from 1994 to 1997, when the Roadrunners captured the NCAA Division II title, then followed head coach Pat Douglass to UC Irvine and went on to coach at South Dakota, Kentucky Wesleyan and USC. At an open practice at the GSA Dignity Health Sports Complex, fans got a look at this year's roster. Lee told the station he has always wanted this job — "I feel like this is my home" — and said his goal is a tough, physical team and a renewed connection with a community that once packed the Icardo Center. Returning guard and forward Jaden Alexander said the culture already feels more professional.

According to 23ABC, vandals hit Bear Mountain Park with graffiti, and part of the picnic table area is now closed off while crews work to clean it up. The Bear Mountain Recreation and Parks District announced the vandalism on its Facebook page Oct. 9. One visitor, who gave only her first name, Maria, told the station it's sad that families can't come picnic with their kids, and that it's hard to explain to her 4-year-old son why there are writings on the playground. The district said maintenance crews have been working tirelessly to remove the damage and that it's grateful for the community's support.

KGET 17 reports that a Kern County judge's ruling could overturn California's fracking law. The decision, if it stands, would reach well beyond Kern County — this is the state's oil-producing heart, and fracking rules shape how local operators work and how the county's largest industry plans ahead. We'll be watching for what the ruling means in practice for Kern operators and regulators in the days to come.

KGET 17 also reports that the Bakersfield VA clinic is moving to the former CRC headquarters on Old River, for now. The move is described as temporary, but it matters to the thousands of local veterans who rely on the clinic for care — a change of address means a change of routine, and we'll pass along details on hours and services as they're confirmed.

23ABC reports that Ward 1 city council candidate Mercy Peña has acknowledged two felony forgery convictions while campaigning for the seat currently held by Eric Arias. Peña confirmed the court records are hers after the station compared signatures, and she currently serves on the Greenfield School District Board of Trustees. She told the station the convictions date to 1992, that she hasn't been expunged, and that she's owning it: "I'm going to fess up to it because it did happen." She said the experience shapes how she looks at city spending, and that her priorities include long-term recovery programs for homelessness and giving residents more say in city decisions.

KGET 17 reports that Congressional District 20 candidate Sandra Van Scotter is talking about running as an underdog and what winning would look like for her. We'll have more on that race as the campaign develops.

Something good

Todd Lee's homecoming is the kind of story that gives a whole program something to rally around. He was part of the 1997 national championship staff, and now he's back where he says he belongs, talking about giving to Bakersfield because Bakersfield gives back. Fans got an early look at the roster at open practice, and there's a familiar face at the front of the gym again. Whatever the season brings, that's a good place to start.

Coming up this week

Public meetings fill out the calendar this week. The Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets today, Tuesday, Oct. 13, at noon — a good one for anyone with thoughts on roads, bike lanes or traffic safety in the city. The Water Board meets Wednesday, Oct. 14, at 10 a.m., always worth watching in a valley that lives and works by its water. Then the Planning Commission meets Thursday, Oct. 15, at 5:30 p.m., where land-use decisions that shape neighborhoods get their first real airing.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch. United We Dance brings festival energy for an all-night show on Friday, Oct. 16. The Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour takes the stage Saturday, Oct. 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour lands Sunday, Oct. 18. The Cults & Classics series screens "Psycho" on Monday, Oct. 19, and Switchfoot plays with special guest Anberlin on the Forever Now Tour on Wednesday, Oct. 21. If you're planning further out, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are already on sale.

Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield. We'll see you tomorrow morning.

The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Thursday, October 15, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Thursday, October 15, and the story leading the day is an officer-involved shooting in southeast Bakersfield near Pacheco Road and Monitor Street that left one person dead and sent officers searching the neighborhood for a second. Expect a warm one — a high near 86 — with moderate air quality and no weather alerts, though crews remain on the Cyrus Fire. Here's what happened while you slept.

The Kern Overnight

The night's biggest call went out as an assault on an officer. summary: The story leading the day is fire weather: with winds up and the ground dry, utilities have already cut power…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Friday, October 16, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield, and happy Friday. The story leading the day is fire weather: with winds up and the ground dry, utilities have already cut power to thousands of Kern customers and are warning that more shutoffs could run through Saturday. Expect another hot one — a high near 91 — with moderate air quality, no weather alerts, and one active fire burning in the county.

The Kern Overnight

Deputies and firefighters had a long night, and the strangest call came out of Lamont. Two vehicles collided on East Bear Mountain Boulevard at General Beale Road, out in the rural stretch east of town, and the first units on scene found a large amount of blood on both cars and inside one of them — but nobody who needed an ambulance. The people involved said no one else had been riding with them, and deputies didn't trust that account. They searched the wreckage and the ground around it for anyone who might have been thrown clear, and a sheriff's helicopter was called in to help sweep the area. The investigation stayed open.

Fire carried the middle of the night. A single-wide mobile home in the 200 block of Oswell Street was burning with moderate smoke showing when Battalion 4 arrived. Engine 41 was assigned to pull a line as fire attack, the rest of the assignment split between water supply and search, and crews reported a knockdown a few minutes later, cancelling a second battalion and a truck. Traffic was shut down in both directions on Oswell while hose lines lay across the road. A second house fire drew a full assignment to the 1400 block of Ridgeview Street in east Bakersfield, and a report of a building on fire at 34th Street and San Dimas Street came in just before dawn.

Elsewhere around the county: a woman swung an ax at a man in the 1400 block of Calcutta Drive in south Bakersfield and then left on foot still carrying it; a driver was found unresponsive behind the wheel at White Lane and Buena Vista Road with CPR under way; a man walked into his home in the 3400 block of Granada Avenue with blood on his hands; and a person was reported down on the railroad tracks on Truxtun Avenue approaching Baker Street, where police and medics worked both sides of the crossing while a train crew was asked how long the person had been there.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 91 today and a low around 63 tonight. It's 63 right now at Meadows Field, so the morning is genuinely pleasant before the afternoon turns hot. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 73, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's worth keeping an eye on through the day. Fire crews are on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire. With dry, breezy conditions in the forecast, that's the number to watch.

Top stories

23ABC reports that utilities have already switched off power for thousands of Kern County customers as high winds and dry conditions raise the wildfire risk, and more shutoffs could be coming. As of 10 p.m. Thursday, Southern California Edison had cut service to 4,251 customers in Kern and PG&E to 593, with notifications sent to thousands more who could be affected. PG&E says roughly 1,100 of its Kern customers could lose power, including 48 on medical baseline, while SCE is weighing outages for more than 20,000 customers here. The potential shutoffs could last into Saturday, so it's worth checking your utility's website and having a plan for refrigerated food, medical equipment and charging.

KGET 17 reports that one person is dead after an officer-involved shooting in south Bakersfield, and that neighbors have been sharing what they saw. That is the extent of what we can tell you this morning — the circumstances, the agency involved and the person's identity aren't detailed in what we have in front of us, so we'll pass along more as it's confirmed.

According to 23ABC, a Bakersfield Christian High School student has founded a nonprofit that opens educational and extracurricular doors for foster youth and underserved children. Mariana Vargas started For A Better Future USA after befriending a girl named Cristina, who grew up in an orphanage in Mexico and spoke only Spanish when she arrived in the classroom; helping her navigate school showed Vargas how much support some kids go without. The nonprofit partners with local businesses — Kumon, Code Ninjas and Mathnasium among them — to provide scholarships, and Kumon Brimhall owner Vikash Lakhani said two students recruited through the program are expected to begin there soon, with Code Ninjas also offering free coding education.

KGET 17 reports that the Ward 3 candidates shared a stage for a debate and found plenty of common ground on the issues — they just didn't agree on how to solve them. The forum gave voters in that part of the city a side-by-side look at the people asking to represent them, which matters most in the final stretch before ballots are cast. We're summarizing from the headline alone here; the station's full report has the specifics of where the candidates split.

Something good

Vera Varner is 82 years old, and one night a year she gets to be a cheerleader again. Varner told 23ABC that Bakersfield College's homecoming is "almost magical" — a chance to reconnect with fellow alumni and perform at halftime, even if, as she joked, it's like a time machine "until the next day you're so sore you can't move." She's hoping more former BC cheerleaders join her at Saturday's game; she figures there should be at least 600 alumni out there. All you need is red and white and a signed waiver, and the station's story has the details.

Separately, KGET 17 reports the Sherna Armstrong Christmas Benefit Concert is looking for sponsors. If your business wants to help holiday music fill the air this season, that's an open door — and a good one.

Coming up this week

Tonight, the Fox Theater hosts United We Dance, a festival-energy show built to run all night. Saturday brings the AiAi & Tekla Comedy Tour to the Fox, and it's also Bakersfield College homecoming — the day Vera Varner and her fellow alumni will be back on the field at halftime. Sunday, Fortune Feimster brings her Taking Care of Biscuits tour to the Fox, and Monday the theater's Cults & Classics series screens Psycho. Switchfoot, with special guest Anberlin, plays the Forever Now Tour at the Fox on Wednesday, October 21.

On the public-meeting side, the Historic Preservation Commission meets Tuesday, October 20, at 10 a.m. Bakersfield's City Council has two sessions on Wednesday, October 21 — one at 3:30 p.m. and one at 5:15 p.m. Agendas and locations are posted through the city, so if you've been meaning to weigh in on something, this is the week to show up.

Have a good Friday, and keep an eye on the wind.

headline: East Bakersfield-Foothill football game stopped due to medical emergency on sideline
summary: It's Saturday, October 17, and the story leading the day is a frightening one that turned into something…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Saturday, October 17, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Saturday, October 17, and the story leading the day is a frightening one that turned into something quietly moving — the East Bakersfield–Foothill football game was stopped before halftime after a medical emergency on the East High sideline. Otherwise, the valley is calm: expect a high near 91 under clear skies, air quality sitting at a moderate 65, no weather alerts in effect, and crews still working one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire. Grab your coffee — here's what happened while you slept.

The Kern Overnight

The biggest call of the night came shortly after 1:15 a.m., when a commercial building near 30th Street and Union Avenue caught fire. Crews arrived to find the loading dock involved and power lines down along one corner of the structure. They set up a command post at the intersection and closed the northbound side of the road while they worked. Firefighters knocked the flames down from the outside first, then moved in to finish off the interior fire, and reported the primary search clear. No injuries were reported.

Fire carried the rest of the night too. Multiple callers reported smoke showing from an apartment window in the 3400 block of Wible Road in southwest Bakersfield, where Truck 7, Truck 1 and two battalion companies were assigned to a second-floor unit in a two-story complex and knocked the fire down. A grass fire was also reported near Cottonwood and Bradshaw.

Elsewhere, police ran a foot chase that ended near Lincoln and Robinson streets in east Bakersfield, with Air 1 overhead talking units onto one person detained on the 1200 block of Lincoln Street — officers were told the man came out of the passenger seat of a car that had been stopped and had tried to get into a house before he was caught. A domestic call in the 7000 block of Willis Avenue turned up a report of a gun, and officers also worked an assault in which a caller said she was held down and had her phone taken. Two crashes drew responses: one at 18th and H streets that left vehicles blocking the roadway, and a single-car wreck on Mohawk Street that sent two people to the hospital by ambulance. A semi was reported driving the wrong way with bright headlights on Highway 58. The log also shows a commercial fire alarm at a hotel on East Brundage Lane that crews traced without finding a fire, a pursuit in Arvin, and a report of a blue sedan stolen from a parking area.

Today's weather

It's 57 degrees right now at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 91 this afternoon — a warm, clear October Saturday. Tonight's low settles around 63. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at 65, which is fine for most folks but worth noting if you're sensitive and planning to spend the afternoon outside. Fire crews remain on one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire. If you're headed to the chalk festival or a ballgame, it's a sunscreen-and-water kind of day.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Friday night's East Bakersfield–Foothill football game was stopped before halftime because of a medical emergency on the East High sideline. According to 23ABC, the Trojans had just taken a 17–0 lead with under two minutes left in the half when play came to an abrupt halt. An ambulance drove onto the track near the 40-yard line, followed by Kern County Fire Department vehicles. A Foothill player and someone on the East sideline told 23ABC that a member of the visiting team's staff collapsed in what they believed was a heart attack, though authorities have not confirmed that or released any information about the person's condition. After the person was taken away, players, cheerleaders and coaches from both schools gathered at midfield for a prayer. The game did not resume and was declared final, with Foothill taking the win — a result that matters a great deal, since the Trojans had forfeited all seven of their previous victories over eligibility violations involving two players and now need to win both of their remaining games to reach the playoffs.

KGET 17 also has the rest of Week 9 high school football scores from around Bakersfield and Kern County, so if you're tracking a team's playoff path, that roundup is the place to find Friday's results.

The California Highway Patrol says a pedestrian suffered major injuries in a collision in Oildale, according to KGET 17. Details on the circumstances were limited in the initial report, but the CHP is handling the investigation. It's a reminder of how quickly things change for people walking along some of our busier corridors, especially after dark.

23ABC is reporting exclusively that a Bakersfield man was detained by ICE while on his way to work, and his business partner is raising concerns about how he was treated. David Rivera, owner of D-R Building Solutions, told the station he got a call from his business partner, Sergio, as the detention was unfolding — Sergio said he'd been pulled over by unmarked vehicles and believed it was ICE. Rivera said he could hear what was happening over the phone and grew worried, particularly when Sergio mentioned a lawyer and, in Rivera's words, it didn't seem to matter. Sergio was able to give Rivera his location before the call ended; Rivera later arrived to find the truck on the side of the freeway with a broken window. Video from the Rapid Response Network of Kern shows the truck on the shoulder. Rivera said Sergio's family is distraught. Authorities have not released information about Sergio's status or the reason for the stop.

And a note from Bakersfield Now: Six Flags Over Georgia has reopened following a deadly fall from its Goliath coaster, though that ride remains closed. It's a national story with local reach, since plenty of Kern families make that trip.

Something good

The Via Arté chalk festival has turned a parking lot at the Marketplace on Ming Avenue into a walk-through gallery, with more than 100 artists at work. It's free and runs today and tomorrow from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., with reservations available at viaartebakersfield.com — you can also buy a 2-by-2-foot square and make your own. Bakersfield Museum of Art marketing manager Lauren Marty told 23ABC the tradition reaches back to Italian street painters who made art on the pavement, something an everyday working person could actually see. Proceeds support the museum's exhibitions, art education and community programs. This year 22 high school teams are competing alongside featured artist Anitta Meza, who started in the student competition 13 years ago and is now creating a 12-by-15-foot piece inspired by words from her aunt, who is battling stage-four thyroid cancer — and it glows in the dark.

Coming up this week

It's a busy stretch at City Hall. The Historic Preservation Commission meets Tuesday, October 20, at 10 a.m., and the Special Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets the same day at 2 p.m., followed by the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2 p.m. On Wednesday, October 21, the City Council holds a 3:30 p.m. session and then its regular meeting at 5:15 p.m. — two separate agendas, so check which one has your item before you head down.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. The AiAi & Tekla Comedy Tour lands tonight, October 17. Fortune Feimster brings her "Taking Care of Biscuits" tour Sunday, October 18. Monday, October 19, is the Cults & Classics screening of "Psycho." Switchfoot plays with special guest Anberlin on the Forever Now Tour Wednesday, October 21, and Henry Cho's Empty Nest Tour comes through Friday, October 23. If you're already thinking ahead to next season, the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026–2027 is on sale now.

Have a good Saturday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there, and if you're near Ming Avenue, go see what a hundred chalk artists can do to a parking lot.

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Sunday, October 18, 2026

Good Sunday morning, Bakersfield. The big story this weekend is a boil water notice in parts of Bear Valley Springs, issued after power shutoffs disrupted the community's water system — we have the details below. Closer to home, a south Bakersfield neighborhood woke up to shell casings and questions after shots were reported overnight, and fire crews stayed busy from Ridgecrest to east Bakersfield. It's a warm one ahead: near 90 this afternoon, air quality sitting at a healthy 38, and no weather alerts anywhere in the county.

The Kern Overnight

The night's largest police response came out of south Bakersfield, where several callers reported gunfire near a court in the 900 block of Karma Court. Officers were told to broadcast for officer safety as they headed in, and once on scene they found a shell casing on the north side of the court. A witness told them two men had already left the area on foot to the north, and no victim was ever located. It's the kind of call that ties up units for a while — a perimeter, a search, a report — and ends without an arrest.

Fire ran alongside the police work all night. Crews were sent to a structure fire at a 1,500-square-foot single-story home on West Moyer Avenue in Ridgecrest, where the first engine arrived to find nothing showing and took command; a second engine was diverted from a call on Highway 14 to help, and the response drew a full assignment of engines plus a battalion chief. In east Bakersfield, crews answered a structure fire reported behind a home in the 1000 block of Sumner Street, with two engines, a truck and a rescue assigned. Grass and lot fires kept other units moving around the county.

Officers also worked a robbery at a mini mart in the 3300 block of Wible Road, where a man in a white shirt and red pants ran off on foot with cash and a metal rod; a person was found nearby shortly after. A fight reported in front of a home in the 2700 block of Whitley Drive drew a caller's estimate of about 40 juveniles, one person with a cut above an eyebrow, and a neighbor's report of ATVs, fireworks and possible gunshots in the area. A vehicle struck a pedestrian on Fremont Street, and a foot chase through the alleys between Lincoln, Quincy and Baker streets ended with one person in custody and a perimeter held for another.

The log filled in around those calls: just after 7 p.m., a man under the influence was lying in front of a dentist's office on the 2200 block of Niles Street and refusing to leave; twenty minutes later, a caller asked officers to check on a 13-year-old reportedly left alone for a week at a home on the 400 block of Willow Drive; and a crash involving a car carrying an infant and a toddler came in around 8:13 p.m.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 90 degrees today and a low around 59 tonight. It's currently 66 degrees at Meadows Field, so the morning is comfortable before the heat builds this afternoon. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is good — an AQI of 38, which is about as clean as the valley gets. Fire crews remain on one active fire in the county, the Cyrus Fire. If you're spending the day outside, the early hours are your friend; by mid-afternoon it will feel more like late summer than mid-October.

Top stories

Bakersfield Now reports that a boil water notice has been issued for parts of Bear Valley Springs amid power shutoff issues. Residents in the affected areas are being told to boil their water before drinking or cooking until the notice is lifted. It's a familiar and frustrating sequence in the mountain communities — shutoffs meant to reduce wildfire risk knock out the pumps and treatment that deliver safe water, and the people who live there absorb the inconvenience. If you have neighbors in Bear Valley Springs, it's worth checking on them today.

According to 23ABC, hundreds of people gathered Saturday at the Liberty Bell in downtown Bakersfield for a "No Kings" vote-early event ahead of the election. Organizer Audrey Chavez described it not as a protest but as a celebration of the right to vote, part of a nationwide effort. People began arriving at 9 a.m., then walked over to the Kern County Elections Department to drop off ballots, with organizers saying they wanted residents to understand the process and have their questions answered. One attendee, David, told the station he came because he believes the country is in trouble and wants people to make their voices heard. The gathering at Truxtun and Chester avenues was one of many held across California in the days before the election.

23ABC also reports that Foothill High School's football team has forfeited all seven of its wins after the California Interscholastic Federation ruled two players ineligible. Athletic Director Mike Biezard told the station the players were initially deemed eligible, but the school received a letter from the CIF on Tuesday reversing that, forcing the forfeits. Biezard said schools don't verify the residential information parents and guardians provide — the CIF does. It remains unclear why the CIF opened its investigation, and the district is withholding further detail to protect the privacy of the boys and their family. A Foothill kicker told 23ABC it isn't right to ruin a season this way, and community members are unhappy that the whole team is paying the price.

KGET 17 reports that Friday's East Bakersfield–Foothill game was stopped before halftime because of a medical emergency on the East High sideline. The Trojans led 17-0 with under two minutes left in the half when play halted; an ambulance drove onto the track near the 40-yard line, followed by Kern County Fire Department vehicles. A Foothill player and someone on East's sideline told the station a member of the visiting staff had collapsed, though authorities have not confirmed that or released any information on the person's condition. After the ambulance left, players, cheerleaders and coaches from both teams gathered at midfield to pray. The game was declared final with Foothill winning — a result the Trojans badly needed, since they must win their last two games to reach the playoffs.

KGET 17 also reports that a pedestrian suffered major injuries in a collision in Oildale, according to the California Highway Patrol. Few details were immediately available, and the investigation is ongoing. It's a reminder of how quickly things change for people walking along the county's busier roads, and we'll pass along more as it comes.

Something good

The Via Arté chalk festival turned an ordinary Bakersfield parking lot into a gallery this weekend, with local artists and neighbors working side by side to fill the pavement with color. Events like this don't happen by accident — they take organizers, sponsors and a lot of willing hands — and the result was a space that people who might never set foot in a museum could walk through and enjoy for free. If you stopped by, you saw the best version of this town: creative, unpretentious, and happy to share.

Coming up this week

It's a busy week at City Hall. The Historic Preservation Commission meets Tuesday, October 20, at 10 a.m., and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets the same day at 2 p.m. Also Tuesday at 2 p.m. is a special meeting of the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee — a good one to watch if you care about bike lanes, sidewalks or how the city moves people around. On Wednesday, October 21, the City Council holds two sessions: a 3:30 p.m. meeting and the regular 5:15 p.m. meeting, both worth checking for the full agendas.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. Tonight, Sunday, October 18, Fortune Feimster brings her "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour to the Fox. Monday, October 19, the Cults & Classics series screens "Psycho." Switchfoot plays with special guest Anberlin on the Forever Now Tour on Wednesday, October 21. Henry Cho brings "The Empty Nest Tour" on Friday, October 23, and Fred Armisen closes out the week Saturday, October 24, with "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome." And if you're already thinking ahead, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics series are on sale now.

Have a good Sunday, and stay cool out there.

headline: Shafter remembers Ronald Pierce, Minter Field Air Museum chairman who spent decades preserving its history
summary: The big story this Monday is a farewell — Shafter gathered at Minter Field over the weekend to remember…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Monday, October 19, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. The big story this Monday is a farewell — Shafter gathered at Minter Field over the weekend to remember Ronald Pierce, the museum's longtime chairman who spent decades keeping the airfield's history alive. Conditions outside are calm and warm: 61° at Meadows Field right now, a high near 86° this afternoon, no active weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a moderate 52.

The Kern Overnight

Kern County dispatch logged 42 incidents between 7 p.m. and just past 5 a.m., and fires made up the largest share of them — 11 in all. Three were logged as structure fires, at 7:37, 8:44 and 4:25 this morning; the rest came in as fires of varying description, including one on South Bliss Street, one on South Chester Avenue, one on Lake Street, and a car fire on Olive Drive just after midnight that followed a crash near Highway 99.

Crashes and traffic accounted for six calls. A crash involving a Nissan was reported on Harris Road around 8:31 p.m., and a tow was requested after a collision damaged a guardrail in the 2 a.m. hour. A hit-and-run involving two vehicles came in a couple of minutes later, and officers responded to a crash on Gosford Road at 5:16 a.m.

Four weapons and assault calls were logged. Minor injuries were reported after a fight at Stockdale and River early in the evening, and an assault involving a knife possibly being used was reported at the Navigation Center late in the night. Two shootings were logged, at 9:03 and 11:16 p.m. Medical and overdose calls numbered five, including a person with a traumatic injury at Cherry Acres. Officers also ran four probation checks and answered four welfare calls. Details on all of these remain limited this morning, and we'll pass along anything more specific as it's confirmed.

Today's weather

It's 61° at Meadows Field to start the day, on the way to a high near 86° — a warm one for mid-October, so plan on water if you're working outside. The low tonight drops to around 54°. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are being reported. Air quality is moderate at 52, which is fine for most of us but worth noting if you're sensitive to smoke or dust. Otherwise, a quiet, clear October day across the valley.

Top stories

23ABC reports that Shafter said goodbye to Ronald Pierce on Sunday, and the send-off fit the man. Dozens gathered at Minter Field Air Museum for a celebration of life that included a flyover, honoring the museum's longtime chairman, who died Sept. 4 after a short illness at 89. A Shafter native, Pierce first knew the airfield as a child while his father worked there during World War II, and from the early 2000s on he shared that history with students and visitors. Friends took the open mic to remember his early-morning dashes to the museum and his anniversary phone calls reminding other husbands to do right by their wives.

According to 23ABC, Felicita Park in Arvin has finished its first major renovation, and it took only four months. The city was awarded a donation of more than $56,000 in late spring, and the park at Felicita Road and Rayo de la Luna Drive now has exercise equipment, new benches and solar lights. Gustavo Aguirre of the Center on Race, Poverty, and the Environment said residents had waited years for lighting and improvements, and park-goers told the station the free equipment makes a fitness routine possible for neighbors who couldn't otherwise afford one.

KGET 17 reports that tributes are still coming in for Bobby Rocha, the East Bakersfield High School athletic trainer who was taken from Friday night's football game by ambulance. The game against Foothill stopped with less than two minutes left before halftime, and players, coaches and cheerleaders from both schools gathered at midfield to pray; officials declared Foothill the winner. Foothill's football program posted a tribute saying its "family is heartbroken," and Bakersfield College held a moment of silence before its homecoming game Saturday.

Bakersfield Now reports that a boil water notice has been issued for parts of Bear Valley Springs amid power shutoff issues. Residents in the affected area should boil tap water before drinking or cooking until the notice is lifted. We'll share any update on the notice's scope or timeline as soon as it's announced.

KGET 17 also reports that a pedestrian suffered major injuries in a collision in Oildale, according to the California Highway Patrol. Few details were available Monday morning, and the CHP's investigation is ongoing.

Something good

The Via Arté chalk festival turned a Bakersfield parking lot into an open-air gallery over the weekend, with local artists and neighbors working side by side to fill the pavement with color for anyone who wanted to stroll through. It's the kind of event that costs nothing to enjoy and makes a plain stretch of asphalt feel like somewhere worth lingering — a good reminder that a lot of the art in this town shows up where you least expect it, and washes away with the next rain.

Coming up this week

It's a busy week at City Hall. Tuesday starts early with the Historic Preservation Commission at 10 a.m., followed by the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2 p.m. and a special meeting of the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee, also at 2 p.m. Wednesday brings two City Council sessions — a 3:30 p.m. meeting and a 5:15 p.m. meeting — so check the agendas if you're tracking a particular item.

At the Fox Theater, the Cults & Classics series screens *Psycho* tonight, Switchfoot brings the Forever Now Tour with special guest Anberlin on Wednesday, comedian Henry Cho performs his Empty Nest Tour on Friday, and Saturday offers a double bill: Fred Armisen's "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome" and the BLADE RAVE, both at the Fox. And if you're planning further out, season passes for the 2026–2027 Cults & Classics run are on sale now.

Have a good Monday, and we'll see you back here tomorrow.

headline: Honor Flight Kern County completes trip weeks after first-ever flight cancellation
summary: It's Tuesday, October 20, and the story leading the day is a somber one — East Bakersfield High is mourning…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Tuesday, October 20, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Tuesday, October 20, and the story leading the day is a somber one — East Bakersfield High is mourning longtime equipment manager Bobby Rocha, who collapsed on the sideline during Friday night's game. Closer to home, it's a mild fall morning: 55 degrees at Meadows Field, no weather alerts anywhere in Kern County, and air quality sitting at a moderate 51. Here's what happened while you slept.

The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call ended without anyone getting hurt. Officers responded to a report of a man holding a knife in his left hand who would not cooperate with commands. He wasn't advancing on anyone, but he stayed armed and refused to put the weapon down, so supervisors set up command and held the scene instead of moving in. About 35 minutes later, officers closed in and took him into custody. Charges including assault with a deadly weapon, criminal threats and child endangerment were requested.

Earlier in the evening, airport police cleared the terminal at Meadows Field after a report of a possible firearm on the property. A man in a black hoodie and black shorts was seen heading toward the employee parking area below the front of the terminal. Officers held the terminal while they searched and reported all channels clear within a few minutes.

Elsewhere around the county, a caller on Pond Road reported about five people firing guns into the air, with three vehicles described leaving the area — a gray Volkswagen, a black truck and a red Chevrolet. Crews went to Bliss and Texas streets for a mini-bike against a vehicle with possibly two patients; Engine 6 found one person down in the roadway and staged incoming units while medics went to work. On Center Street in east Bakersfield, a caller reported a man hitting windows with a machete he kept in his vehicle; he was described as 35 years old and believed to be under the influence of alcohol.

Fires kept crews moving all night — a U-Haul on Lake Street, a vehicle on Mayer Avenue, a patch of grass and brush larger than a car near Alfred Harrell Highway, and a structure fire call after 4 a.m. The log also included a pair of court order calls that turned up no violations, a two-vehicle crash that left the roadway blocked, a Nissan crash on Harris Road, an assault on California Avenue involving a victim in a wheelchair, and a suspected DUI driver who tried to run from a crash before witnesses held him on the sidewalk.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 82 degrees today and a low around 55 tonight. It's currently 55 at Meadows Field. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is moderate at 51 — a decent day to be outside, though sensitive folks may want to keep an eye on it as the afternoon warms up. No active fires are being reported in the county this morning.

Top stories

23ABC reports that Honor Flight Kern County landed back at Meadows Field after taking 20 veterans to Washington, D.C. The trip came just weeks after the first cancellation in the program's history, when issues pushing a plane back from the gate delayed departure and forced the flight to stand down. That flight is rescheduled for spring of next year, but the organization wanted to put together one more trip for 2026, sending almost two dozen veterans and guardians each. It was a family affair for U.S. Army veteran Lowell Tallon, who was slated to be on the cancelled flight — his son and daughter came along this time. "You see it on television, but it's different when you're there," Lowell said. The next Honor Flight is set for spring 2027.

According to 23ABC, two Arvin markets are offering free grocery delivery to residents who are afraid to leave their homes amid immigration enforcement activity in the community. La Plazita Market Carniceria is now delivering at no charge, cashier Belen Rosas said, and the store has seen a grateful response from neighbors who have called to ask about the service. At La Familia Market and Bin Store, business dropped sharply after footage of ICE activity in Arvin spread on social media — Maribel Lopez said one recent day was so slow the staff went hours without a customer. After watching La Plazita step up, La Familia decided to do the same, offering free local delivery on weekends. At least one person was picked up by ICE at the Bear Mountain Car Wash last week.

23ABC reports that East Bakersfield High School is mourning equipment manager Bobby Rocha, who collapsed on the sideline of Friday night's football game against Foothill. He was rushed to the hospital and later died. Those who knew him remembered him as delightful, funny and caring; colleague and family friend Bree Candelaria called him "a breath of fresh air" and said the East High community is in shock. In a statement to 23ABC, the Kern High School District said it was heartbroken over the loss of Rocha, describing him as a beloved football coach and a respected member of the community. The coroner's office has not yet released a cause of death. Play was stopped after he collapsed and the game ended, with Foothill declared the winner.

KGET 17 reports that closing arguments are set in the Demi Dominguez maternal death trial. The case has drawn attention across Kern County for its focus on a death during pregnancy and childbirth, and the arguments mark the final stage before the matter goes to a jury. We'll follow the outcome as it develops.

Bakersfield Now reports that Rosedale teachers say changes to their health benefits are cutting into their paychecks as talks continue. Educators have raised the issue as negotiations move forward, saying the shifts in benefit costs are showing up in take-home pay. The district and its teachers remain in discussions.

KGET 17 reports that California Attorney General Rob Bonta weighed in on the U.S. government's crackdown on voter fraud in the state, calling it a "drop in the bucket." Bonta's remarks push back on the scale of the federal effort as it touches California elections. The comments add the state's voice to a running national dispute over election enforcement.

Bakersfield Now reports that Bakersfield police arrested one person in northeast Bakersfield who was found with a gun. Few details were immediately available, and we'll pass along more as it comes.

Something good

Honor Flight Kern County's return to Meadows Field was the kind of homecoming worth pausing for — veterans stepping off the plane to friends, family and community members who turned out to welcome them back. For Lowell Tallon, the trip doubled as a family reunion in the capital, with both his son and daughter alongside him at the memorials. After a cancellation that stung the whole program, this one landed exactly the way it should.

Coming up this week

It's a busy stretch at City Hall. The Historic Preservation Commission meets today at 10 a.m., followed by the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission and a special Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee, both at 2 p.m. Wednesday brings two City Council sessions — a 3:30 p.m. meeting and a 5:15 p.m. meeting — so check the agendas if you're planning to weigh in on anything.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full week lined up. Switchfoot brings the Forever Now Tour with special guest Anberlin on Wednesday, October 21. Comedian Henry Cho takes the stage Thursday, October 23, for The Empty Nest Tour. Saturday, October 24, brings two shows — Fred Armisen's "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome" and BLADE RAVE. And Sunday, October 25, REZA closes out the weekend with Edge of Illusion. The Fox's Cults & Classics season pass for 2026-2027 is also on sale now.

Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield. We'll be back tomorrow morning.

content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Wednesday, October 21, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a deadly shooting at a Mojave store on Highway 58, where deputies found a man unresponsive and locked the business down while they sorted out what happened. Closer to home, a transit bus went off the road in southeast Bakersfield with six passengers hurt, and an east Bakersfield apartment fire displaced five people. Look for a high near 71 today under a flood watch that runs through Thursday evening, with air quality sitting at a moderate 59.

The Kern Overnight

Gunfire made for the worst of the night. Deputies were called to a store on Highway 58 in Mojave just after 1 a.m. and found a man on the ground who was unresponsive; an ambulance was summoned and the store was locked down while investigators worked. Witnesses described a burgundy car with a disabled plate pulling out of the lot, driven by a light-skinned man with long hair, and callers reported two people running from the store toward the apartments behind it. One person detained at the scene said he saw the car leave.

Elsewhere, a single gunshot brought deputies to 22nd Street in central Bakersfield and turned up nothing behind it. Officers were sent to a bar where a man with a knife in his pocket was threatening a customer, and to an apartment complex where a man who threatened a resident and a roommate left with a handgun in a black backpack. A thief assaulted a worker who confronted him on South Union Avenue, and someone reported three or four people walking around with a shotgun.

Fire filled the rest of the night. A rig burned on the Brundage bridge, and a transit bus went off the road at Belle Terrace and South Washington in southeast Bakersfield just before 8 p.m., with six passengers reporting pain and dispatchers calling a third ambulance. Multiple callers reported fire in an east Bakersfield apartment on Monterey Street a little after 3 a.m., and the Red Cross was brought in for three women and two men who were displaced. A reinforced response went to a house on Angela Way in the Station 8 area before 5 a.m., where crews found the house charged with smoke on the east side and fire showing at a rear corner, knocked down a contents fire in the garage and secured the gas and electric. A grass fire on Elk Hills Road just before midnight drew two dozers, a water tender and several patrols, with crews routed in through oil field gates that the company opened for them.

Today's weather

Expect a high near 71 degrees and a low around 54 tonight. It's currently 59 at Meadows Field. The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a flood watch that took effect at 5:04 this morning and runs until 8 p.m. Thursday, so keep an eye on low-lying roads and crossings if you're out and about. Air quality is 59, which registers as moderate — fine for most of us, but sensitive folks may want to take it easy on extended outdoor exertion. No active fires were reported in the region as of this morning.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that a new poll shows Xavier Becerra with a wide lead over Steve Hilton in the California governor race. The survey puts the Democratic candidate well ahead of his Republican rival as the campaign moves deeper into the fall. For Kern County, the governor's race matters in concrete ways — water policy, oil and agriculture regulation, and the state funding that flows into local schools and roads all get shaped by whoever takes the office. We'll be watching whether the numbers hold as more voters tune in.

According to 23ABC, tens of thousands of California state workers are expected to walk off the job Wednesday in a one-day strike that could affect services at the DMV, unemployment offices and other state agencies. Members of SEIU Local 1000 are protesting what they call bad-faith bargaining by Gov. Gavin Newsom's administration; the union has been negotiating a new labor agreement since its three-year contract expired June 30, and this would be Local 1000's first statewide walkout in its 44-year history. The union represents about 100,000 public workers across dozens of agencies, and roughly 5,000 are legally excluded from participating because their absence would pose an imminent threat to public health or safety. DMV services could be delayed and some offices could close early, with possible effects at EDD, CalFresh and state parks. Union President Anica Walls urged Californians to "give our employees some grace," suggesting anyone who finds limited service at the DMV make an appointment for another day. The Public Employment Relations Board sided with the union last month, concluding that CalHR refused to meet and confer in good faith, while CalHR says departments have contingency plans for potential disruptions. The union could still call the strike off, and both sides are scheduled to keep talking.

Bakersfield Now reports that the Tulare County Sheriff's Office is searching for four men accused of robbing a truck stop in Delano and stealing the register. Deputies are asking for the public's help identifying the group. Truck stops along the 99 corridor are busy, cash-handling operations, and robberies there put late-night workers and travelers at risk — a reminder to keep an eye out and report anything that looks off.

23ABC tells us that newly sworn-in U.S. Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling visited Kern County on Tuesday, touring agricultural and logistics operations and sitting down for a one-on-one interview after a roundtable at Grimmway Farms in Arvin. Sonderling made two stops here — the Wonderful Logistics Center in Shafter in the morning and Grimmway in the afternoon — and said he came to hear employers' workforce challenges and find ways to draw more people into agriculture careers. A key takeaway, he said, is the need for workers who are tech-savvy, whether that means running automation or working alongside it. He talked about partnering with workforce development boards, community colleges and the Pre-K-12 system to get those changing skills into classrooms. Kern's unemployment has historically run above the state average, with agriculture's seasonality pushing joblessness up in winter and down in the growing months — so what happens to training pipelines here is not abstract.

Bakersfield Now also reports that President Trump says the White House is exploring Trump Accounts for adults. The accounts, as described, would be a new savings vehicle, and the administration says it is looking at extending the concept beyond children. Details are still thin, and we'll pass along specifics as they firm up.

KGET 17 reports that power has been restored to homes following a PG&E outage in southwest Bakersfield. Crews got the lights back on for affected customers. Outages are a familiar nuisance in that part of town, and it's worth noting when they're resolved cleanly.

Something good

The Kern County Sheriff's Office is hosting a National Night Out event that includes trick-or-treating, bringing deputies and residents together for an evening of community connection — a good chance for kids to meet the people who patrol their neighborhoods, and for grown-ups to put faces to the badges.

And Honor Flight veterans got a warm welcome back in Bakersfield after a special trip. Whatever else is going on, that's the kind of homecoming this town does well.

Coming up this week

The Bakersfield City Council meets twice today at City Hall — a regular session at 5:15 p.m. and a second meeting at 3:30 p.m. Also today, the Special Prop 47 Local Advisory Committee convenes at 1 p.m. If you've got opinions about how the city spends its dollars or how Proposition 47 funds are directed locally, these are the rooms to be in.

Tonight at 6, Kern County Veteran Service holds a workshop at its office on Golden State Avenue to walk veterans through the VA benefits that make homebuying easier. Realtors and a veteran couple who just bought their first home will lead the session, aimed at cutting through a financing process that can feel convoluted. A note on the flyer: it lists the date as Thursday, October 21, but the 21st falls on a Wednesday, which is when the workshop is actually happening.

The Fox Theater has a full slate this week. Switchfoot brings the Forever Now Tour with special guest Anberlin tonight. Henry Cho's Empty Nest Tour lands Friday, October 23. Saturday, October 24 brings two shows — Fred Armisen's "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome" and BLADE RAVE. And Sunday, October 25, REZA presents Edge of Illusion. If you're planning further out, the Fox has also opened a season pass for its Cults & Classics series running through 2026 and 2027.

Have a good Wednesday, and stay dry out there.

headline: Bakersfield sets aside $4M for jail bed pilot targeting repeat offenders, but calls for further discussion
summary: Gunfire reported in two parts of town and a stabbing near K Street kept officers busy overnight, and rain…
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield Daily Brief: Thursday, October 22, 2026

Good morning, Bakersfield. Gunfire reported in two parts of town and a stabbing near K Street kept officers busy overnight, and rain that moved through before dawn brought part of a roof down over an occupied apartment in the southwest. Today looks cool and damp — a high near 70, a low around 55, and a Flood Watch that runs until 8 p.m. Air quality is good at 33, and no active fires are reported in the area.

The Kern Overnight

Gunfire was reported twice overnight, in two different corners of the city. A little after 12:30 a.m., callers reported four to eight shots in the area of River Boulevard and Panorama Drive in east Bakersfield, and officers were sent to look. At midnight, two callers reported hearing two shots near Ming Avenue and Barrington Street in southwest Bakersfield. Officers were also sent to a stabbing report near K Street at 4:32 a.m.

Deputies responded to Harrington Street in southwest Bakersfield shortly after 1 a.m. on an assault with a deadly weapon report, where a man was reported swinging a metal pole at a woman. Nobody was hurt. A second weapons call drew deputies to the 2nd and 3rd street area.

A traffic stop on Fairfax Road turned into a pursuit that ran south on Madison Street and then through southeast Bakersfield on Watts, Lotus and Cottonwood before the driver pulled over westbound at Shellmacher Avenue before 8 p.m. Three people were in the car, and all were compliant.

Both stolen-vehicle calls came in the small hours — a Tahoe from a convenience store lot on Olive Drive, and a Kia from a delivery driver on Wilson Avenue in north Bakersfield. And the rain did real damage before 6 a.m., when part of a roof came down at an apartment on Actis Street in southwest Bakersfield and water ran inside the unit. Crews told the occupants to get out.

Elsewhere in the log: a caller asked officers to take an assault report on Washington Avenue in north Bakersfield, with the two people involved already gone in a gold sedan; Engine 41 was sent to a damaged power pole on Los Robles Drive; a man was found unconscious behind the wheel of a parked SUV at a gas station on Belvedere Avenue and an ambulance was called; an ambulance was called to Jackson Park for a person with traumatic injuries; crews handled a medical emergency on I Street in Mojave; and Engine 3 put out a trash can fire near the stadium.

Today's weather

It's 55 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, and we're looking at a high near 70 with a low around 55 tonight. The bigger story is the Flood Watch, issued by the National Weather Service office in Hanford at 5:38 a.m. and running until 8 p.m. tonight — so if you're out on the roads, give yourself extra room and watch for standing water in the usual low spots. Air quality is good, at an index of 33, and there are no active fires reported in the region. A cool, wet Thursday, then, with the kind of morning that makes the valley smell like rain.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that the Bakersfield City Council has set aside $4 million for a jail bed pilot aimed at repeat offenders, though the vote came with calls for more discussion before the program moves forward. The money would fund local jail space as part of a broader effort to keep people accused of repeated offenses off the streets while their cases work through the system. Supporters see it as a practical tool for a problem that shows up in police logs night after night; the pushback suggests the council isn't finished debating how the program should work, or how its results will be measured.

According to 23ABC, a 16-year-old has been arrested in connection with the incident that became a deadly police shooting last week in southeast Bakersfield. Police say that around 9:15 p.m. on Wednesday, Oct. 14, officers tried to contact two men near the 1000 block of Pacheco Road; both fled, and shots were fired by Officers Thomas Jannuzi, Dillon Cravens and Rudy Ulloa-Berumen. One of the men, 23-year-old Daniel James Ruiz, was shot and killed near the home. The second person surrendered Tuesday afternoon and was arrested on a warrant for weapons charges, then booked into Kern County Juvenile Hall. Police are asking anyone with information to call the department.

KGET 17 reports that the Hard Rock Casino Tejon has broken ground on its future hotel-resort site, a 400-room expansion expected to add jobs and new amenities to the Tejon area. It's a notable milestone for the project and for the stretch of the county along the Grapevine, where new economic activity has been anticipated since the casino opened. The build-out will take time, but the groundbreaking puts the hotel portion of the resort formally in motion.

23ABC reports that community members in Wasco gathered at Barker Park to protest reported ICE enforcement activity in their community. Residents took to social media Wednesday morning sounding the alarm about reported detentions, and video sent to the station appeared to show officers detaining a man near 16th and Griffith; when 23ABC went to the area, a car was still there with a window smashed. Wasco Police Chief Alecio Mora said his department was aware of enforcement but wasn't told ahead of time, and noted that Senate Bill 54 prohibits local officers from taking part in ICE operations. He encouraged residents to keep calling police to report crimes.

KGET 17 reports that a verdict has awarded Demi Dominguez's family millions of dollars, though the family will not receive the full award. The outcome closes a chapter in a case that has been followed closely in Bakersfield, and the gap between the verdict figure and what the family ultimately collects is the part likely to draw attention in the days ahead.

Bakersfield Now reports that an Eyewitness News morning anchor has obtained a restraining order against a man alleged to be the news station shooter. The order is a legal step meant to keep distance between the two while the broader case proceeds — a reminder that the fallout from that episode at the station is still working its way through the courts.

Something good

The Hard Rock Casino Tejon's groundbreaking isn't just about a building — a 400-room hotel means housekeeping, food service, maintenance and front-desk jobs for people who live around Tejon and the Grapevine, plus new amenities for visitors passing through on I-5. It's the kind of project that ripples outward into the local economy for years. Worth a nod this morning.

And Friday brings the Hot Pink Celebration, hosted by the local nonprofit Links for Life at Luigi's, with doors opening at 6 p.m. The evening brings together patients, survivors, families and healthcare professionals for Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Links for Life provides wigs, grocery assistance and support groups to patients and survivors here in Kern County. As executive director Jennifer Henry told 23ABC, roughly one in eight women will be diagnosed with breast cancer, and about 450 women in Kern County will hear that news this year. Adventist Health nurse supervisor Jacqui Engstrom noted that only about 65 percent of local women are getting their screenings — a reminder that a monthly self-exam and, for women over 40, a yearly mammogram, are the simplest tools we have.

Coming up this week

The Fox Theater has a full slate over the next several days. Henry Cho brings The Empty Nest Tour to the Fox on Friday, Oct. 23. Saturday, Oct. 24 offers two very different nights under the same roof: Fred Armisen's Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome, and BLADE RAVE. Sunday, Oct. 25 brings REZA | Edge of Illusion, and Monday, Oct. 26, J & J Investigations leads Ghost Tours at the theater — fitting for the last week of October. Looking further out, the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026-2027 is on sale now for the coming season.

No public meetings are on the calendar we're tracking for this week, but keep an eye on the city and county agendas as the jail bed pilot discussion continues — that conversation is likely to resurface at a future council session.

If you're heading out this morning, take the rain seriously and leave a little early. We'll be back tomorrow with whatever the night brings.
